## Audio route, Speaker and mute

Where the voice comes out, who owns the audio session, and what mutes what.

**Siblings:** Classic · Gemini, Qwen, Grok and Local Live (default and
echo-cancelling audio) · GPT-Live (WebRTC) · calls from Hermes (CallKit's
Speaker button, and the call screen's own Speaker) · CarPlay · AirPods and Bluetooth · Read Aloud · the Voice
settings speech test · the call
screen's Mute and Silence · the minimised call bar · a Watch-answered call
kept on the iPhone's headset (the Watch's Mute and End) · composer
dictation and voice messages (chats and group rooms), which take the
microphone · voice clips in the chat · the Read Aloud buttons in chats and group rooms

**Code**
- Session owner: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceAudioSessionCoordinator.swift` (ensureConversationSpeaker, isNativeCallAudioActive), `Conduit/Voice/VoiceAudioSessionConfiguration.swift`
- Playback: `Conduit/Voice/AVSpeechPlaybackService.swift` (resumeOnFreshEngine), `Conduit/Voice/VoiceAudioEngineRecovery.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/AVAudioCaptureService.swift` (VoicePCMEncoding.splitPCM16: a stream's odd byte, for both playbacks)
- Live audio: `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveAudioLink.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/LiveVoiceEchoCancellingAudio.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/EchoCancellingVoiceConversationAudio.swift`, a reply's end in `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveConversationController.swift` (turnComplete, endReply)
- Mute and Silence: `Conduit/Views/LiveVoiceCallSheet.swift`, `Conduit/Views/MinimisedLiveVoiceBar.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/HeadsetMicrophoneMute.swift`
- The call screen's Speaker in a call from Hermes: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceAudioSessionCoordinator.swift` (NativeCallSpeakerState, setNativeCallSpeaker, nativeCallRouteChanged, called from HermesNativeCalls' route observer), `Conduit/Views/LiveVoiceCallSheet.swift` (NativeCallSpeakerButton, LiveVoiceCallButtonRowFit), `Conduit/Views/VoiceConversationSheet.swift` (Classic's V1 card and V2 row)
- A Watch answer kept on the iPhone's headset: `Conduit/Voice/HermesNativeCalls.swift` (keepsWatchAnswer, muteOnWatch, inAppMuteChanged), `Conduit/Services/AppState+HermesCalls.swift` (nativeCallVoiceMuted), `ConduitWatch/HermesWatchCalls.swift` (phoneCallMuted)
- Read Aloud: `Conduit/Voice/MessageReadAloudController.swift` (routeChanged, onTakenOverByCapture), `Conduit/Views/ReadAloudPlayerBar.swift`
- Read Aloud kept off calls and the microphone: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (readAloudAudioBusyReason, under readAloudUnavailableReason, which the buttons in `Conduit/Views/ChatRowState.swift` and `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` read), `Conduit/Voice/VoiceAudioSessionCoordinator.swift` (acquire's onTakenOver), `Conduit/Voice/AVSpeechPlaybackService.swift` (onTakenOverByCapture), `Conduit/Voice/MessageReadAloudController.swift` (yieldToHeldMicrophone), `Conduit/Views/Components/InlineAudioClip.swift` (a clip's lease), `Conduit/Services/AppState+HermesCalls.swift` (setNativeHermesCallActive), the speech tests' gate in `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (isCallHoldingAudio, runVoiceTTSTest, runVoiceASRTest)
- Speech test: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceConversationController.swift` (runSpeechTest)
- Background time: `Conduit/Services/BackgroundTaskHold.swift` (HermesNativeCalls' muteOnWatch)

**Rulings**
- During a call from Hermes, CallKit owns the audio session: Conduit never deactivates or re-activates it, so the Speaker button stays true (2026-10-21, #1093; 2026-10-23, #1148).
- A call from Hermes starts on the earpiece (or the headset, the car), like a phone call (#1171). Conduit's call screen covers CallKit's, whose Speaker button iOS shows only on the lock screen or away from the app, so every mode's call screen (Classic, Gemini, Qwen, Grok, GPT-Live, Local Live) has Speaker of its own during a call from Hermes on an iPhone (not iPad or Mac, which have no earpiece). It makes the same override CallKit's button does, never re-activating or reconfiguring the session; off clears it, back to the earpiece or the headset that is on. It is lit whenever the call plays from the loudspeaker, whichever control put it there. A row of six sizes its buttons to fit; Silence's glyph is a waveform so it isn't taken for Speaker (2026-11-06, #1847).
- A conversation's replies move from the earpiece to the speaker, never during a CallKit call (2026-10-19, #943).
- Silence mutes the assistant's voice apart from the microphone; its speech is dropped, not held, and job news waits for unmute (2026-10-09, #488).
- An alarm or phone call pauses a live call, which comes back when the audio does (2026-10-04, #380).
- A call from Hermes answered on the Watch plays on the iPhone's headset when one is on there (AirPods, wired, never the car's); the Watch's Mute and End control it like a phone call's, and a mute from any of Conduit's own controls reaches the Watch (Eric 2026-10-24, #1225).
- A route change mid-reply (AirPods, Speaker, a dock) never drops speech: a conversation's reply, Read Aloud and the speech test play on from where they were on a fresh engine; an encoded clip follows the route itself, and a fresh engine that won't start ends Read Aloud rather than restarting past the dropped audio (Eric 2026-11-02, from issue 1641, #1650).
- A streamed reply's odd trailing byte waits for the next chunk on storage of its own (VoicePCMEncoding.splitPCM16), in the live modes' echo-cancelling audio and the default playback alike. A route change's restart copies it and tears down: left as an emptied slice of the stream, clearing it made Foundation trap (29 crash reports from build 244, 2026-11-04, #1733). A reply's end drops it, so it never shifts the next reply: Classic and Read Aloud at `finish()`, the live modes at turnComplete on either audio (`GeminiLiveAudioOutput.endReply`), where the stream stays open across replies. An interruption, a rate change and a call's end drop it too. The Watch's direct calls cut each chunk on its own and carry nothing between them (2026-11-05, issue 1791, #1794).
- Headphones taken out (AirPods back in the case, a cable pulled) pause Read Aloud, as iOS media does, instead of reading on from the speaker; Resume carries on. Live calls and Classic keep talking, like a phone call (Eric 2026-11-02, #1650).
- Read Aloud never plays over a call or the microphone: the call's microphone would hear it as the user (each engine's echo cancelling knows only its own voice) and two voices would talk at once. During any call (Classic, the live modes, minimised or not, a call from Hermes) its buttons in chats and group rooms are off, and a tap that still reaches it is refused with "Read aloud can't play during a call."; it never ends the call. A tap while dictation or a voice message holds the microphone says "Read aloud can't play while the microphone is in use." Opening a call stops Read Aloud, and so does dictation or a voice message taking the microphone; a reading whose stream opens under a held microphone ends before it plays, as a cancellation, so Hermes speech isn't marked failed and swapped for the iPhone's voice. A reading still opening when a call from Hermes starts ends then, or when its audio arrives. A voice clip playing in the chat pauses when dictation or a voice message takes the microphone too; one the user plays during a call still plays, by their choice. The Voice settings speech and transcription tests refuse to run during a call ("End the call to run this test."). The speech test is no call: Read Aloud takes over from it (2026-11-05, issue 1770, #1772).
- In a call from Hermes, standalone playback (a clip in the chat) plays within CallKit's session and never reconfigures or re-activates it; the call's end applies its own policy (2026-11-05, issue 1770, #1772).

**Open gaps**
- Silence isn't on CarPlay or the minimised bar (#488).
- Classic still ends with "Audio was interrupted." when an alarm or phone call takes the audio, where live calls pause; only CarPlay and calls from Hermes restart it (#380, #1155).

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1847 (an answered call from Hermes has Speaker on the call screen in every mode, for a tester who couldn't leave the earpiece; CarPlay and the Watch play on their own routes, the minimised bar opens the screen); 2026-11-05, #1794 (a live reply's odd trailing byte is dropped at turnComplete instead of shifting the next reply, Gemini, Qwen, Grok and Local Live on both audios, issue 1791; Classic and Read Aloud already did, the Watch carries none, GPT-Live is WebRTC); 2026-11-05, #1772 (Read Aloud kept off calls and the microphone, standalone playback leaves a call from Hermes' session alone, issue 1770); 2026-11-04, #1733 (a stream's odd byte kept on its own storage, so a route change's restart no longer traps); 2026-11-02, #1650 (Read Aloud and the speech test play on after a route change instead of restarting with the queued middle dropped, issue 1641; headphones taken out pause Read Aloud); 2026-10-30, #1524 (Read Aloud reads a Desktop card as a short note; route, Speaker and mute unchanged); 2026-10-26, #1247 (a mute reaching the Watch keeps Conduit running through BackgroundTaskHold); 2026-10-25, Qwen in the siblings, and its mute reaching the Watch, at #1182, carried in #1235; 2026-10-24, #1225: the Watch's Mute and End for a call kept on the iPhone's headset; seeded from main at 64d53c3.

## Talking over Hermes

Speaking while Hermes talks or thinks: barge-in, talk-over, steering, push to
talk, and how long the microphone waits.

**Siblings:** Classic (phone, CarPlay, locked phone) · Gemini Live · Qwen
Live · Grok Live · GPT-Live · Local Live · Watch calls · headset, speaker and car routes ·
push to talk · Continuous Conversation · the Action, headset and CarPlay
buttons · the Interrupt button, CarPlay's Stop, the Watch orb and Classic's spoken Stop phrases · End Conversation, the orphan retry after a suspension, a fresh voice conversation over a running turn, the
chat's own Stop, /stop, a send that replaces the turn and cancelling a voice job in the open chat (a
cancelled turn's late words) · the
notifier's Local Live read-back relay (phone socket and Watch bridge) · docs/VOICE_SETTINGS.md and
docs/OWN_VOICE_SERVER.md · the notifier's README (read-back)

| Mode | On a headset | On the speaker or in the car |
|---|---|---|
| Classic | talk-over starts a new turn; speech while Hermes thinks, or over its acknowledgement, steers | the same, with "Talk over it on the speaker" on |
| Gemini, Qwen, Grok, Local Live | barge-in | barge-in with "Talk over it on the speaker" on |
| GPT-Live | barge-in (WebRTC cancels the echo) | barge-in |

Calls from Hermes use the default audio in every mode, so the speaker and car column's talk-over does not apply to them (see the rulings below).

**Code**
- Routes: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceBargeInRoutePolicy.swift`
- Classic: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceConversationController.swift` (isTalkOverAvailable, isSteerAvailable, isAcknowledgementSteerable, beginPushToTalk, isWholeUtteranceStopCommand, cancelRetiredTurn), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (voiceCancelledTurns, runningTurnGenerationLookup, voiceBackgroundJobSupervisor (its cancel notes the open chat's turn), interruptForVoice, cancelCurrent, interruptForReplacement, noteRunningTurnBeforeCancel, Reconciliation.bufferedGenerations, Reconciliation.bufferedEntries, bufferIfReconciling, applyNumberedStreamEvent, generations(_:of:keptIn:), noteVoiceCancelledTurn, voiceCancelNoteWrites, voiceCancelNote, restoreVoiceCancelNote, noteVoiceStoppedTurn, takeVoiceEventAfterCancel, handleStreamEvent, handledStreamEventGeneration), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (runningTurnGeneration, deliveringEventGeneration, cancel), `Conduit/Voice/VoiceSpeechDetector.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/EchoCancellingVoiceConversationAudio.swift`
- Live modes: `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveConversationController.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/LiveVoiceEchoCancellingAudio.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveConversationController.swift`
- Interrupt: `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveConversationController.swift` (interruptSpeaking), `Shared/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveSessionControlling.swift` (cancelResponse), `Shared/LocalLive/LocalLiveSession.swift` (cancelResponse), `Shared/LocalLive/LocalLiveProtocol.swift` (responseCancel), `ConduitWatch/WatchDirectCallModel.swift` (tapOrb), `ConduitWatch/WatchBridgeCallModel.swift` (tapOrb), `notifier/dashboard/api/local_live_read_back.py` (_LocalLiveReadBack.from_client, _stop; the phone's socket and the Watch's bridge both run it)
- Push to talk surfaces: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (pushToTalkSurfaceAvailable)
- Which audio a conversation runs on: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (usesEchoCancellingVoiceAudio: never in a call from Hermes), `Conduit/Voice/VoiceAudioSessionCoordinator.swift` (isInNativeCall)
- Settings: `Conduit/Views/VoiceSettingsView.swift`, `Conduit/Views/GeminiLiveViews.swift`, `Conduit/Views/GrokLiveViews.swift`

**Rulings**
- In Classic, talking over a spoken reply stops it and starts a new turn; speech while Hermes thinks steers it (2026-10-04, #391). Hermes' acknowledgement while it works isn't the reply: talking over it, Interrupt, CarPlay's Stop or a push to talk press stops it and steers the running turn (2026-10-27, #1390).
- Talking over on the speaker is opt-in, "Talk over it on the speaker", off by default, one setting shared by Qwen, Gemini, Grok and Classic, which each mode's caption says (2026-10-03, #351; Classic 2026-10-04, #393; Qwen 2026-10-25, #1182).
- A call from Hermes never uses talk-over's echo-cancelling engine, in any mode that has it (Classic, Gemini, Qwen, Grok, Local Live; GPT-Live's WebRTC audio never did), on the phone or in the car: it takes the default audio, and each mode's talk-over caption says so. Under CallKit's session every voice-processing engine that starts sets a session property whose route change stops it a moment later, so the call looped through engine rebuilds for 20 seconds before it spoke, or kept a last engine with no speaker side and stayed silent (Ul'dah's logs, 2026-11-01/02). The call starts on the earpiece, where talk-over adds nothing; on the speaker or in the car the microphone closes while Hermes talks, as with the setting off. The user's own calls keep the setting (Eric 2026-11-02, #1659).
- Push to talk is per profile and off by default. While held no silence timer runs; a press while Hermes speaks interrupts, while it thinks steers. CarPlay and calls from Hermes stay hands-free (2026-10-22, #1106).
- Interrupt (CarPlay's Stop and the Watch orb too) stops what plays on the device. In Local Live (the phone's Interrupt, CarPlay's Stop and the Watch orb) it also sends the speech server `response.cancel`, which the read-back relay passes on even when no sentence is in progress, so a server that shuts its own microphone while its reply plays listens again; nothing is guessed from the audio, and background jobs go on. Gemini, Grok and Qwen stop only what plays here: their servers hear the user over the reply and keep no gate (2026-10-27, #1331, notifier #404, from #1325).
- A filler a read-back speech server says on its own while Hermes works (ConvFill's "let me look that up") plays on the call as the reply's start: Hermes' sentences wait for it to end, and talking over it, Interrupt, CarPlay's Stop and the Watch orb stop it like the reply, on the phone's socket and the Watch's bridge alike (2026-11-06, notifier #588, carrying ds-002's #582).
- Interrupt drops the rest of a model turn only while that turn is still arriving. Pressed after it ended, while its last audio still plays, it silences that tail and nothing more: the model's next reply (a job update, a text Send to Hermes answer, a turn of its own) is heard and captioned. The same holds for the Watch orb, in direct calls and over the bridge, and for CarPlay's Stop, which runs the phone's Interrupt (2026-11-05, #1795, issue 1790).
- With Continuous Conversation on, the default, Classic keeps listening through silence instead of pausing the microphone (2026-10-10, #520).
- Every intentional stop of a running turn in Classic (talking over it, Interrupt, CarPlay's Stop, a push to talk press, and a spoken Stop phrase in a steer or approval answer window) retires the turn before it cancels it and listens again: the cancelled turn's late interrupted or cancellation event belongs to it and never ends the window that opened, nor shows a failure for a stop the user asked for. When the cancel fails, the next submission cancels that turn again first, as after a suspension, so its reply is never taken as the new turn's (2026-11-03, #1694, issue 1691).
- A cancelled turn's late words are never spoken as the next question's reply (Eric, 2026-11-03, issue 1691).
- How that is done is #1696's design, not yet confirmed by Eric (2026-11-03, #1696): every cancel of the open chat's turn (these stops, an orphan's cancel after a suspension, End Conversation, starting a fresh voice conversation over a running turn, and the chat's own Stop, /stop, a send that replaces the turn, or cancelling a voice job in the open chat) notes the turn the chat was running by its execution generation, and that turn's later words (start, deltas, commentary) never reach Voice while that chat stays open (under any id it goes by) and until the next turn's first event, even once the next question was sent, so words it still streams are never spoken as that question's reply. The next turn's first event ends the watch. Each chat keeps its own note, and a cancel that fails takes back the note it made, since that turn still runs, but leaves one another cancel of that chat made meanwhile. A cancel that reads the chat again after a stale generation stops the turn Hermes names there, and the note becomes that turn (newer, lower when this socket's number was too high, or one this socket never saw start), as long as the chat showed a turn running and no other cancel of it noted meanwhile. Where the open chat holds notes under more than one of its ids, the newest counts and the next turn ends them all. Events a resume holds keep the turn they named for their replay, so they are told apart the same way. The turn's end (its completion, failure or interruption) reaches Voice as an end with no words: a conversation still waiting on that turn (stopped from the chat) finishes what it already said and listens again, without speaking or writing the rest of the reply the user stopped, and one waiting on the next question ignores it until that reply starts, so the stopped turn never fails or ends the next question's wait. Only the session authority numbers its turns: on `hermes dashboard` nothing is noted or held back.

**Open gaps**
- A cancelled turn whose start Voice never saw: held in a resume's buffer and replayed after the cancel, or still in the hop to the main actor when the chat's Stop noted it. The start is held from Voice, so a Classic conversation still waiting on that very turn (stopped from the chat, not by Voice) ignores its end and stays thinking until the next turn's first event or the user speaks. Telling that wait from one on the next question needs the controller to know which turn it awaits; both windows are narrow (a resume, or a few milliseconds, racing a chat Stop), so this is left for now (2026-11-03, #1696).
- Push to talk is Classic only: not the live modes, the Watch, or the Action, headset and CarPlay buttons (#1106).

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1902 (a read-back server's own filler plays and opens the reply, and stops like it, notifier #588); 2026-11-05, #1795 (Interrupt after a turn ended only silences its tail, on the phone, CarPlay and the Watch); 2026-11-03, #1696 (a cancelled turn's words stay away from Voice, by its execution generation, until the next turn's first event, even after the next question was sent; its end reaches Voice as an interruption); 2026-11-03, #1694 (a spoken Stop retires the turn it cancels, as talking over and Interrupt do; a failed cancel is retried before the next turn); 2026-11-02, #1659 (a call from Hermes takes the default audio with talk-over on); 2026-10-28, #1462 (the notifier code it lists moved from dashboard/plugin_api.py to dashboard/api/, one module per feature, notifier #449); 2026-10-27, #1390 (Classic: cutting Hermes' acknowledgement short steers); 2026-10-27, #1378 (CarPlay's Stop on Local Live tells the server too); 2026-10-27, #1331 (Interrupt tells a Local Live server, #1325); 2026-10-25, Qwen in the siblings, the table and the shared caption, at #1182, carried in #1235; 2026-10-23, seeded from main at 64d53c3.

## Files Hermes attaches, in what voices say

A reply can attach a file with Hermes' `MEDIA:<path>` tag (text_to_speech
answers with one) or carry a delivery directive (`[[audio_as_voice]]`). The
chat shows the file; nothing that speaks the reply reads the tag out, and
no live model is handed the path to read out either.

**Siblings:** Read Aloud · Classic voice's spoken reply (phone, CarPlay) ·
Local Live's spoken and shown split (the call's screen shows the file) ·
live read-back of a reply asked for again, and the result a Hermes call
reads out · job results, chat replies (a job's thread reply, and the open
chat's latest reply in a chat call's instructions) and read_chat as Gemini, Qwen, Grok,
GPT-Live and Local Live get them, on the phone and the Watch, and a
Hermes call's reply in its instructions · the
notifier's line for a spoken turn, which tells the model its answer is
heard · chat bubbles (the file card; a Markdown file opens in the
Markdown reader, see Artifacts) · a bot's message in a group room (the same
cards, read from the bot's profile, see Pictures in messages)

**Code**
- The file card: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (GatewayMediaFileCard; a Markdown file opens `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownDocumentSheet.swift`)
- The tag grammar: `Conduit/Views/Components/GatewayMediaTags.swift` (removingTags, namingFiles; also built into the Watch app, `project.yml`)
- Streaming speech: `Conduit/Voice/SpokenMediaTagFilter.swift`, used by `Conduit/Voice/SpokenTextFilter.swift` (Classic, Read Aloud's Now Playing) and `Conduit/Voice/LocalLive/SpokenVisualSplitter.swift` (Local Live, which puts the files on the call's screen)
- Read Aloud: `Conduit/Voice/MessageReadAloudController.swift` (toggle)
- Live read-back: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceReadBack.swift` (plainSpeech)
- What live models are handed: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceBackgroundJobs.swift` (completionPrompt, threadReplyPrompt, replyBlock), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (liveVoiceThreadInstructions: the open chat's latest reply), `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveToolBridge.swift` (a job's tool response, read_chat), `Shared/WatchVoice/WatchJobRelay.swift` (WatchJobAnswer.completionPrompt), `Shared/WatchVoice/VoiceChatToolText.swift` (readResult, and delegatedRead for GPT-Live's "Read chat:" in `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveDelegationBridge.swift` and the Watch's `Shared/WatchVoice/WatchToolRelay.swift`)
- A Hermes call's result: `Conduit/Voice/HermesCalls.swift` (instructionBlock names files; spokenBrief uses plainSpeech)
- Local Live's screen: `Conduit/Voice/LocalLive/LocalLiveTurnRunner.swift` (finish)
- What the model reads: `notifier/turn_surface.py` (SPOKEN_HINT)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/HermesVoiceGatewayTimeoutTests+LocalLive.swift` (testSpokenVisualSplitterLeavesFileTagsUnsaid), `ConduitTests/GeminiLiveVoiceTests.swift` (testSpokenMediaTagFilter…, testSpokenTextFilterLeavesFileTagsUnsaid), `ConduitTests/VoiceBackgroundJobTests.swift` (testLiveModelsAreToldOfAFileNotItsPath, plainSpeech), `notifier/tests/test_turn_surface.py`

**Rulings**
- A tag is never said, and a line that was only a tag says nothing; the words around it, and a link's label or an image's alt text, are said as written. A tag in a `>` quote is text, as Hermes doesn't deliver it, and is said like the rest of the quote. A quoted tag needs a path: one starting at a root, a home folder or a drive, or ending in a known extension, so "social media: \"we're live!\"" is words in speech, for live models and in the chat bubble alike (#1449). A quoted line's path is text too, so it is said and handed to live models as written; Hermes sends no file for it (2026-10-28, #1434, after a Local voice call on the farm read "MEDIA:/opt/data/cache/audio/tts_….mp3" out and its microphone heard "media." back).
- Streaming voices hold from where a tag may begin (with its emphasis or `[label](`) to the end of its line, and only while it can still be one: `MEDIA:` with a path after it, or a directive. Prose such as "social media: we shipped" is said as it comes; a `[` with no `]` waits up to 80 characters, then is said as it comes (Local Live's splitter, older than this, holds a `[` until its `)` or the line's end, for links). Once a tag may have begun, the rest of its line waits for the line's end, the price of a reply being said the same however it is split (#1449). Text that can't start a tag goes out as it came, its chunks unchanged ("One " then "turn."), so a space said before a tag that arrives later stays, and "Hello!" is said while a "!" after a space or mark waits for a possible image.
- Local Live puts a tagged file on the call's screen, as the chat shows it (a tag written as a link included), even when the model showed its own card or the call cut the reply off for its own line (#1449).
- A live model is told of a file by name ("(a file in the chat: report.pdf)"), never its path: a job's result, a chat reply, a chat read into the call and the reply a Hermes call is about alike (#1449).
- A file card opens its file in the chat's viewers; a Markdown file opens in the Markdown reader Artifacts uses, formatted, falling back to Quick Look when it isn't UTF-8 or is over 16 MB (2026-11-06, #1884, carrying #1879).
- A spoken message's line tells the model its answer is heard: say it in words, not with text_to_speech or a sound file of its own; a file the user asks for is still fine. Hermes' own spoken-reply note isn't on every Hermes (2026-10-28, #1434, notifier #444, 0.115.1).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-07, #1914 (a group room's bot messages draw their tags as files too, read from the bot's profile; voices unchanged, rooms have none); 2026-11-06, #1884 (a Markdown file card opens the Markdown reader, as Artifacts does since #1879); 2026-11-01, #1631 (an answer to a question this socket never saw passes the call's chat and profile, for the gateway's own listener; see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-30, #1524 (Hermes Desktop's directives are read alongside, with their own entry, Cards made for Hermes Desktop); 2026-10-28, #1434, carried in #1449.

## Qwen direct voice

A live call on Alibaba Cloud's Qwen realtime model, from the phone or the
Watch, with temporary credentials the notifier mints.

**Siblings:** phone direct voice · Watch direct voice · CarPlay · incoming
Hermes calls · tools and jobs · consent · saved transcripts · notifier tokens

**Code**
- Adapter: `Shared/GeminiLive/QwenLiveSocket.swift`, `Shared/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveSession.swift`
- Credentials: `Shared/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveToken.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveTokenClient.swift`
- Watch wire: `Shared/WatchVoice/WatchDirectWire.swift`, `Shared/WatchVoice/WatchVoiceWire.swift`
- Provider setup: `docs/QWEN_LIVE.md`; notifier: `notifier/dashboard/api/gemini_qwen_live.py`
- Plugin capability inventory: `Conduit/Views/ConduitPluginViews.swift` (separate Gemini/Qwen feature entries)
- Lifecycle/recovery: `Conduit/Watch/WatchDirectBroker.swift` (directToken, tokenRefusalAfterMint), `ConduitWatch/WatchDirectCallModel.swift`, `Conduit/CarPlay/CarPlayVoiceCoordinator.swift`
- Watch relay token: `Shared/WatchVoice/WatchToolRelayClient.swift` (keeps `qwen_live_token` beside `live_token`), tests in `ConduitTests/WatchVoiceWireTests.swift`
- Which provider runs: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (configuredLiveVoiceEngine, isQwenLiveEnabled, resumeVoiceCall, adoptSyncedVoicePreferences); what models read: `Conduit/Services/AppState+AgentSettings.swift` (voice.mode, voice.qwen.*, voice.live.save_calls)
- Phone entry, shared settings and captions: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift`, `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift`, `Conduit/Views/GeminiLiveViews.swift`, `Conduit/Views/VoiceChatCallTranscriptSheet.swift`
- Picker/setup identity: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceModeChoice.swift`, `Conduit/Views/VoiceSettingsView.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/VoiceSetupIssue.swift`
- Saved-call preferences/identity: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceTypes.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/VoiceHistory.swift`
- Watch transport and diagnostics: `ConduitWatch/WatchGeminiSocket.swift`
- Watch capability compatibility tests: `ConduitTests/HermesCallsTests.swift` (legacy plugins, Qwen-only and concurrent providers)
- Background time: `Conduit/Services/BackgroundTaskHold.swift` (the Watch broker's directToken)

**Rulings**
- Gemini and Qwen are independent picker entries, concurrently configurable on
  the host, with separate preferences, consent, data permissions and saved
  call identity. Shared controllers/adapters must not combine their product
  identities (2026-10-24, maintainer request on #1182).
- Both providers connect directly from the device. Watch starts explicitly
  name the provider; reconnect grants authorize the selected token tool only,
  and a token minted after the call ended or its provider's consent was
  withdrawn never reaches the Watch (Gemini too).
- With both providers' flags on (a synced blob merged across devices), Gemini
  wins everywhere: normal routing, a resumed call, CarPlay and voice.mode.
- Qwen voice can be selected on the phone independently of Gemini, with the
  host's configured voice as fallback. Qwen uses Hermes search functions.
- Hermes reads and changes Qwen's lookups, memory and personality
  (voice.qwen.*) as it does the other providers'. The Qwen voice is a typed
  name, and the settings Hermes sees have no free-text kind, so it stays
  phone-only (#1235 review).
- Qwen inherits job approvals/questions, follow-up steering, quiet job-result
  delivery, barge-in, the audio routes, bounded socket sends and calls from
  Hermes through the shared direct-call controller/tool bridge, and is named
  in those entries ("Hermes is waiting on you", "Voice follow-ups", "Job
  results during calls", "Tools and consent in calls", "Calls from Hermes",
  "Audio route, Speaker and mute", "Talking over Hermes", "Live-call sends on
  a slow connection"), which apply to Qwen as to Gemini. Provider consent and
  history stay separate.

**Open gaps**
- Real credentials, entitlement, voice availability and Watch background
  behavior need device testing; mocked tests cannot establish them.
- A screen question on a Qwen profile falls back to Classic voice:
  `Conduit/Services/AppState+ScreenQuestion.swift` (ScreenQuestionVoiceRouting.liveEngines)
  lists GPT-Live, Gemini and Grok only, until Qwen is device-tested there.

**Checked:** 2026-10-28, #1462 (the notifier code it lists moved from dashboard/plugin_api.py to dashboard/api/, one module per feature, notifier #449); 2026-10-28, #1424 (QwenLiveSocket traces turn detection and speech start and end); 2026-10-26, #1247 (the Watch broker's token answers keep Conduit running through BackgroundTaskHold); 2026-10-25, voice.qwen.* and save_calls naming Qwen, the Watch's qwen_live_token, a token minted after consent was withdrawn, provider precedence and the screen-question gap, at #1182, carried in #1235; 2026-10-24, #1182: independent provider routes and regression tests.

## Texting someone for the user

Hermes writes a text for someone ("text my wife her flight landed") and
puts it on a contact card; Send text opens Messages with the number and
the text filled in, and the user taps Send there.

**Siblings:** typed chats (conduit_show) · the call screen (Gemini, Grok and
Local Live show_on_screen, and Classic through Hermes) · GPT-Live · the saved
call transcript · group rooms · the Watch · CarPlay · an iPad without
Messages · what conduit_show, conduit_contacts and the voice contacts tool
tell models · Settings > Contacts' caption

**Code**
- Card and Send text: `Conduit/Cards/RichMediaCard.swift` (RichPerson.message), `Conduit/Cards/RichMediaCardViews.swift` (RichPersonRow, RichTextComposeSheet)
- Schema: `Conduit/Cards/card-schema.json`, `Conduit/Cards/RichCardSchema.swift`; feature "text-drafts" in `Conduit/Services/PresentedScreens.swift`
- Live models' show_on_screen text: `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveToolBridge.swift`
- Notifier: `notifier/cards/card-schema.json` (people[].message), `notifier/card_schema.py`, `notifier/show_tool.py` (TEXT_DRAFTS_FEATURE), `notifier/phone_tool.py` (CONTACTS_SCHEMA, VOICE_CONTACTS_DESCRIPTION)

**Rulings**
- Nothing is sent for the user: Messages opens filled in and only their tap sends it, so models say it's ready, never that it was sent (2026-10-23, #1159).
- A text needs the person's phone; one without is dropped (2026-10-23, #1159).
- A Conduit that doesn't say "text-drafts" gets the card without the text, and Hermes hears to put the text in its reply (2026-10-23, #1159).

**Open gaps**
- No queued send for when the user isn't looking: CarPlay and the Watch show no card, and a locked phone waits for the user to open the chat (#1159).
- GPT-Live can't put the card on the call screen itself; it asks Hermes (#366).
- A room's boards leave contact cards out, so no Send text in group rooms.
- Line breaks in the text become spaces, as in every card's text.
- Hermes doesn't hear whether the user sent or cancelled it.

**Checked:** 2026-11-04, #1739 (room boards leave contact cards out); 2026-10-23, at #1174.

## Message row actions

The controls on a message: the row under a reply, the row under your own
message, their long-press and selection menus, and the same actions in the
other chat surfaces.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats and Bot Chat (one row view) · group rooms ·
the selection menu · the long-press menu · VoiceOver labels · pinned replies
(the bar, and the sheet from the chat and from the Chats list) · your own
message's row · the "Replying to" card on a sent message, on a steered
one and in group rooms · /undo and /retry, which Edit and resend and Retry run · the composer's
restore of words put back (failed sends, the waiting message's Edit) · the
chat's saved copy, whose rows stand in while it opens or offline

**Code**
- Reply row: `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (AssistantMessageActions, ReadAloudButton, AssistantMessageMoreMenu), `Conduit/Views/Components/MessageReactionViews.swift` (MessageReactButton)
- Your own message's row: `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (UserMessageCopyButton, UserMessageMoreMenu)
- Edit and resend, Retry: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (editAndResend, rewindTurn, rewindLastTurns, latestTurnRanTools); tests in `ConduitTests/AppStateSessionCompressTests.swift` and `ConduitTests/ChatQuoteTests.swift`
- "Replying to" card and its jump: `Conduit/Views/Components/ChatQuote.swift` (ReplyReferenceQuoteCard, QuotedReplyJump), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (showQuotedReply, quotedReplyMessageID, showQuotedRoomMessage, quotedRoomMessageID), `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (GroupUserBubble, the room's pendingQuotedReplyJump), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (UserMessageContent, SteerMessageContent, pendingQuotedReplyJump), `Conduit/Services/TranscriptScroller.swift` (explicitMessageRequested, a room's jump too)
- Edit and resend's words in the composer: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (applyComposerRestoreRequests), `Conduit/Models/PendingComposerSend.swift` (ComposerDraft.restoring)
- Which reply offers Retry: `Conduit/Views/ChatRowState.swift` (ChatRowFacts.retryableReplyID, from the rows drawn, worked out by `Conduit/Views/TranscriptModel.swift`)
- The saved copy's rows: the chat's own rows while they stand in, their cards' jump turned off in `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (quotedReplyJump); Edit and resend, Branch, Retry and Read aloud off through `Conduit/Views/ChatRowState.swift` (isOffline)
- Selection and long-press menus: `Conduit/Views/Components/SelectableTextView.swift` (MarkdownSelectionObserverGestureRecognizer, which fails once the last finger lifts through UIGestureRecognizer.fingerStillDown in `Conduit/Services/InteractionIdleState.swift`; test `ConduitTests/ChatTextSelectionTests.swift` testPassiveRecognizersSeeTheirLastFingerLift)
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (GroupMessageCopyButton, GroupMessageQuoteButton, GroupReadAloudButton)
- Pins: `Conduit/Views/PinnedReplyViews.swift`, `Conduit/Models/PinnedReplies.swift` (overview), `Conduit/Services/AppState+PinnedReplies.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (deleteBot, forgetBotChatPinnedReplies), the sheet's Chats-list entry points in `Conduit/Views/SidebarView.swift` and `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ChatsView.swift` (showPinnedReplies)
- Read Aloud: `Conduit/Voice/MessageReadAloudController.swift`, `Conduit/Views/ReadAloudPlayerBar.swift`
- Branch (the ⋯ menu, /branch and /fork): `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (branchFromAssistantMessage), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (branchSession); tests in `ConduitTests/AppStateChatResumeTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- A reply's row is React, Copy, Read aloud and ⋯ (Quote, Branch, Retry on the newest reply (2026-10-28, issue 1420, #1446), Pin reply, and Show thinking when the run above it has thinking that Settings keeps for On request (see Steps in a turn)); no more icons of their own under messages (2026-10-23, #1156; 2026-10-25, #1243).
- Pin lives in the long-press and selection menus, not the row: Pin for a passage, Pin reply for the whole reply (2026-10-20, #982 and #1097; 2026-10-23, #1156).
- A branch opens by the stored id `session.create` names, and by its runtime id only when Hermes names none: Hermes' `session.resume` finds sessions only by stored id or title, so the runtime id is "session not found" (2026-10-27, issue 1400, #1402).
- Your own message's row is Copy and ⋯ (Quote, Edit and resend). Quote puts its words in the draft as a `>` quote, as a selection's Quote does (2026-10-28, issue 1420, #1446).
- Edit and resend takes back the message and everything after it through Hermes' rewind, as /undo does, and puts its words back ahead of whatever is typed in that chat's draft (even when another chat opened meanwhile), a quoted reply as its "Replying to" chip. When the composer already holds a different chip, the restored one comes back as a `>` quote, for a send that didn't go too; it asks first when later messages would go, and takes nothing back when Hermes' history holds later messages it didn't ask about (sent from another device), loading them so the next try asks. /undo and /retry keep their words in their chat's draft too when another chat opened while they ran. Not offered for a message with pictures, files or a recording, which can't come back as they were. There is no edit in place: the model already answered the original (2026-10-28, issue 1420, #1446).
- Retry is on the newest reply only while it answers the last message sent (a message after it, stopped or unanswered, is what /retry would resend), runs /retry, and asks first when the newest turn ran steps, since retrying runs them again (2026-10-28, issue 1420, #1446).
- Tapping a "Replying to" card scrolls to the reply it quoted, in a chat and in a group room (a member's message), found by its words since the envelope carries no id; one not in the loaded transcript says so. A waiting message's card, and a room's message still sending, looks through the whole transcript, since it comes last. Desktop groups, read-only, and the saved copy, whose rows stand in until Hermes sends the chat's (so Edit and resend and Retry are off there), keep a card that doesn't jump (2026-10-28, issue 1420, #1446; the copy drawn as the chat's own rows since 2026-10-30, #1550).
- Double-tap and long-press on text stay text selection; reactions come from React or a reaction chip (2026-10-07, #437).
- The selection's touch watcher on a text view (prose, code boxes, table cells) never takes part in a gesture, and fails once the last finger lifts, as the app's other touch watchers do: UIKit resets the gestures a touch went through only when all of them have finished, so one left waiting held the chat's scroll and the swipe back, and a flick from the screen's left edge over a code box or a table left the chat unable to scroll until it was opened again (2026-11-06, issue 1687, #1843; found on Eric's phone with the debugger).
- Read Aloud has no estimated follow-along highlight; only exact word timings from Hermes would bring it back (2026-10-19, #923).
- A quoted reply travels in the message text, since Hermes has no field for hidden context (2026-10-04, #387).
- Deleting a bot drops its Bot Chat pins under every profile, not only the one in use (#982 follow-up, #1191).
- The Pinned replies sheet opened from a chat starts on This chat, with All chats a tap away and that chat's section first; the filter shows while this chat and another both have pins, and once shown stays until the sheet closes, so unpinning this chat's last pin leaves This chat empty. Opened from the Chats list it lists every chat by latest pin (2026-10-25, issue 1267, #1269).

**Open gaps**
- Group rooms still show Copy, Quote and Read aloud as three icons, with no React and no ⋯ (#1156). Edit and resend and Retry are not needed there: a room is shared and has no rewind.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1843 (the selection's touch watcher fails once the last finger lifts, issue 1687; menus and selection unchanged); 2026-11-04, #1751 (a pin's excerpt leaves out the plugin's hidden `::conduit-board` line, see Cards Hermes shows); 2026-11-01, #1631 (on the gateway's own listener this speaks the session authority's shapes, see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-31, #1590 (a group room's jump goes through its own TranscriptScroller too, the quoted message at the top with the room browsing there, without the animation the room's stack gave it; Code); 2026-10-31, #1577 (the jump goes through TranscriptScroller now that chats draw on the transcript; Code); 2026-10-31, #1566 (the jump's rule in TranscriptScroller, not called yet; Code); 2026-10-31, #1565 (the reply offering Retry, and the latest one reactions go to, are worked out once per change of the rows drawn; Code); 2026-10-31, #1552 (a deleted bot's kept settings answers go with its pins and held rows; pins unchanged); 2026-10-30, #1550 (the saved copy's rows are drawn by the chat's own row view while they stand in; their cards still don't jump and Hermes' actions stay off); 2026-10-30, #1524 (Read Aloud says a Desktop card's note, and a quote chip names one); 2026-10-28, #1446 (your own message's ⋯ with Quote and Edit and resend, Retry in the newest reply's ⋯, the "Replying to" card's jump in chats and group rooms, ComposerDraft.restoring keeps a second chip as a quote for failed sends too, the saved copy's cards don't jump, /undo and /retry words kept when the chat changes; selection and long-press menus unchanged); 2026-10-27, #1402 (Branch opens the new chat by its stored id; the row, menus and pins needed no change); 2026-10-26, #1311 (a drawn reply's text view is laid out as it mounts; plugin (same status rows, Update and Cancel) · the Settings and Chats notice
that opens it · Settings > Notifications' Compatibility links to the plugin
page (host and pairing rows) · Finish setting up's plugin row · Settings > Conduit plugin >
Update notices, which decides when all three ask · the host-run update on the
notifier (`/self/update`) and its push when it ends · the phone-run steps for
a plugin without it · Restart Gateway (Settings > Connection and the chat's Gateway sheet), which shares the drain step's running-work list and Restart now (`GatewayWaitView`) · every profile that turns the plugin on, which the dashboard links to the main install (`notifier/profile_copies.py`) · what a plugin request says on a profile that turned the plugin off, and the README's steps for turning it on there · every screen that reads a plugin route's 404 as "update the plugin": call watches, Gemini, Qwen, Grok, GPT-Live and Local Live (and the Watch's GPT-Live check), the speech server, chat takeover, phone, health and location sharing and their deletes, Log to Hermes, voice-call saves, Kanban's task lookup · Pulse's loop, which runs in the dashboard (`notifier/pulse.py`, its lease in `notifier/pulse_store.py`) · the plugin's CHANGELOG.md (What's New) · what the
confirmation and README say about restarts

- Tests: `ConduitTests/GatewayRestartTests+PluginUpdate.swift`, `ConduitTests/DashboardProxySignOutTests.swift` (testAPluginTurnedOffForTheProfileSaysHowToTurnItOn), `ConduitTests/HermesCallsTests.swift` (testWatchForAProfileWithThePluginOffSaysHowToTurnItOn), `ConduitTests/ChatTakeoverTests.swift` (testAProfileWithThePluginOffSaysHowToTurnItOn), `ConduitTests/VoiceHistoryTests.swift` (testVoiceHistoryMapsThePluginsStatuses), `notifier/tests/test_self_update.py`, `notifier/tests/test_install_scan.py`, `notifier/upstream/test_install_scan.py` (Hermes' own scanner over the shipped files, on every notifier PR)

**Rulings**
- No automatic updates: restarts are the user's call; the notice offers each version once (Never offers none, below), and Update runs the whole update (2026-10-13, #582, Eric).
- App Store builds are asked only below the stable floor, TestFlight and Xcode builds for every version on notifier main (2026-10-20, #984; 2026-10-23, #1166, Eric). Superseded: Automatic is gone, and Stable versions only is the default for every build, Automatic's users included, so TestFlight and Xcode builds ask for the stable version too unless the user picks Every new version. Conduit no longer reads where it was installed from. A plugin release a build needs between App Store builds gets there by raising channels.yaml's `stable:` (2026-10-30, #1529, Eric: too many plugin updates).
- The notice stays until the update truly ends: after the host is done, it shows Reconnecting until Conduit is back, has read the new plugin and the gateway serves, and only then says the plugin is ready. A failure the plugin's report contradicts (the new version runs) reads as ready, not as a silent close (2026-10-24, Eric's report on build 228).
- A gateway restart that takes the dashboard down with it (a service manager restarting both) still finishes the host job: the restarted dashboard marks it done when it loaded the new version (2026-10-24, notifier 0.69.1).
- An update never restarts the gateway into a running turn: Hermes' restart then refuses new work until the turn ends (agent.restart_after_turn_timeout, 30 minutes by default; `--interrupt` only skips the CLI's question), and Conduit can't reach the gateway meanwhile. The host-run update waits for the gateway's running work first, while it still serves (up to 30 minutes, then restarts anyway), and a restart that still meets work is waited on as draining, not failed after three minutes; both show as "Letting running tasks finish…". A dashboard restarted during the wait (before the restart is sent) restarts the gateway itself and ends the job, rather than marking it done while the gateway runs the old plugin (2026-11-05, notifier #554, issue notifier #546). Superseded in part: the host-run update's own wait is 10 minutes, not 30, since past it the gateway's restart waits for the same work again up to its own cap and the two stacked to an hour (2026-11-07, Eric: an update sat on "Letting running tasks finish…" behind a mail poller's turn he didn't know was running).
- "Letting running tasks finish…" names what it waits on and offers Restart now, in the update (Settings and the notice) and in Restart Gateway alike: each chat (its bot, title and running time), cron job or unnamed task, and when the gateway restarts anyway. Restart now ends the update's wait, stops the chats Conduit can reach (session.interrupt, which a draining gateway still takes), and whatever still runs a few seconds later the plugin ends with `systemctl restart --no-block` on a gateway systemd runs (its stop gives work agent.restart_drain_timeout, 60 s, then ends it). A second `hermes gateway restart` can't do it: it joins the drain under way. This replaces the earlier "no interrupt button" ruling (2026-11-07, Eric: "let me have a way to force restart too"; #1909 with notifier 590).
- An update works on a dashboard that kept running after Hermes was updated under it. That process holds a mix of the Hermes it started with and the new one, and Hermes' own pull fails inside its code ("'PythonDeclaration' object has no attribute 'installs_packages'", a dashboard started on Hermes 0.22.3 updated to 0.22.4+). The host-run update notices Hermes' loaded files changed on disk since the process started and pulls in a fresh process of the Hermes on disk; the dashboard restart at the end of the update loads it here too. For a host still on an older plugin, Conduit restarts the dashboard and runs the update again once when the pull fails inside Hermes' code with a missing name, and otherwise says to restart the dashboard (2026-11-06, #1893 with notifier #585, issue 1889).
- Every process the update restarts runs the new code at once, Pulse's loop included: a dashboard restarted by its service manager (a new pid) takes Pulse over from the old one without waiting out its lease (2026-10-26, notifier #392, Eric's report on 0.81.1).
- The notice's What's New opens the notes in a sheet, presented by the notes it shows (a sheet item, not a flag); Settings shows the same notes inline in a disclosure (2026-10-25, Eric's report of a blank sheet, #1227).
- Update notices has a Never choice: the notice, the Settings card and Finish setting up never ask for an update (a newer version, a missing feature, a plugin below this build's floor), only for the restart of an update already on the host. A missing plugin is still offered for install: installing isn't updating. Settings > Notifications' Compatibility host link follows the same `needsAttention`, so under Never it points at the plugin page only for an install, a restart or a plugin that isn't running; its pairing-row link for an outdated pairing still shows, being on a Settings page rather than a prompt. Settings > Conduit plugin still lists missing features and offers the update whatever the choice (`updateAvailable` ignores it); Finish setting up shows done, saying a newer version or the missing features wait in Settings. "Not now" on a restart (under any choice) belongs to the version on disk, so the next update's restart asks again, and a "Not now" prunes only its own dashboard's older ones. It began as malaiwah's "Only when needed" (#1521), tied to `recommendedVersion`; that hand-set floor (0.48.0) sits below the stable one, so Eric made it plain Never (2026-10-30, #1529; Michel's first-time walkthrough found the same update asked for in four places).
- Every file the plugin ships passes Hermes' install scan, which reads the whole checkout (the contract tests and the relay included) and refuses a dangerous verdict even with --force: no literal that looks like a token outside test folders (2026-10-27, notifier #418, Eric's host stuck on 0.84.1).
- An update reaches every profile that turns the plugin on. Hermes loads a profile's chat-turn plugins from its own plugins/ folder only (its dashboard falls back to the main home's), so the dashboard links each such profile's plugins/conduit_push to the main install when it starts, before an update restarts the gateway, and when the main copy loads. A copy the profile had of its own (a clone's) moves to its plugins-backup/, never deleted. Where no link can be made, the main install is copied in, marked as ours and replaced when it falls behind. A profile counts when its config lists the plugin in plugins.enabled, or has no plugins.enabled list (Hermes then loads what's installed) and holds a copy already. A profile whose allow-list leaves the plugin out or disables it, whose config can't be read, or whose own copy is newer than the main install (a build put there on purpose) is left alone. This isn't an automatic update: it runs what the user already updated to (2026-10-31, notifier #482, issue #1538: Eric's Nahida, Raiden and Zhongli ran 0.1.0 from July, so their pushes had no chat title and opened nothing).
- No high finding either: one makes the verdict caution, which the one-tap update can't confirm, so it holds every host on the old version just as surely. The notifier's upstream contract runs Hermes' own scanner on every PR and fails on a high or critical finding; README examples write a secret as a placeholder (`<token>`), never as a shell variable (2026-10-29, notifier #467, issue #1500: the crash report curl examples held hosts on 0.119.x).

**Open gaps**
- A profile that hasn't turned the plugin on gets Hermes' bare 404 "Plugin not found" for every plugin request, the Folder tab's and the Artifacts list's among them. Conduit says which plugin and profile, and how to turn it on: add it to plugins.enabled in that profile's config.yaml on the host (and take it out of plugins.disabled) and restart Hermes, since `hermes -p <name> plugins enable` finds only a plugin in the profile's own plugins/ folder, which a profile made without --clone doesn't have until the dashboard links it, and it links only a profile that turned the plugin on. The dashboard's own profile gets `hermes plugins enable`. It stays a 404, so screens that fall back on one still do. Uploads (room files, room pictures) get the same words. A screen that reads a 404 as an older plugin asks first whether it was this refusal, and then gives these words in its own place instead of "update the plugin": the live model's answer when a call watch is refused (issue 1671), the live voices' and the speech server's status, takeover, the sharing pauses, Log to Hermes, the Watch's GPT-Live check and Save Now's result for voice calls. A voice call that meets it waits to save rather than being marked as one the host can't save, a delete that meets it isn't counted as done (nothing on the host was deleted), and Kanban's task lookup doesn't read it as "not on this board". Should Hermes give the same bare words for a plugin removed from the host, a delete waits there rather than counting as done: it errs on the side of never claiming a deletion that didn't happen. A plugin that isn't installed at all doesn't reach these words in practice: without Conduit's plugin the unscoped capabilities read fails first and the update notice offers the install, Kanban is bundled, and rich-ui is asked only once Hermes lists it. Proposed in #1633 (2026-11-01, issue #1630), not yet ruled on by Eric.
- Conduit doesn't turn the plugin on for a profile itself, as Hermes' own plugin routes act on the dashboard's profile only; a one-tap Turn on for this profile is left for Eric to decide (#1633).
- Hermes Desktop's own serve process on the host keeps the old plugin until Desktop restarts; nothing tells the user.
- The running-work list and Restart now need the plugin the dashboard is running to have them (0.135.0+). The first update to 0.135 runs on the old plugin, so its drain step still shows the bare label; later updates and Restart Gateway show the list.
- Where the gateway itself serves the dashboard (`hermes webapp`), a draining gateway refuses every plugin request, so the list and Restart now can't be read there; Conduit shows the bare label. Conduit's socket still takes session.interrupt then, so the chats could be stopped from the chat list's own sessions; not built.
- The forced restart is systemd only; launchd, Windows and s6 hosts get a 501 saying to stop and start the gateway on the host.
- A dashboard without a fixed basic-auth secret signs Conduit out at every restart; the updater signs in again, but the chat may land on the sign-in screen.

**Checked:** 2026-11-07, #1909 with notifier 590 (the drain step and Restart Gateway name what they wait on and offer Restart now; the host's own wait is 10 minutes; the plugin's README /self sections and CHANGELOG.md describe it; the confirmation's text needed no change); 2026-11-06, #1893 with notifier #585 (issue 1889: an update on a dashboard Hermes was updated under pulls in a fresh Hermes process, and Conduit restarts the dashboard and runs it again once for an older plugin; Settings' and the notice's failure row show Hermes' words with the restart hint; the phone-run steps' error gets the hint; the README needed no change); 2026-11-05, #1779 (a review on notifier #554: a dashboard restarted during the wait for the gateway's work restarts the gateway itself; the app needed no change); 2026-11-05, #1777 with notifier #554 (notifier issue 546): the host-run update waits for the gateway's running work before its restart and waits out a draining restart; Settings' and the notice's step reads the host's gateway_stage as draining; the confirmation already said the restarts wait for running chats; the phone-run steps keep their own drain watch (GatewayRestartMonitor's 10 minutes) and are only for plugins without the host-run update; the README's /self/update section and CHANGELOG.md describe it; 2026-11-02, #1675 (issue 1671: every screen that read a plugin route's 404 as "update the plugin" says how to turn the plugin on for a profile that turned it off, the live model's answer to a refused call watch first; deletes and voice-call saves no longer count it as done or unsupported; the README needed no change); 2026-11-02, #1665 (#1663 made requestEncodedJSON count writes for the first reads' fence; the plugin-off refusal needed no change); 2026-11-01, #1633 with notifier #505 (issue #1630): a request to a profile that turned the plugin off says how to turn it on, every screen through the bridge; the README's steps for another profile name the config.yaml route for one made without --clone; the update path needed no change; 2026-10-31, #1557 with notifier #482 (issue #1538): a profile's turns load only its own plugins folder, so the dashboard links every profile that turns the plugin on to the main install; the app's update path, notice and version check needed no change, as they read the main install every profile now runs; 2026-10-30, #1529 (carrying #1521): the in-chat notice, the Settings card and Finish setting up all read `updateRecommended`, so the choice reaches each, from launch; Settings' Update reads `updateAvailable`, which it leaves alone; under Never, Finish setting up still offers the update for a plugin older than 0.4, which can't report anything, as the setup step it is; the confirmation, README, CHANGELOG.md and the notifier needed no change (the update itself is unchanged); 2026-10-29, #1501 with notifier #467: Hermes' scan held the update at caution over two README curl examples (issue #1500); the app's update path and its error text needed no change; 2026-10-28, #1462 (the notifier code it lists moved from dashboard/plugin_api.py to dashboard/api/, one module per feature, notifier #449); 2026-10-27, at #1350 with notifier #418: Hermes' install scan refused 0.95.0 over upstream/conftest.py's token; the app's update path needed no change; 2026-10-26, at #1293 with notifier #392: the dashboard restart itself needed no change (systemd restarts it with the gateway, elsewhere the update re-execs it);
