## Moving pictures

A bot's or profile's picture can move: a GIF, another animated picture or a
short video picked with Choose GIF or Video, or a still photo brought to
life on the phone, becomes a looping animated PNG, stored and synced like any
picture.

**Siblings:** Choose GIF or Video beside Choose Photo in New Bot and Edit Bot's
Edit Picture menu
(see Bots: create and edit), and Bring to Life there for a still · the same
items in a Settings > Profiles card's Edit menu (the profile picker) · a
profile kept on the phone alone (a gateway without the asset store) · the
faces that play it: Bots Home's portraits, the Bot Overview's header, the bot
editor and the Profiles cards (see Bots Home) · the faces that keep the first
frame: chat rows, the transcript, the profile strip, group room members, the
@ list and every menu (not needed: lists and rows, where many moving faces
would cost battery for little) · Hermes' asset store (not needed: it takes a
PNG up to 2 MB by its bytes, and an animated PNG is one) · Hermes Desktop
(not needed: its picture is an img tag, which plays it; its own uploads stay
stills, upstream) · Duplicate (not needed: it copies the bytes) · generated
pictures and group room pictures (not needed: Hermes' image generation and
Image Playground make stills, and rooms show as rows and chips) · Watch, CarPlay, widgets and
notifications (not needed: they draw no faces) · the notifier (not needed: it
serves no pictures) · the text that describes it (the editor's caption under
the Edit Picture menu, which names a brought-to-life still too, README.md's bots and profiles lines)

**Code**
- Making one: `Conduit/Services/AnimatedAvatar.swift` (frames from a picture file or a video, thinned, squared and written as a looping APNG under maxBytes, picture(fromPicked:), message(for:), pick(from:): a Photos pick's own file, a still among them used as a photo)
- Saving: `Conduit/Views/BotEditorSheet.swift` (Choose GIF or Video's photosPicker, useAnimation, previewPlayback, canSave waiting for it, the caption), `Conduit/Views/ProfilePickerSheet.swift` (the Edit menu's Choose GIF or Video, saveAnimation), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (setProfilePhoto's animation, moveDevicePhotoToHermes carrying a phone-only moving picture over as it is, through BotAvatarImage.hermesPicture in `Conduit/Services/BotManagement.swift`, botAvatarPlayback, profileAvatarPlayback), `Conduit/Services/ProfileAppearanceStore.swift` (saveAvatar keeps a moving picture's bytes; ProfileAvatarImageCache.isAnimated and revision)
- Bring to Life: `Conduit/Services/LivingPortrait.swift` (Vision's subject cut-out, the loop's pose, frames over a softened background, message(for:)), `Conduit/Views/BotEditorSheet.swift` (bringToLife, the Edit Picture menu's item while a still shows), `Conduit/Views/ProfilePickerSheet.swift` (the Edit menu's Bring to Life, for a still photo)
- Playing: `Conduit/Views/Components/AnimatedAvatarFrames.swift` (AnimatedAvatarFrames, AnimatedAvatarPlayer), `Conduit/Views/BotEditorSheet.swift` (BotAvatarView's playback), `Conduit/Views/BotRosterView.swift` (BotMonogramView's animates), `Conduit/Views/ProfilePickerSheet.swift` (ProfileAvatarView's animates), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2BotsHome.swift` (the portrait and the Bot Overview's header)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/AnimatedAvatarTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- Pictures people pick, not generated video: most Hermes hosts have no video backend, so a moving picture is a GIF or a short video the person brings (Eric, 2026-11-05). Bring to Life, the on-device living portrait, is the one made from a still (Eric 2026-11-05, #1822, after trying the demo): Vision lifts the subject out, and it breathes and sways over a softened copy of the picture in a seamless 3-second loop, 36 frames, the same APNG; nothing inside the subject moves. It's offered for a still only, in the bot editor while a still shows (a fresh pick to save or discard, a picture from Image Playground included) and in a profile card's Edit menu (saved at once, like a photo); a picture with no subject Vision can find says so.
- A moving picture is an animated PNG in the same `avatar` asset, so nothing else changes: Hermes keeps it, Desktop plays it, and every still face shows its first frame. It's made on the phone from the first 3 seconds, at most 36 frames, 256 px, then smaller and fewer frames until it fits 1.5 MB, under Hermes' 2 MB cap since every fetch sends it whole; one that won't fit says to try a shorter or simpler clip.
- It's picked with Choose GIF or Video, the Photos picker, which hands over the original file; Choose Photo stays the cropping picker for stills, since its crop keeps a GIF's first frame only and Conduit has no crop of its own (Eric 2026-11-05, #1812: a GIF moved in the picker, not on the crop screen or after). The Photos picker can't trim, so a longer video gives its first 3 seconds. A still picked there is used as a photo, centered, without the crop.
- It plays only where the face is what you're looking at (a Bots Home portrait, the Bot Overview, the editors), only while the app is active, and never with Reduce Motion or in Low Power Mode; Bots Home's portraits also stop while the tab doesn't show, as their motion does. ImageIO's player decodes a frame at a time, so a moving face holds one frame.

**Open gaps**
- Not yet measured on a device: what many moving portraits cost on Bots Home.
- Bring to Life's cut-out is only tried on a device: Vision's foreground mask needs one, so the tests draw the subject. Group room pictures don't offer it (rooms show as rows and chips).
- A video can't be trimmed to the part to keep: the first 3 seconds are used.
- A Live Photo is picked as a still.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1862 (nothing played: the player's Group had no child to start it, now a ZStack; its items sit in the bot editor's Edit Picture menu); 2026-11-05, #1822 (Bring to Life: a still's subject sways, made on the phone); 2026-11-05, #1813 (Image Playground's pictures are stills too, see Pictures from Image Playground); 2026-11-05, #1817 (a picked file with no known extension is told apart by its bytes, so a video is never read whole); 2026-11-05, #1812 (Choose GIF or Video, the Photos picker, since Choose Photo's crop flattened a GIF on Eric's device); 2026-11-05, #1782 (the Bot Overview's header plays its fallback profile face too; the phone-only carry-over is tested); 2026-11-05, #1778 (added: moving pictures from a GIF or a short video)

## Pictures from Image Playground

Apple's Image Playground makes a bot's, a profile's or a group chat's
picture, using the system's own sheet. It needs no Hermes backend, no key
and no cost to us.

**Siblings:** Edit Bot and New Bot's Generate (see Bots: create and edit) ·
a Settings > Profiles card's Edit menu · a group chat's menu, in the
drawer shell and V2's conversation menu (GroupRoomActionItems) · Hermes' own
generated pictures (kept, next to it in a menu when both work) · Moving
pictures (not needed: Image Playground makes stills) · Watch, CarPlay,
widgets and notifications (not needed: they draw no faces) · Hermes Desktop
and the notifier (not needed: the picture is saved like a chosen photo) ·
the text that describes it (the editor's hint, README.md's bots and
profiles lines)

**Code**
- `Conduit/Views/Components/ImagePlaygroundPicture.swift` (availability, current, Prompt, image(at:), imagePlaygroundPicture, readsImagePlaygroundAvailability)
- `Conduit/Views/BotEditorSheet.swift` (generateItems in the Edit Picture menu, playgroundPrompt, the hint), `Conduit/Views/ProfilePickerSheet.swift` (the Edit menu item), `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (GroupRoomPictureRequest.playground, GroupRoomPicturePicker's sheet)
- `project.yml` (ImagePlayground.framework weak-linked: iOS 17 has none)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ImagePlaygroundPictureTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- It's offered only where `supportsImagePlayground` is true: iOS 18.1+, Apple Intelligence hardware, turned on and set up, in a supported language and region. The system doesn't say which condition failed, so 8 GB of RAM or more (every Apple Intelligence device has it, every iPhone without it has 6 GB or less) separates a device that could turn it on from one that never can.
- A capable device with it off gets one line in the bot editor naming Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri. No public link opens that page. Menus (Profiles, group chats) only show the item when it works. A device that never can shows nothing. (Eric 2026-11-05, #1813: hint if capable, else hide.)
- The sheet starts from the name as one concept and the description and SOUL (a group's members) as text to extract ideas from, capped at 2,000 characters, with the current picture as the source image. It opens on Animation, the style that reads best as a small round face. The person can change all of it in the sheet.
- The picked picture is saved like a chosen photo: a 256 px PNG for a bot or a profile on Hermes, a JPEG for a profile kept on the phone alone, the room's 256 px JPEG for a group chat. The headless ImageCreator isn't used: it stops working in iOS 27.

**Open gaps**
- Not yet tried on a device: the sheet can't run on a simulator without Apple Intelligence. On a Mac (iPad app), what `supportsImagePlayground` says is untested.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1862 (Generate is an item, or a submenu, in the bot editor's Edit Picture menu); 2026-11-05, #1813 (added)

## Opening a Bot Chat

How Conduit finds a bot's one Bot Chat (the hidden session titled "Bot Chat"
in the bot's profile), makes it the first time, and opens it.

**Siblings:** a tap in the Bots list, on Hermes' roster or the one kept from
its last answer, a Bots Home portrait or its overview's Chat (#1678) · a new bot's first open and its
introduction · a push or a call from a Bot Chat · a link, card or artifact
that names a bot · a widget, Shortcuts or shared-draft open of a Bot Chat (opens an existing chat only, by the lookup's row) · a last-chat restore that lands on a Bot Chat (resumes the saved row's stored id) · Hermes Desktop's Bot Chat open (same lookup, same title,
same stored-id open)

**Code**
- Open: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (openBotChat, resolveAndOpenBotChat, createAndOpenBotChat, adoptWinningBotChat, openCanonicalBotChat, openNewBotChat, openLinkedBotChat)
- Where it shows: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (beginOpeningBotChat, endOpeningBotChat, botChatOpeningPlaced, botChatOpening, placesConversationAsBotChat), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2Shell.swift` (openConversation)
- Lookup: `Conduit/Services/BotModeModels.swift` (BotChatLookupRow, BotChatResolver, BotChatTitleCollision), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (findBotChatSession, createBotChatSession)
- Callers: `Conduit/Views/BotRosterView.swift`, `Conduit/Views/V2/V2BotsHome.swift` (BotPortraitCell), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2VoiceButton.swift` (call, Bots Home's voice menu, which then starts voice in the chat), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (routeBotOwnedNotification, the push and call route), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (openWidgetConversation), `Conduit/Services/AppState+WidgetLaunch.swift`

**Rulings**
- One chat per bot, found by its title on the bot's profile; a lookup that fails, or comes back empty while the roster still names a chat, never makes a new one (Desktop's rule).
- A chat Conduit makes is opened by its stored id, as Desktop does: Hermes resumes a chat by its stored key and answers 4007 for a runtime id. Opening the runtime id failed the open, so a new bot's first message went to a chat Conduit didn't have open and was gone on the way back (2026-10-26, a tester's report via Eric, #1300). A create that names no stored id is found by its title, which has just landed, and that row is opened; the runtime id is never resumed.
- A title collision while making the chat adopts the chat that won instead of making a second one.
- A Bot Chat opened from Bots (a portrait, the overview's Chat, a Bots list row, a new bot) shows in Bots whatever chat was open before: the list marks the bot's chat as coming before it closes, since the shell places the conversation then, before the open lands. The shell spends the mark as it places it, and the open's end clears it, opened or not, so a plain session a notification opens meanwhile still goes to Sessions (2026-11-03, #1700).
- A room tapped on Bots Home uses the same mark, under its `room:` key (`BotZoomArm.roomKey`), so it opens in Bots over whatever chat was open too (2026-11-06, #1864; see Bots Home).
- On the gateway's own listener the chat is made in the session authority's create shape, still hidden and following the profile's config: the authority takes both keys (2026-11-01, #1631).
- A row of the kept roster opens through the same lookup, its kept chat counting as the roster's last confirmation, so an empty lookup still makes no chat, and so does a widget's open of a kept bot's chat (2026-10-31, #1568).
- A push or a call from a Bot Chat is routed by the roster Hermes confirmed on this connection, never the kept one: a push that crosses profiles asks for the roster again at the tap, and one that can't be told apart from a workspace's waits or is refused, as before. A kept copy is no evidence: a bot made since its answer is missing from it, and its chat would open as the workspace's own (2026-10-31, #1568).

**Open gaps**
- The new-bot fix (#1300) was read from Conduit's and Hermes' code, not reproduced on a device; a tester confirms it on the next build.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1864 (a room tapped on Bots Home is marked as coming too, under its own key); 2026-11-03, #1714 (Bots Home's voice menu opens a Bot Chat the same way, marked as coming from Bots); 2026-11-03, #1703 (the `bot-workstreams` qualifiers go now that Bot Mode is on main); 2026-11-03, #1701 (`bot-workstreams` merged into main for TestFlight, as its PRs left this entry); 2026-11-03, #1700 (on `bot-workstreams`, a Bot Chat opened from Bots, by a portrait, the overview's Chat, a row or a new bot, stays in Bots whatever was open before, the mark spent as the shell places it; the open itself unchanged; Code, Rulings); 2026-11-03, #1686 (on `bot-workstreams`, only a chat opened by its portrait's tap zooms out of it; every other open of a Bot Chat, a notification's, widget's, Shortcut's, call's or link's, pushes as before; the open itself unchanged); 2026-11-03, #1678 (Bots Home's portrait and its overview's Chat open through openBotChat, as the row did; the lookup is unchanged); 2026-11-01, #1631 (on the gateway's own listener the lookup and the hidden, profile-following create take the session authority's shapes, probed by notifier #504's listener leg; see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-31, #1568 (a kept row's tap and a widget's open of a kept bot's chat; a push's routing keeps to Hermes' confirmed roster, recorded); 2026-10-28, #1457 (the main bot goes by its Conduit name, see Profile names); 2026-10-28, #1448 (a restored Bot Chat names an unnamed bot by its id capitalized, also when saved with the id as its label); 2026-10-26, #1300.

## Bot mentions and teammate messages

How the user brings another bot into a chat, and how bots' messages to each
other read in it.

**Siblings:** the @ list while typing · Mention a Bot in the composer's + menu ·
chats, project chats and Bot Chats (the chat's own bot is left out) · group
rooms (their own @ list and recipient picks) · the note that tells the bot
who each tag is · a teammate's delivery in the chat ("Message from Atlas") ·
the bot's folded reply to it ("Replied to Atlas") · the same notes in a saved
chat's copy · the sender's step ("Messaged Atlas") · the Live Activity's tool line ·
Hermes Desktop's bot chat · chat list previews and quotes · Read Aloud and live voice ·
the bot's SOUL messaging section · README.md's bots line · the plugin's
move of an old Bot Chat under its gateway, which keeps a bot reachable while its chat is open

**Code**
- Tags and the note to the bot: `Conduit/Services/BotMentions.swift`, `Conduit/Services/GroupChatModels.swift` (MentionAutocomplete), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (composerMentionCandidates and mentionAnnotatedOutboundText, from the shown roster, which is in the bots' order, see Bots Home)
- Composer: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (mentionCandidates, attachmentButton), `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift`
- Teammate messages: `Conduit/Services/BotTeammateMessages.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (shownBotRoster, and shownBotRosterChanged, which TeammateMessageNote reads it again on), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (TeammateMessageNote, TeammateReplyNote, SettledToolCardContent.stepTitle, runningToolTitle), `Conduit/Views/ChatRowState.swift` (teammateReplies, botLabels), `Conduit/Views/ChatActivityRows.swift` (ChatStepSubject, ChatWorkingLine.currentToolTitle), `Conduit/Views/ChatRowDisclosure.swift` (how the notes open); a saved copy's rows are the chat's own while they stand in, folded from the rows drawn (`Conduit/Views/ChatRowState.swift`, ChatRowFacts.teammateReplies, worked out by `Conduit/Views/TranscriptModel.swift` once per change of the rows)
- Previews, quotes and speech: `Conduit/Services/PreviewText.swift` (strip), read by the chat list and spoken previews
- Tool categories: `Shared/Widgets/HermesTurnActivity.swift`, and its twin, `notifier/live_activity.py` (`tool_category`, notifier #338)
- The messaging protocol a bot is born with: `Conduit/Services/BotManagement.swift` (BotSoul)
- An old Bot Chat moved under its gateway: `notifier/bot_chat_adopt.py` (notifier #492)

**Rulings**
- A tag is sent as typed; Conduit only adds a note naming the teammate, and the bot sends with its own `message_agent` tool. Nothing is delivered from the phone (upstream Desktop's mention middleware).
- Mention a Bot inserts the same tag the @ list does, at the end of the draft (2026-10-24, #1181, Eric asked for an easier way to tag another bot).
- A user turn signed "Message from 🤖 Name", "Message from Name (@handle)" or "[Message from agent 'name']" is a teammate's delivery and reads as a note with the bot's face, its text one tap away. An unsigned "Message from Name: …" stays the user's text, unlike Desktop (2026-10-24, #1181).
- A `message_agent` call, or a terminal `hermes -p name chat … -q "Message from …"` run, reads as "Messaged Name" (2026-10-24, #1181).
- A step's subject line prefers a `message` field after the usual keys, for every tool, so a delivery shows what was said (2026-10-24, #1181).
- `message_agent` is a messaging tool on the Live Activity, in both the app's and the plugin's category lists (2026-10-24, #1181, notifier #338).
- A delivery previews as "Atlas: what it said" wherever `PreviewText` reads it (the chat list, spoken previews), and its body renders as Markdown. A quote is taken from the opened note's text, so it carries no signature. Read Aloud and live voice speak replies, never a delivery, so they need nothing (2026-10-24, #1192).
- The bot's replies to a delivery it didn't ask for fold under "Replied to Atlas" until the user next writes; a delivery answering the bot's own `message_agent` doesn't fold, and a reply still streaming stays open (upstream `dispatchedTo`, 2026-10-24).
- A terminal or `process` delivery's step shows the message, not the command, and the teammate's answer from the output as a note under it; a failed send (an error or non-zero exit) stays a plain tool step (2026-10-24).
- The working line says "Messaging Atlas…" while a delivery runs. The Live Activity keeps "Sending a message": it carries only a tool category, never names, by design (2026-10-24).
- A signature is read from the first 320 characters, so a message of any length is still a delivery; tool calls past 64 KB aren't scanned. A signed name may contain "(" ("Atlas (v2)") (2026-10-24).
- A "Messaged" step names the bot from the roster, and redraws when the roster loads (2026-10-24). Until Hermes' roster answers, the notes, replies and steps name teammates from the bots kept from its last answer, so a name doesn't change when it does, and the @ list, Mention a Bot and the note to the bot offer and name the kept bots; a tag for one Hermes no longer has reaches no one, as a mistyped tag does (2026-10-31, #1568).
- Group rooms have no Mention a Bot item: their recipient picks do the same job (2026-10-24).
- A Bot Chat from before Hermes' gateway owned sessions (no chat_id, no local keys) is moved under its profile's gateway by the plugin, a native resume and detach soon after a restart, because Hermes' relay only moves it while nothing holds it, and Conduit's open chat holds it: every message to that bot was refused, "held by another session writer" (2026-11-01, notifier #492, Eric's report on Zhongli; Zhongli's and Rei's moved by hand on .52 with his OK).
- A delivery's note and a folded reply open and close like every other row: the chat's scroller hears first, so the tapped row stays put, and the choice outlives the row being rebuilt (2026-10-25, Eric's report: opening either one froze the app until iOS ended it).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-03, #1703 (the `bot-workstreams` qualifiers go now that Bot Mode is on main); 2026-11-03, #1701 (`bot-workstreams` merged into main for TestFlight, as its PRs left this entry); 2026-11-03, #1679 (on `bot-workstreams`, the @ list and Mention a Bot list the bots in the order set on Bots Home; tags and notes unchanged); 2026-11-01, #1619 (the working line also titles work tools, "Starting work…"; teammate deliveries' titles unchanged); 2026-11-01, #1604 (an old Bot Chat moved under its gateway by the plugin, notifier #492; Siblings, Code, Rulings); 2026-10-31, #1577 (TranscriptScroller is the scroller that hears first, now that chats draw on the transcript; Rulings); 2026-10-31, #1568 (teammates named, the @ list and Mention a Bot offered, and the note to the bot written from the kept bots until Hermes answers; a teammate's note reads the bots again once a change has landed, so the empty roster before Hermes answers never takes its name; Code); 2026-10-31, #1565 (the folded replies are worked out once per change of the rows drawn, not on each publish; Code); 2026-10-30, #1550 (a saved copy's notes and folded replies are drawn by the chat's own rows, folded as Hermes' rows will be); 2026-10-30, #1524 (Hermes Desktop's directives are read alongside, with their own entry, Cards made for Hermes Desktop); 2026-10-28, #1448 (an unnamed teammate is named by its id capitalized in its notes, replies and steps, through displayLabel); 2026-10-25, at #1259.

## Cron jobs delivered to a bot

A scheduled job whose `deliver` is `bot-chat` or `bot-chat:<profile>` sends
each run's report to that bot's Bot Chat. Hermes delivers it as a turn (the
bot reads it, acts and summarizes, a model call every run); with the plugin,
it just shows the report there unless the job lets the
bot act on it.

**Siblings:** the plugin's delivery in front of Hermes' own, in the process
that runs the jobs (a note in the Bot Chat, as Hermes writes a cron result
into a local chat, or Hermes' turn) · the per-job choice in the job editor,
under Delivery, and in a blueprint's form when its delivery is a Bot Chat, kept by the plugin beside the muted jobs (Cron
notifications), with its footer · the report's card in the Bot Chat · the
cron tool's result the model reads when it creates or edits such a job ·
the job's own run, its push and its session, unchanged (Cron runs) · a Bot
Chat in another profile (`bot-chat:<name>`), served by this process's
gateway or another · Hermes Desktop (not needed: it shows the note as
Hermes' local-chat note) · Watch and CarPlay (not needed: no transcript
cards) · notifier README.md's Cron jobs delivered to a Bot Chat

**Code**
- Notifier: `notifier/cron_bot_chat.py` (install, show, the note's HEADER, annotate for the cron tool), `notifier/cron_store.py` (act, set_act, lets_act), `notifier/dashboard/api/notifications.py` (`act` and `shows_reports` on /cron/notifications), `notifier/dashboard/api/capabilities.py` (cron-bot-chat-reports), `notifier/__init__.py` (install, _transform_tool_result)
- App: `Conduit/Services/CronNotifications.swift` (Choices with showsReports, choices, setActs), `Conduit/Services/AppState+CronNotifications.swift` (supportsCronBotChatReports, offersCronBotChatChoice, cronJobLetsBotAct, setCronJobLetsBotAct), `Conduit/Views/V2/CronJobEditorSheet.swift` (CronBotChoiceSection, deliversToBotChat, the editor's save, CronBlueprintForm's choice and create), `Conduit/Views/CronReportCard.swift` (CronBotChatReport, CronReportCard), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (the card in a system row)
- Tests: notifier tests/test_cron_bot_chat.py and tests/test_cron_notifications.py; `ConduitTests/GatewayRestartTests+CronNotifications.swift` (testABotChatJobsChoiceIsReadSentAndOptional, testABotChatReportReadsAsTheJobAndItsReport)

**Rulings**
- Each job has its own choice, Just show it by default, Let the bot act on it when picked (Eric, 2026-11-03: some people want the report in front of them without opening cron sessions, some want the bot to act on it). A job that isn't listed just shows, a new job included, and so does one the agent made.
- Just show it writes the report into the Bot Chat as a note, the way Hermes writes a cron result into a local chat: no turn, no model call, no reply; the bot sees it as context on its next turn. Its first line names the job and says nobody asked for a reply, and Conduit shows it as a card: the job's name, the first six lines, all of it a tap away. The first line is a contract between the plugin's HEADER and CronBotChatReport: change both together.
- A failure report follows the same choice, and is dropped where the profile hides warning notifications, as Hermes drops its own.
- The cron tool's result for such a job tells the model which it is, so it doesn't promise to act on a report it will only see.
- Only a Hermes that can write the note gets it (the route's `shows_reports`; v0.22.5 can't, the canary from late October can). On one that can't, every job keeps Hermes' turn and the editor offers no choice, so it never says a report just shows when it won't.

**Open gaps**
- A run's push still opens the run's own session, not the Bot Chat with its report.
- With no Bot Chat yet, a report has nowhere to show: the run records a delivery error (Hermes' turn would have made the chat).
- A Bot Chat whose owner runs in another process, or refuses it (one made in an app that Hermes' door hasn't taken yet), gets the note straight in its history, waiting up to a minute for a running turn; an app already showing it sees the note on its next read.
- The model can't change the choice itself; it tells the user to.
- Tried on Hermes' canary (notifier upstream/test_cron_bot_chat.py) but not yet on a phone: the card in a real Bot Chat, and a report that arrives during a turn.
- Hermes' own side, unchanged by the plugin: in the canary test, a job that lets the bot act was refused (`runtime_coordination_required`, delivery failed) while a socket session that had resumed the Bot Chat held its writer.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1793 (the job editor's delivery and When it runs built from Settings' pieces, see Sheets in Settings' look); 2026-11-03, #1703 (on main now, with notifier #519: the branch notes go and the notifier paths are checked; Eric: lookups is the default, with notifier 0.127.1, in the plugin and in Edit Bot > Work); 2026-11-03, #1701 (`bot-workstreams` merged into main for TestFlight, as its PRs left this entry); 2026-11-03, #1690 (added, with notifier #518).

## A cron job's Run history

A scheduled job's sheet lists that job's past runs, newest first, and a tap
opens the run's chat. A job that hasn't run says so.

**Siblings:** the sheet in both shells (one `CronJobDetailSheet`, from the
Cron list and from Tasks › Scheduled) · Run now, which reads the history
again · the dashboard's per-job route and the gateway's `cron.runs`, read
without a dashboard · the Scheduled filter in the chats list (not needed: it
lists `cronSessions`, every run, not one job's) · Watch, CarPlay and the
notifier (not needed: no cron history there)

**Code**
- App: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (loadCronRuns, cronRunsJobID, cronRunsLoaded, decodeCronRun), `Conduit/Models/Models.swift` (CronRun, isRun(ofJob:)), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (cronRuns), `Conduit/Views/SidebarView.swift` (CronJobDetailSheet's Run history), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2TasksView.swift` (the sheet from Tasks)
- Test: `ConduitTests/SidebarLayoutTests+CronRunHistory.swift`

**Rulings**
- The dashboard's per-job route is the job's history, an empty answer too: it never falls back to `cron.runs`, which lists every job's runs (#1707).
- Without a dashboard, `cron.runs` keeps only the runs that name the job (`job_id` or `cron_job_id`) or carry Hermes' run session id, `cron_<job id>_<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>`. A run that says neither is no job's: an empty history beats another job's.
- The list belongs to one job: opening another job shows a spinner until its answer lands, never the last job's runs or "This job has not run yet." before it knows, and only the newest read's answer is kept. Before the job's first answer, a read that fails, or can't be made offline, says so in the sheet instead; a later refresh that fails keeps the runs shown and reports through the app's error message.
- Runs that name another profile are left out; a run that names none is kept.

**Open gaps**
- Without a dashboard, a run of Hermes' unified runtime (a `local-*` id) that `cron.runs` doesn't name a job for is left out of every job's history.

**Checked:** 2026-11-03, #1712 (added, fixing #1707).

## Links in messages

A tap on a link in a reply opens it, the first time, wherever the reply is
drawn until a touch mounts its text view.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats and Bot Chat (one chat view) · group rooms ·
table cells with a link, and every cell once selection is on (see Tables in messages) · VoiceOver and Switch Control (text view always mounted) · Voice Control and Full
Keyboard Access (the text view mounts and lays out when they ask for the
reply's elements) · long-press Open Link · file paths, linked to the Folder
(Workspace files) · a reply's `conduit://session/` links to its workstreams,
drawn as work cards under it, and the workstream refs a Bot Chat reply names in its words, linked in place (Bot workstreams, #1677)

**Code**
- Drawn until touched, mounted on touch: `Conduit/Views/Components/SelectableTextView.swift` (drawsUntilTouched, SelectableTextViewHostView.hitTest and accessibilityElements, mountTextViewForTouch)
- File paths and Markdown links to files: `Conduit/Views/Components/SelectableTextView.swift` (bridge), `Conduit/Services/WorkspaceFiles.swift` (WorkspacePathLinks, url(forLink:)), `Conduit/Services/ConduitAppLink.swift` (file), `Conduit/Services/AppState+Workspace.swift` (absoluteWorkspacePath, revealWorkspaceFile)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/DrawnTextLinkTapTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/WorkspaceFilesTests.swift` (testMarkdownLinksToHostFilesOpenInTheFolder, testAReplysMarkdownFileLinkIsDrawnAsAFolderLink)
- Surfaces that draw until touched: `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift`, `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (selectableTextDrawsUntilTouched); work links as cards, `Conduit/Services/BotWorkstreams.swift` (BotWorkLinks) and `Conduit/Views/BotWorkViews.swift` (BotWorkLinkCard); named refs linked in place, `BotWorkLinks.linkingNamedRefs` and `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (`BotChatWorkReply`, `AssistantBubble.shownContent`); table cells with a link, `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (MarkdownTableRowView.cellDrawsAsText)

**Rulings**
- The touch that mounts a reply's text view is routed to it laid out, so it finds the link under the finger; a link never needs a second tap (2026-10-26, #1303, carried in #1311).
- A file path in a reply is a `conduit://file` link, drawn as a link, that opens the Folder at that file; only inside the app (2026-10-27, #1399).
- A Markdown link whose destination is a file on the Hermes host (a report linked as clients/acme/report.xlsx, an absolute path, one from the home folder, `./` or a drive, or a `file:///` URL; a relative one needs a known file type and a first segment that isn't a web host) opens the Folder at that file like a path the reply names, never the system, which looked for the file on the phone or Mac and reported it missing; web, mail and other schemes, anchors and `file://` on another machine stay as written (2026-11-05, #1814, issue 1809).
- A reply's "[Open W3](conduit://session/…)" link to a workstream leaves its words and becomes a work card under it, a button (one tap, VoiceOver and Switch Control as any button, so no long-press Open Link); the rest of the reply stays as written (2026-11-01, #1637, Eric's Gridania test). Hermes Desktop's `@session:` reference to the same session the plugin puts right after it (Desktop's chip for the workstream) goes with it; any other reference stays (2026-11-03, #1710, notifier #526).
- A workstream ref a Bot Chat reply names in its words ("W50 found …") becomes a link to that workstream's chat in place, once the bot's work list has it; never inside code, a link (its text or address), a URL, a path or a file name. Only the drawn text changes: Copy and Read Aloud keep the reply's own words (Eric 2026-11-03: the coordinator should link its work; #1677).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1819 (a tapped bare file name finds the chat's own file, see Workspace files); 2026-11-05, #1814 (a Markdown link to a host file opens the Folder, issue 1809; chats, Bot Chats, group rooms and table cells all draw through the bridge, so all get it; long-press Open Link opens the same Folder link); 2026-11-03, #1710 (a work link's Desktop reference goes with it into the card); 2026-11-03, #1701 (`bot-workstreams` merged into main for TestFlight, as its PRs left this entry); 2026-11-03, #1677 (on `bot-workstreams`: the workstream refs a Bot Chat reply names linked in place); 2026-11-01, #1637 (a reply's links to its workstreams drawn as work cards); 2026-10-31, #1596 (table cells with a link are always on the drawn-until-touched path); 2026-10-30, #1535 (table cells join the drawn-until-touched path once selection is on); 2026-10-29, #1491 (a room's pictures open in the picture viewer); 2026-10-27, #1399 (file paths); #1311 (carries #1303; Voice Control and Full Keyboard Access in Siblings).

## Markdown lists in messages

How a reply's lists read: numbering, loose lists, and the same list in every
view that draws Markdown.

**Siblings:** chat bubbles (block views and prose runs) · very long replies
(chunked) · selection and Copy · group rooms · tool results · call job cards ·
Read Aloud and live voice read-back · chat list previews and quotes

**Code**
- Parser and block views: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (MarkdownParser, MarkdownList, MarkdownSelectionFormatter)
- Prose runs: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownProseRun.swift`
- Long replies: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownLargeDocument.swift` (splitListItems; LargeStreamPromotion while streaming), `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownLargeDocumentView.swift`, `Conduit/Views/Components/StreamingText.swift` (largeStableChunks)
- Selection: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownSelectionCoordinator.swift`
- Copy response (copies the source): `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (copyResponse)
- Other surfaces drawing MarkdownText: `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift`, `Conduit/Views/ToolResultViews.swift`, `Conduit/Views/LiveVoiceCallJobs.swift`
- Spoken text (source lines, not parsed blocks): `Conduit/Voice/VoiceReadBack.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/SpokenTextFilter.swift`
- Previews and quotes: `Conduit/Services/PreviewText.swift`, `Conduit/Views/Components/ChatQuote.swift`

**Rulings**
- Ordered lists number as CommonMark and Hermes Desktop do: blank lines between items keep one list (2026-10-23, #1168), and a list starts at its first item's number, so steps split by a code block carry on; a marker is one to nine ASCII digits, anything else is text (2026-10-23, #1175, Eric).
- Every view that draws a list reads the parsed block, so a numbering change is a parser change plus each renderer's marker; long replies bake ordinals into continuation chunks (#1168).
- An item that is a Hermes Desktop card, or a preview where previews draw (`holdsDirective`), ends the list: the block draws on its own, and the items after it start a new list from the number written on the first of them (2026-10-30, #1524, see Cards made for Hermes Desktop). An item that is only the plugin's hidden `::conduit-board` line ends it the same way, with nothing drawn between, so the next items carry on from their written number (2026-11-04, #1751).

**Open gaps**
- Nested lists are flattened: an indented sub-list draws as its own list at the left edge.
- Read Aloud and live read-back speak the numbers as written, so "1. 1. 1." is spoken 1, 1, 1 while the screen draws 1, 2, 3.
- Copy response under a reply copies the Markdown source, so "1. 1. 1." copies as written while the screen draws 1, 2, 3; selection Copy matches the screen where the list is selectable text (prose runs, one text view).
- A list drawn as a block view (outside a prose run, e.g. under VoiceOver or next to a task list) keeps its number outside the selectable text, so selection Copy leaves the number out.
- A reply that grows past 16 KB (two chunks) while streaming is parsed per promoted slice, so a list cut at a slice boundary carries on from the number written on the slice's first item (right when numbered 1, 2, 3; restarts for "1. 1. 1."). It was the large-document size (100 KB) until issue 1720: a 50 KB reply paid 45 to 160 ms a tick, up to 30 ticks a second. The settled reply still parses whole below 100 KB, and a streaming reply's slices draw diagrams and formulas in place below it too (2026-11-04, #1734).
- A marker past two digits ("100.") can crowd its column in the block view.
- A single list item too big for one long-reply chunk is split into paragraphs that each repeat its number.
- A long reply's continuation chunks draw list items as paragraphs with the number baked in, so they lose the list's styled marker column.

**Checked:** 2026-11-04, #1751 (an item that is only the hidden board line ends a list, as a card does); 2026-11-04, #1734 (a streaming reply is promoted into slices from 16 KB rather than the large-document size, issue 1720; the settled reply unchanged); 2026-10-30, #1524 (a Desktop card ends a list; previews and quotes name it); 2026-10-28, #1449 (speech leaves Hermes' file tags out, see Files Hermes attaches); 2026-10-28, #1430 (speech no longer takes a `* ` item marker for the start of a narrated action); 2026-10-23, at #1175.

## Tables in messages

How a reply's Markdown table is drawn, selected and copied, in every view
that draws Markdown.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats and Bot Chat (one chat view: plain cells)
· group rooms and other Markdown surfaces (selectable cells from the start) ·
very long replies and big tables (paged) · the long-press menu (Copy Table,
Select Text), the pointer's Copy Table button, and VoiceOver's actions for them (Copy Table on every surface) · a pointer on a Mac or an
iPad · selection across the reply · Copy response · links in cells (a cell with a link is always a selectable cell and opens it as Links in messages does)

**Code**
- Tables, cells and the menu: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (MarkdownTable, MarkdownTableRowView, MarkdownPlainCell, MarkdownTableMenu, LargeMarkdownTable; MarkdownTableLayout for column widths and Copy Table's text)
- Plain cells in the chat: `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (markdownTablePlainCells)
- Long replies: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownLargeDocumentView.swift`, `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownRichContent.swift` (isComplexTable); while streaming, `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownLargeDocument.swift` (MarkdownStableBoundaryScanner.noteTableRow), tests `ConduitTests/MarkdownLargeDocumentTests.swift` (testALongStreamingTableIsNeverCutInside, testATableWithoutOuterPipesIsOneSpan, testPipesOutsideATableOpenNoSpan, testATableOpenAtTheEndClosesOnFinish)
- Selection: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownSelectionCoordinator.swift` (deferRegistration, which mounts a waiting table when a selection begins; tableMountKey); test `ConduitTests/MarkdownSelectionCoordinatorTests.swift` (testTableMountAndItsFirstCellsMountBothWait)
- Selectable cells, drawn until touched in the chat: `Conduit/Views/Components/SelectableTextView.swift`
- Which cells draw as text: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (MarkdownTableRowView.cellDrawsAsText)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/MarkdownTableLayoutTests.swift` (plain cells, link cells), `ConduitTests/MarkdownLargeDocumentTests.swift` (testLargeChatTableDrawsOnlyLinkCellsAsText), `ConduitUITests/SelectionObserverUITests.swift` (testTapOnLinkInChatTableCellOpensIt, on `Conduit/Views/SelectionFixtureView.swift`'s chat table)

**Rulings**
- The chat draws table cells without a link as plain text, the cheapest to build as rows scroll in (#693). A long press offers Copy Table and Select Text; Select Text draws the cells as selectable text until the row is taken down.
- Selection on a table turns on as it does for the reply's drawn text: a selection that starts elsewhere in the message mounts the cells, so a drag from the text above or below carries into the table, and a pointer over the table (a Mac, an iPad's trackpad or mouse) turns it on, so a click and drag selects in a cell and Cmd+C and the context menu's Copy work (2026-10-30, issue 1531, #1535; Eric: most selections start in the text around the table).
- A pointer over a table (a Mac, an iPad's trackpad or mouse) shows a Copy Table button at the table's top right, on every Markdown surface, since the cells' own right-click menu replaces the table's (2026-10-30, Eric, #1540).
- Column widths come from each cell's own measured width, kept by its text, size and references, so a table streaming in measures only its new cells, and a width change measures none again (2026-11-04, #1743: every publish measured every cell, the top Conduit cost of a streaming table under Time Profiler).
- A streaming reply past 16 KB is drawn in slices with a live tail (see Markdown lists in messages), and a table is one span to the slicer, as a code block is: a slice ends before or after it, never between its rows, so the rows streaming in keep their header. The span starts at the header once the separator row under it confirms the table, as the parser reads one, and runs over every line with a `|`, so a table without outer pipes counts too; prose with a `|` and a fence opener with one in its info string open none (2026-11-04, #1734, from the reviews). A table that grows past the large-document size before it ends draws through the long-reply presentation, as an unclosed code block does.
- VoiceOver's Copy Table is on every table, whether or not selection is on, group rooms' included: a VoiceOver user selecting cell by cell has no other way to take the whole table (#1535).
- A cell with a link is never plain text: it draws as a selectable cell (drawn until touched in the chat), so a click or tap opens the link as the reply's other links do. A plain cell's SwiftUI link lost the click to the row's tap that puts the keyboard away (2026-10-31, Eric asked for issue 1585 to be fixed, #1596; #693's plain cells kept for every cell without a link). The table's own deferred mount waits under a key of its own (`tableMountKey`), so a first cell with a link, which waits under its segment, doesn't replace it (#1596).

**Open gaps**
- On a touch screen, once selection is on (Select Text, or a selection elsewhere in the message), the long-press menu is the text's own, so Copy Table is gone for that table until its row is taken down; selecting across the table copies its cells, and Copy response copies the reply.
- No Copy cell or Copy row (asked for as optional in issue 1531).
- On a touch screen, a long press on a cell with a link is the text's own menu (the link's, or selection), so Copy Table and Select Text are reached from the table's other cells; on a table whose every cell has a link, only through VoiceOver's actions or Copy response (#1596).
- A cell with a link costs a drawn text host as its row scrolls in, which plain cells don't; a table of mostly links pays it on most cells (#1596, not measured).
- The pointer's Copy Table button covers the corner of the last header cell while the pointer is over the table.
- A big table mounts its rows in batches (`LargeMarkdownTable`), and a selection copies only mounted cells, so a selection across a table past its first batch leaves the rest out until Show more; Copy Table copies every row.

**Checked:** 2026-11-04, #1743 (each cell's width is measured once); 2026-11-04, #1734 (a streaming table is never sliced between its rows, now that slicing starts at 16 KB; the other surfaces don't stream in slices); 2026-11-01, #1621 (the UI test finds a link cell as a Link or a TextView: a cell that's all link reads as a Link to accessibility); 2026-10-31, #1596 (a cell with a link draws as a selectable cell, so its link opens; Links in messages' Siblings); 2026-10-30, #1540 (the pointer's Copy Table button); #1535 (a selection in the message mounts the cells; VoiceOver's Copy Table kept).

## Attaching files

Photos, camera shots and any other file go into the composer as
attachments, staged on the device and sent with the next message.

**Siblings:** chat composer (chats, project chats, Bot Chat) · the full
editor · group rooms · the composer's text field (pasted pictures, long
pasted text, files dropped on it) · iPad and Mac (the same fields; Cmd-V
and Paste and Match Style) · the sent message and a room message (a paste
reads "Pasted text") · Hermes Desktop (the same threshold and file name) ·
README.md's feature list

| Way in | Chat composer and its full editor | Group room and its full editor |
|---|---|---|
| Attach › Camera, Photo Library, Document | yes | yes, with a plugin that stores room files |
| A picture pasted in the field | yes, one picture | no |
| Text pasted in the field, over 3,000 characters | yes, as a text attachment | yes, with a plugin that stores room files |
| Files dragged onto the chat, the room, the field or the full editor | yes | yes, with a plugin that stores room files |

**Code**
- Staging and its limits: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerAttachments.swift` (AttachmentSizeLimit, AttachmentTypePolicy, AttachmentStaging's stageCopy and finishStaging)
- Dropped files: `Conduit/Views/Components/AttachmentDrop.swift` (AttachmentDrop and its take, stage and stageImageObject, attachmentDropTarget and its outline, attachmentDragEnded), `Conduit/Views/Components/ReturnKeyTextView.swift` (fieldDrop, takeDrop, FieldDropHandler: every composer field's only drop interaction, and dragEnded), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerPasteTextView.swift` (takesDroppedFiles, takeDroppedFiles), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` and `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (the drop targets), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (dropIntoComposer, dropIntoRoomComposer), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerFullEditor.swift` (onDropFiles)
- Chat composer: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (attachmentButton, handleDocumentSelection, handleDroppedFiles, handlePastedImage, attachLongPaste, pastedTextActions), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerPasteTextView.swift` (paste(itemProviders:), onDroppedFiles)
- Long pastes: `Conduit/Views/Components/PastedTextAttachment.swift` (PastedText: threshold, name, staging; PastedTextSheet), `Conduit/Views/Components/ReturnKeyTextView.swift` (onLongTextPaste, paste and pasteAndMatchStyle, for every composer field), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerAttachments.swift` (ComposerAttachmentChip, AttachmentTypePolicy.displayName), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (UserDocumentAttachmentChip), `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (GroupMessageFiles)
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift` (attachButton, importDocuments, importDroppedFiles, finishImport, attachLongPaste, pastedTextActions)
- A picture as an image object, and its PNG (paste and drop): `Shared/ShareDraft/ProviderPicture.swift` (loadImage, pngData)
- Sending a staged picture, for either server: `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (attachImage, detachImage, authorityStagedImages, sendPrompt's `attachments`)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ComposerAttachmentPolicyTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/PastedTextAttachmentTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/ComposerPasteTextViewTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- Every way in stages the same way: copied into the staging folder, size checked against the device's limit before it is read, images providers can't read re-encoded as JPEG, and anything left out named in the composer's notice. Nothing is sent until the user presses Send (2026-10-28, #1411).
- A drop attaches files and leaves the rest: words dragged from another app go into the draft only when dropped on the field, and a link stays a link. Text counts as a file only when it comes as a named file. One picture dropped or pasted on the field keeps the picture paste; several items, or any other file, are staged like picked documents (2026-10-28, #1411, from #1408).
- A locked chat composer takes no drop, as its Attach menu is off then; a room on a plugin that can't store its files says what fixes it, as its Attach menu does (2026-10-28, #1411).
- A composer field's only drop interaction is its own; UIKit's text drop is kept off every field, since it took a picture dropped from Finder and never finished it, so nothing attached and the drag hung (issue 1689). The chat composer's field stages files itself (a lone picture keeps the picture paste), and takes none while the composer is locked; a room's field and the full editor turn files down, so the room or the editor around them attaches them. Words and links go into the draft where they're dropped, and words dragged within a field move there, as before; a link a browser offers with its page as text is still a link, while a picture dragged from a page (which carries its address too) is a file. A drop of files and words together on a room's field or the full editor goes to the room or editor, which attaches the files and leaves the words out, as a drop elsewhere on it does (2026-11-03, #1695).
- The chat's or room's "Drop to attach" outline goes away when the drag does, wherever it ends: dropped on the chat, on the composer's field, or elsewhere, or called off. SwiftUI raises and lowers it as the drag comes, goes or is called off over the chat; the target's own drop and the field, when a drag that reached it ends, lower it too, since a drag that ends on the field never tells the chat it left (issue 1689, build 250, 2026-11-04, #1766) The field's end clears every target's outline, not only its own drag's: with two drags at once on an iPad, one ending on a field takes down the other's outline early, though a drop there still attaches. Accepted as cosmetic rather than tracking each drag's session, which SwiftUI's drop doesn't expose (2026-11-04, #1766 review).
- A dropped picture whose file can't be read is taken as the image object it also offers and staged as PNG (its name's own extension dropped), then finished like any staged file, the size limit included; it is the one drop decoded before its size is checked, a picture-sized read. A dropped picture's PNG is checked against the limit before it is written. A pasted or dropped picture with no bitmap of its own (`pngData()` nil) is drawn once and that is written, up to 64 million pixels. As the share sheet does (see Sharing into Conduit; 2026-11-05, #1821, issue 1747).
- A dropped folder is taken but not attached: the composer's notice names it and says to drop the files inside. Files dropped with it still attach (2026-10-28, #1422).
- Text pasted in a composer field (inline or full editor, chat or room) over 3,000 characters, Hermes Desktop's threshold, goes in as a removable text attachment instead of into the field: a `.txt` named as Desktop names a paste (`pasted_content_<time>_<hex>.txt`), staged and sent like any file, so Hermes puts its text in the prompt through the `@file:` reference and a reopened chat, here or in Desktop, shows it as pasted text. Pasted over a selection, it still replaces the selection. Its chip shows the first words; a tap shows the whole paste to read or edit, and Paste as text puts it back in the field after what was typed, and clearing its text removes it, as × does. The file is written off the main actor; if it can't be written, the words go into the field after all. Only the Paste command (`paste(_:)`: Cmd-V, the edit menu, the keyboard's Paste) attaches it; words that come through the item-provider route, dropped or from a keyboard action, stay words, so the clipboard is read only when the user pastes. A shorter paste, a picture, or a paste where the composer can't take files (locked, a chat still on its way, whose waiting message is words only, or a room on a plugin that can't store files) goes into the field as before, and so does one too big for the attachment limit, which can't go as a file. Dropped words stay words, as above. The message also sends the paste's first 1,000 characters as `title_preview`, as Desktop does, so a chat that opens with a paste gets a title from its words, not its file name; a Hermes that refuses the key gets the message without it (Eric asked for it, 2026-10-29, #1515).
- A picture is staged with `image.attach_bytes` on either server. The dashboard holds it for the chat's next message; the gateway's own listener only stages it, so Conduit names it in that message's `attachments` (path and type) and taking it back before the send just drops it from that list (2026-11-02, #1631, checked against a real listener: a staged picture the message doesn't name never reaches the model). A send that fails takes back every picture it staged, on either server, so none rides on the chat's next message (2026-11-02, #1631).
- A paste is an attachment like any other: while Hermes replies it goes as Queue (#1154), `/new` in a Bot Chat refuses it, Edit and resend is off for its message, and the draft keeps it. Paste as text turns it back into words to Steer with (2026-10-29, #1515).

**Open gaps**
- A dropped folder's files aren't attached for the user; they drop the files themselves.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1821 (a dropped picture whose file fails is taken as its image object; pictures without a bitmap are drawn before they're written); 2026-11-04, #1766 (the "Drop to attach" outline clears when a drag ends on the field); 2026-11-03, #1695 (a file dropped on a composer field attaches instead of hanging the drop, issue 1689); 2026-11-02, #1631 (pictures reach the reply on the gateway's own listener; see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-29, #1515 (long pastes become text attachments); 2026-10-28, #1422 (folder drops say why they aren't attached).

## A chat while it opens

A chat that's opened again shows what it had at once, while Hermes sends
the rest, instead of a blank chat.

**Siblings:** chats and project chats · Bot Chat · group rooms · a cold
launch and a chat picked in the saved Chats list (the same read-only copy) ·
a profile switch (the chat the new profile opens on), whether from the strip,
the picker, CarPlay, or a chat opened in another profile from All chats, a
notification, a link, a widget or a Shortcut · iPad and Mac windows (the same chat view) · Settings' Data handling caption ·
the notifier's history page route (`POST /sessions/history-page`, its README section and changelog) ·
Load earlier (what it brought in is kept in memory when the chat is left and grafted back when it opens again; a chat past 1,000 rows lets go of its oldest pages and Load earlier reads them again; its pages need no saved rows, since they read past the newest page) ·
voice's reads of a chat (the last reply read back, a voice row's history): their newest page goes through the history page too ·
what the saved rows draw, the chat's own rows (each with its entry): message row actions, bot mentions and teammate messages, steps in a turn, pictures in messages and the picture viewer, cards drawn in web pages, self-improvement updates, and bars lists scroll under ·
docs/PLAN_CARD.md (not needed: the plan card still doesn't show while saved rows stand in, as it says) ·
Watch and CarPlay (not needed: neither shows a transcript)

| Opening | Shows while it loads | Kept |
|---|---|---|
| A chat or project chat | its saved copy (the rows it had loaded when it was left, up to 500), drawn as its own rows until Hermes' replace them in place | on the phone, the last 100 chats left per dashboard and profile while their files fit 64 MB (the newest always stays); in memory, the last 16 read, saved or read ahead while their files fit 32 MB, and each dashboard and profile's saved Chats list and list of its copies once read or saved, with no budget, until a sign-out, a removed dashboard or Delete saved chats. Once the live list is in, the copies of the 6 chats opened last in the profile are read ahead, and for a switch each other profile's saved list and last chat, into room memory has free |
| A Bot Chat | the copy kept when it was left (after a `/new`, the compacted chat as it showed), drawn the same way | in memory, per dashboard and bot, one per bot, up to 500 rows, eight bots' at most with the least recently kept dropped first (#1837, issue 1831) (its newest page's raw rows, for the history page, are kept on the phone under the bot's profile like any chat's, until the bot is deleted or they're pruned) |
| A group room | the events it had | in memory, per dashboard and room, up to 400 events, until the room leaves the list |
| A chat never opened | nothing, as before | not applicable |

**Code**
- Chats: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (performSessionOpenNotingRefusal and its landing from saved rows, savedRowsEndMidTurn, presentSavedCopyWhileOpening, which reads a copy not in memory through readTranscript, warmSavedCopy from `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ChatsView.swift`'s and `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ProjectPage.swift`'s rows, recordOfflineChatCopy; presentRestoredChatAfterProfileChange and its rollback in switchProfile; prefetchSavedChats from savedChatListReplacedByLiveList; makeDefaultOfflineChatCache; holdBackgroundTaskUntilCacheWritesLand), `Conduit/Services/OfflineChatCache.swift` (loadTranscript, readTranscript, keptTranscripts, warmTranscript, keptRows; writesAsynchronously: record, recordChatList and recordHeldRows on the store's queue, the removals' performAndWait, keptIndexes and keptChatLists; unchangedEntry; prefetch; OfflineCachedMessage.rowId)
- The saved rows drawn as the chat's: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (chatRowsOnScreen, savedCopyScrollSessionKey, chatOnScreenIsBusy, chatImageGallery), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (the scroller fed chatRowsOnScreen, and told when saved rows Hermes' matched leave; drawnScrollSessionKey, and drawnOrFallbackScrollSessionKey, which names the conversation the rows' kept heights go by (drawnConversation); transcriptTopBar, savedCopyStatus, quotedReplyJump, transcriptBackfillAvailable), `Conduit/Views/TranscriptModel.swift` (rows, in order: Load earlier, the saved copy's status or an empty chat's welcome, the chat's rows, the live turn's and a send waiting; the status and the welcome follow the rows drawn, never while the chat's rows are on their way to the scroller, as on a new view's first pass), `Conduit/Views/OfflineChatBanner.swift`, `Conduit/Views/ChatRowState.swift` (ChatRowFacts, from the rows drawn, which TranscriptModel works out; isOffline keeps Hermes' actions off), `Conduit/Services/TranscriptScroller.swift` (transcriptChanged's isProvisional; replyStartLandingRequested's transition, which the open's own switch keeps; see Following the latest message), `Conduit/Services/AppState+PendingSend.swift` (a message waiting under saved rows is scrolled to)
- The newest page's rows, read without the ones the phone holds: `Conduit/Services/HistoryPage.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (historyPagePayload, from fetchPersistedHistoryPayload and voiceHistoryPage, which latestSavedThreadReply and voiceRowMessages read through), `Conduit/Services/DashboardTicketBridge.swift` (requestJSON's readsOnly: the read fails with the page on a sign-out, as a GET does; receive parses its answer, as every request's, off the main thread when it's over 64 KB, as a long chat's page is, and where it arrives when smaller, then hands it to answer on the main actor), `Conduit/Services/OfflineChatCache.swift` (heldRowsFileURL, loadHeldRows, writeHeldRows through recordHeldRows, removeHeldRows from deleteBot; boundedTranscripts for the copies' budget); notifier: `notifier/dashboard/api/history.py`
- The open's last reads: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (scheduleChatResumeContextRefresh beside schedulePendingApprovalsRefresh in reconcile, refreshContextUsage; ChatResumeLifecycleOperations.afterResumeApplied, the tests' window between the transcript applied and the settle)
- A chat opened again: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (requestOpenSession and openChatIsSettled, the open chat's tap; LeftBackfilledTranscript, keepLeftBackfilledTranscript from performSessionOpenNotingRefusal, createNewSession and switchProfile, takeLeftBackfilledTranscript in reconcile's graft, forgetLeftBackfilledTranscripts; trimLoadedHistoryIfLong and loadedHistoryRowLimit, and loadEarlierMessages, which notes loadedPageStarts; the reconcile's window and applyPersistedForegroundAdvancement, which carry them), `Conduit/Services/PersistedTranscriptWindow.swift` (grafting, trimmingLoadedHistory, PersistedTranscriptWindowState.loadedPageStarts and pageStartsCarried; foldedPageStart and movingPageStarts, which move a page start off a tool result a page boundary fold took into its call card), `Conduit/Services/TranscriptScroller.swift` (setMode's reachedLatest, the reader back at the newest row, and browsingOlderRows, which sets AppState's chatReaderIsUpInOlderRows), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (ChatScrollEventRouter, which hands reachedLatest to trimLoadedHistoryIfLong; onAppear, where a new chat view's scroller sets chatReaderIsUpInOlderRows), `Conduit/Services/SessionPresentationCache.swift` (merge's CachedPoolIndex and bestMatch; bestMatchByScanning, the scan it replaced, kept for its test)
- Bot Chat: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (keepBotChatCopy, botChatCopyOwner, noteBotChatOpen, outgoingBotChatCopyOwner and where it's cleared: flushPendingPresentationCache, performSessionOpenNotingRefusal, switchDashboard, createNewSession; presentKeptBotChatCopy, keptBotChatCopies)
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (openGroupRoom, parkActiveRoomSend, keptRoomReplays; chatSyncErrorMessage, chatErrorBehindRoom and closeRoomSurfaceBackToChat for the chat's error under a room)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/OfflineChatCacheTests.swift` (testACopyNotInMemoryIsReadOffTheMainThread, testACopyReadOffTheMainThreadShowsWhileTheChatOpens), `ConduitTests/CompactResumeTranscriptTests.swift` (testAChatOpenedAgainKeepsTheRowsLoadEarlierBroughtIn, testTappingTheOpenChatAgainDoesNotOpenItAgain, testALongChatLetsGoOfItsOldestPagesAndLoadEarlierBringsThemBack, testAChatBackMidTurnLeavesItsKeptRowsForTheNextOpen, testALongChatLeftWhileReadingOlderRowsKeepsThemUntilBackAtTheNewestRow, testToolCallSplitAcrossPageBoundaryReconstructsOneRun's page starts), `ConduitTests/AppStateForegroundLifecycleTests.swift` (testAForegroundAdvanceKeepsTheLoadedPageStartsForALongChat), `ConduitTests/TranscriptScrollerTests.swift` (testScrollingBackDownToTheLatestRowSaysSo), `ConduitTests/SessionPresentationCacheTests.swift` (testTheIndexedMatcherPicksWhatTheFullScanDid), `ConduitTests/AppStateChatResumeTests.swift` (testAnOpenDoesNotWaitForTheContextRead), `ConduitTests/ChatScrollStateTests+TranscriptModel.swift` (the rows drawn, the saved copy's status and the welcome), `ConduitTests/TranscriptScrollerTests.swift` (testHermesRowsAfterSavedOnesDoNotArmTheHold, testASwitchKeepsTheLandingItsOwnOpenAskedFor, testASwitchDropsALandingAnEarlierOpenAskedFor), `ConduitTests/HistoryPageTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/GroupChatSessionSafetyTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/CrossProfilePresentationCacheTests.swift` (testTheOutgoingTranscriptLeavesWhenTheProfileChangesOver), `ConduitTests/AppStateChatResumeTests.swift` (testAChatSyncErrorWaitsBehindAnOpenRoom), `ConduitTests/AnimatedAvatarTests.swift` (testKeptBotChatCopiesDropTheLeastRecentlyKeptPastTheirCount); notifier: `notifier/tests/test_history_page.py`, `notifier/upstream/test_history_page.py`

**Rulings**
- A chat that opens with saved rows (opened again, a Bot Chat's kept copy, the chat a launch or a profile switch opens on, a chat picked in the saved list) shows them as its own: the chat's scroll view draws them, provisional until Hermes answers, and Hermes' rows replace them by id in the same update, so the rows still there stay where they are and nothing is laid out again. They never enter the live transcript, so approvals, paging, resume and sends never read them, and while they stand in nothing that needs Hermes' word acts on them (Edit and resend, Retry, Branch, reactions, pins, Read aloud, Explain, a "Replying to" jump, Load earlier). The offline banner shows only while Hermes can't be reached. An unread chat whose saved rows end mid-turn lands at that turn's reply start from them, since Hermes' rows start there too (2026-10-30, #1550, from issue #1533: Eric replaced #1404's ruling, under which the copy was an overlay the live transcript replaced wholesale, with this).
- Copies are kept per dashboard and profile (Bot Chat: per bot), so another profile's history never shows (2026-10-27, #1404).
- A profile switch takes the outgoing profile's transcript, and any reply still streaming into it, off the screen as the profile changes over: the chat the new profile opens on shows its saved copy (a Bot Chat, its kept copy), or nothing, until Hermes sends it, and a chat opened in that profile replaces it as it opens. It used to stay up under the new chat's title for the whole switch, several seconds on a real dashboard. A switch that fails puts the outgoing chat and its transcript back as they were, over a chat opened during the switch (the transcript never onto another dashboard), until the reconnect resolves it (2026-10-28, #1447, Eric asked for it, from issue #1442).
- A group room on screen shows only its own errors. The chat under it can still sync (a return to the app), and its error used to land in the room's banner, read as the room failing (issue #1459). A chat sync's error raised while a room is on screen waits and shows when the room closes back to that chat (closed, or gone: disbanded or not found); opening another chat or a new one, switching profile, a reconnect or the chat resuming meanwhile drops it (2026-10-28, #1461, from issue #1459, which Eric asked to fix).
- A chat's newest page is read through the notifier's history page route when the plugin lists `history-page` (plugin 0.121+): the plugin reads Hermes' own `/messages` page and sends each row the phone kept from the last read as its fingerprint, and Conduit puts those rows back in place, so the page it reads is Hermes' answer row for row; an edit, an /undo or a compaction changes a row's fingerprint and that row comes in full. The kept rows are Hermes' raw rows, never the saved copy, which stays presentation only; they're kept for the last 100 chats read per dashboard and profile within 32 MB, beside the copies' 64 MB, and kept only when nothing was removed from the saved chats during the read (a sign-out, a removed dashboard, Delete saved chats, a deleted chat, a deleted bot, whose held rows go with it) and the same sign-in still holds. A host that can't serve the route for a profile (405, 501) isn't asked again that run. A refusal from the route (an older Hermes, a profile that turned the plugin off) or a fingerprint the phone no longer holds reads Hermes' route instead; the link's own trouble fails the read as Hermes' route would. Every open still reads the page: issue #1525's skip-the-read on a matching chat-list stamp was left out, since the list can be older than the chat on a dropping link (2026-10-30, #1536 and notifier #477, from issue #1525, Eric approved).
- Saving for a chat never runs on a tap: the app's store writes copies, held rows and the saved Chats list on its own queue and answers from memory meanwhile (a list as soon as it's given, a copy or an index once written), and a copy left again unchanged within 5 minutes isn't written again. A removal (a deleted chat, a deleted bot's held rows, Delete saved chats, a sign-out, a removed dashboard) waits for the saves queued before it, so it still takes them and the held rows' check before their write still holds. Once the live list is in, what a tap shows next is read ahead into memory (2026-10-30, #1545, Eric asked for loads to move to the background and every screen to show its last saved state at once, from issue #1533).
- A Bot Chat's copy is kept only for the bot owning the id the chat is open as (the registry first, then the roster and the saved last-chat reference). The chat's other ids never decide the bot: the scroll identity's aliases can name the chat it replaced, another bot's, so an ordinary chat left after a Bot Chat keeps no copy for it, and reopening one bot never shows another's chat. The owner is taken before a bot open notes its own ids, so a bot opening as the same id never takes the copy of the chat being left (2026-10-28, #1432).
- Tapping the chat already open (its id, or one its Chats row lists beside the open one), connected, with its own rows up and nothing under way (no open, reconcile, saved place being restored, room, or turn) marks it read and opens nothing: it already shows Hermes' rows as they stream in, so a second open only read them again and dropped what Load earlier had brought in. The scroll stays where it is, as a re-tap of the same chat always left it. A chat left after Load earlier brought in older rows keeps its rows and paging window in memory, the last 3 such chats per dashboard, under the ids its window's own open vouched for (never the scroll identity's aliases); the reconcile that brings it back into an empty chat (an open, a new chat and back, the chat a profile switch opens on) grafts Hermes' newest page onto them under the reconnect graft's rules, or lets the page stand alone; one that comes back mid-turn, whose rows come from the resume, or an open cancelled or overtaken before its rows land, leaves them kept for the next open. They go with the chat's saved copy: a deleted chat, a removed dashboard, a sign-out, Delete saved chats. A copy not in memory is read on the store's queue while the open goes ahead, and shows when it's in if the open still owns the chat and Hermes' rows haven't come first (2026-11-05, #1836, issues 1825 and 1826).
- A chat past 1,000 rows (twice the saved copy's 500) lets go of its oldest pages Load earlier brought in, out of sight above the reader: when the reader scrolls back down to the newest row between turns, and as the chat is left after Load earlier from its newest row between turns (what's kept in memory is cut back too; a reader left up in the older rows keeps them, so their place comes back with the chat, and the chat cuts back once they're at the newest row again). A page start on a tool result that a page boundary fold takes into its call card moves to that card, so the cut keeps the run whole. A reconcile that grafts onto the older rows, and a foreground advance, keep the page starts noted on them, each claiming no more coverage than the refreshed page (Hermes' newer side may have shrunk, by an /undo or another device), so Load earlier after a cut there first reads back over rows it holds, as after any graft, and never skips one. It goes back to the newest page start that still keeps 1,000 rows, with the paging window as it stood there, so Load earlier reads on from that page and brings the rest back from Hermes. Nothing goes while a turn runs, while saved rows stand in, or while the reader is up in the older rows; the saved copy is unchanged (Eric, 2026-11-05, picked over keeping everything or a window both ways; #1839 and #1844, issue 1828).
- An open, a refresh and a reconnect's resume settle once Hermes' transcript is applied: the context ring's breakdown read (`session.context_breakdown`) goes on beside them, as the approvals read does, and applies only while the same client has the same chat open. The resume's own snapshot sets the ring first, so the open's finish, an unread chat's landing and the viewport's transition no longer wait a round trip for it (2026-11-05, #1836, issue 1824).
- A Chats row that shows (a top-level row, an expanded child, a match found by its messages, a project page's row, and another profile's row in All, under that profile; by any id the row answers to) reads its chat's saved copy into memory on the store's queue, as the read-ahead does: only while there's room among the 16 kept, and first to go. Tapping it then shows the copy without reading and decoding its file on the main thread (2026-11-04, #1734, issue 1725). A copy saved maps only the rows it keeps, the last 500 saved ones, and the chat list it saves with it is mapped on the store's queue.

**Open gaps**
- A chat whose live transcript lands somewhere other than its newest row moves there at the handover: a restored reading place, and an unread reply when the saved rows already had one (Hermes' rows can start a newer turn below them, so that landing waits for them).
- Saved rows older than Hermes' newest page leave the screen when it lands, since the live transcript starts at that page (Load earlier brings them back): a reader who scrolled up into them is moved (#1550).
- While saved rows stand in they show no pins, and the pinned replies bar and the plan card wait for Hermes' rows: both are read from the live transcript. An open choice made on a chat picked in the saved list (a run of steps opened) closes when the chat opens, as the choices follow the live chat (#1550).
- Bot Chat copies and group room events are memory only, so they don't outlive Conduit being stopped (a Bot Chat's held raw rows do, but only stand in for rows of a later read, never show on their own).
- An error already on the chat when a room opens is cleared by the open (openGroupRoom) and doesn't come back when the room closes; only a sync error raised while the room is up waits (#1461 review). `errorMessage` holds non-chat errors too, so carrying it needs a rule for which ones are the chat's.
- Settings' Data handling caption says recent conversations, and what each screen last showed, are kept so Conduit opens straight to them while it connects (#1552). It doesn't mention a chat reopening where it was, since that keeps nothing more on the device.
- A launch reads the chat it opens on and its saved list on the main thread, as they're its first frame, and so does a chat picked in the saved list (#1404, #1536, #1545). Every other open, and the chat a profile switch opens on, reads a copy not in memory off it (#1836); such a copy then shows a moment after the tap, where a copy in memory shows with it. A row the V2 Chats list or a project page shows reads its chat's copy ahead as it appears (#1734); the V1 sidebar's rows don't.
- A chat left after Load earlier keeps its older rows only in memory, for this run: once Conduit is stopped, or past the last 3 such chats, it opens from its newest page again (#1836).
- A removal waits on the main thread for the saves queued before it (reads ahead still queued skip themselves): at most a long chat's copy being written or one being read ahead, tens of milliseconds (#1545).
- A 404 from the history page route isn't remembered, since Hermes' own "no such chat" comes through as one: a profile whose plugin is off while the dashboard still lists `history-page` reads Hermes' route after it on each open (#1536 review).
- A deleted chat's held rows go with it under the ids the delete names and their saved aliases; under an id neither names they stay until the scope's held rows are pruned (#1536 review).
- While saved rows stand in, VoiceOver reads them with no "opening" announcement; the header and composer say Conduit is connecting, as for a chat picked in the saved list (#1404, #1550).

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1844 (a page start on a tool result a page boundary fold takes in moves to its call card; a foreground advance's carry tested; Rulings, Code, Tests); 2026-11-06, #1837 (kept Bot Chat copies capped at eight, least recently kept dropped; a ninth bot's chat opens without its copy until left again); 2026-11-06, #1842 (a new chat view's scroller sets whether the reader is up in older rows; Code); 2026-11-05, #1839 (a chat past 1,000 rows lets go of its oldest loaded pages when the reader is back at the newest row or leaves; TranscriptScroller keeps their scroll rules; Code, Tests); 2026-10-31, #1566 (TranscriptScroller keeps the saved rows' scroll rules, not called yet; nothing changes; Code); 2026-10-31, #1565 (TranscriptModel decides the rows the chat draws, the saved copy's status and an empty chat's welcome among them, from the rows the engine has, and not while the chat's rows are on their way to it; nothing on screen changes; Code); 2026-10-31, #1552 (the open profile's kept settings answers are read ahead with its chats); 2026-10-30, #1550 (saved rows drawn as the chat's own and replaced in place, Eric's ruling replacing #1404's; an unread chat left mid-turn lands from its saved rows); 2026-10-30, #1547 (the saved lists and lists of copies kept in memory, in Kept; the newest page's answer parsed off the main thread when it's big, in Code);
