copies keep up to 500 rows for 100 chats within 64 MB); 2026-10-28, #1461 (a chat's sync error stays out of a room on screen); 2026-10-28, #1447 (a profile switch shows the new profile's chat, not the outgoing transcript); 2026-10-28, #1432.

## The chat Conduit opens on

Coming back to Conduit after iOS closed it in the background opens where
the reader was in a chat, as an ordinary return does; a launch the user
chose (after swiping Conduit away, or the first one) opens on Bots (Bots Home).

**Siblings:** chats and project chats (Chats) · Bot Chat (Bots) · group rooms
(open again once Hermes is connected) · the pages under the chat (a
project's page, Pulse, Artifacts) · an ordinary return, where the tab's path
is still in memory · iPhone, iPad and Mac windows (split, the chat beside the
list) · a notification, widget, link or Shortcut at launch (pushes its own
chat over it, as before) · the Bots list's kept rooms (Screens that open on
their last answer: a kept room opens as Hermes lists it, the same rule) ·
which chat it is: When returning to Conduit's
Continue or Latest (never a bot's workstream chat on its own, and never Pulse's chat, even a saved one, as no list shows them; see Bot workstreams and Pulse), and the saved copy that shows while it connects (A chat
while it opens) · the drawer shell's "Open to" (Sessions) choice · Settings'
When returning to Conduit caption · Watch and CarPlay (not needed: no chat
list to land on)

**Code**
- `Conduit/Views/V2/V2Shell.swift` (V2ReopenedConversation: record, launch; init(conversationOnLeave:reopening:) seeds the tab's path, conversationToReopen keeps the window's record, reopenRoomIfWaiting, giveUpRoomIfLeft, Launch.roomStep), `Conduit/Views/RootView.swift` (MainView's SceneStorage conversationOnLeave, conversationToReopen)
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (groupRoomsListed, published so a waiting room opens once Hermes lists its rooms; groupRoomsComplete, set by refreshGroupRooms when the list has no next page; refreshGroupChatSupport; openGroupRoom)
- "Open to": `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (chatReturnSurfaceApplies, requestPreferredReturnSurface, claimPreferredReturnSurfacePresentation), `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (ChatReturnBehaviorSettings: the picker and the caption for each shell)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/V2ReopenedConversationTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/ChatReturnSurfaceTests.swift` (testV2IgnoresASessionsPickedUnderTheDrawerShell)

**Rulings**
- V2 opens on the Chats list, not the last chat (Eric, 2026-10-15); since Bot Mode reached main it opens on Bots Home instead (Eric, 2026-11-03, #1678; see Bots Home). Either way, except after iOS ended Conduit in the background: then it opens where the chat was showing, in Chats or Bots, with the pages under it (Eric, 2026-10-31, #1597, from issue #1559). The window keeps that as SceneStorage, which iOS restores after it ended the app and drops when the user swipes it away, so iOS itself tells the two launches apart. The chat is the one Conduit resumes, under the saved copy while it connects; with no chat to resume it opens on the first tab. A page under it that's gone (a project this profile no longer lists, Pulse no longer showing) is left out.
- Only a chat on screen is kept: Tasks or Settings opened over a chat, the Chats or Bots list, or any time Conduit gives way to its sign-in screen (a sign-out, or a sign-in that has to be done again) drops the record, and so does turning V2 off. The next launch then opens on the first tab (Bots), since the reader had left the chat or must sign in first.
- The reopened chat and its pages are in the tab's path when the shell is made, never pushed during the launch's first layout (that left the app never idle).
- A group room that was showing opens again once Hermes is connected and lists its rooms, as a tap on its row would, its screen pushed as it opens; the tab shows meanwhile, with no error before Hermes lists the room. A tap that takes the reader elsewhere first (another tab or a page included), or a room Hermes' whole list no longer has (or disbanded), gives it up; a list cut into pages that doesn't reach it leaves it waiting. Conduit reads only Hermes' first page of rooms, so a room past it stays waiting until the reader goes elsewhere (Open gaps). A notification, widget or Shortcut waiting at launch gives it up too, so opening the room never cancels the chat it pushes. A launch whose list request fails or is cut short keeps it and tries again on the next connection or once Hermes lists its rooms, and the window keeps the room's record meanwhile, so a launch cut short tries again too. Once the room's screen is up it is the reader's: a failed load shows the room's own error, as a tap's would, and the record keeps the room for the next launch.
- "Open to" belongs to the drawer shell, and V2 hides it: a Sessions picked there is ignored under V2, on launch and on return. Before, it closed the chat on every return to Conduit with no setting left to change it (#1597).

**Open gaps**
- A room past Hermes' first page of `groups.list` never opens: the launch's reopen and the Bots list both read only that page. The Bots list's tap on a kept room is harsher: on a partial page it says "That chat is no longer available" (openGroupRoom doesn't check groupRoomsComplete). Reading the later pages fixes both.
- The list's scroll position and search under the reopened chat aren't kept: Back shows the list at its top.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1810 (the chat Conduit resumes on its own skips Pulse's chat too, by AppState.isUnlistedChat; see Pulse); 2026-11-04, #1759 (the chat Conduit resumes on its own skips a bot's workstream chats, as the lists do; see Bot workstreams); 2026-11-04, #1735 (the bot roster's and Group Chats' reads ask again on their own after a failure; what they open on is unchanged); 2026-11-03, #1703 (the `bot-workstreams` qualifiers go now that Bot Mode is on main); 2026-11-03, #1701 (`bot-workstreams` merged into main for TestFlight, as its PRs left this entry); 2026-11-03, #1678 (on `bot-workstreams` the app opens on Bots Home, a launch whose kept chat was in Sessions opening there; the record and the reopen are unchanged); 2026-11-01, #1605 (a room past Hermes' first page of rooms stays waiting, open gap); 2026-10-31, #1597 (added; the record dropped at sign-out and with V2 off, a waiting room's record kept until Hermes lists it, a page tap or a launch's notification, widget or Shortcut gives it up, a partial room list doesn't, a failed load on the room's screen shows its error, the caption names the resumed chat, from review).

## Screens that open on their last answer

A screen that reads Hermes draws what Hermes told it last time at once,
kept on the phone, while it asks again, and the new answer changes only
what changed.

**Siblings:** the agent settings pages: Model (Default model, Fast mode and
limits, Fallback models), Chat, Workspace, Memory & delegation (Delegate
model, Pause delegation) and Advanced · Settings > Pulse and What Pulse
remembers · Settings > Usage · Voice settings (the setup steps, the provider
sections, the API keys, Speech to text's speech server, Local's fast model
and the Voice replies model) · Models & providers' Helper models (the same
kept slots) · the models the model sheet, the bot
editor's Model page and the Voice replies, Voice jobs and Settings > Pulse
model pickers list (the `model.options` answer Usage keeps; the model sheet
asks for its chat's session) · the saved chats, whose wipes take the kept answers (Delete Saved
Chats, a sign-out, a removed dashboard; a deleted bot takes its own) ·
Settings' Data handling caption and the Delete Saved Chats confirmation ·
the Bots list: its bots, Desktop's groups, the hosted rooms and their
pictures, and the bots' faces (done) · the teammate names chats and rooms
show (done: from the kept bots until Hermes answers, so a name doesn't
change) · Capabilities' tabs: the installed skills and toolsets, the
official skills, the year's tool calls, the MCP servers and catalog, and
the plugins and plugin catalog (done) · the Kanban task composer's skill
picker, which lists the installed skills (done) · the Kanban model
override's roster (done) · the Tasks board: its
boards, the board shown and its cards, the profiles, projects and
orchestration settings (done) · the Artifacts lists: the Artifacts page, a
chat's own (its sheet or the panel beside it) and Bot Chats' (done) · the
Folder tab: a folder's listing and Recently Changed, in Artifacts and the
drawer shell's Workspace (done) · Capabilities' pages: a skill's SKILL.md,
a catalog skill's preview, a toolset's backends and keys, and where the
terminal runs (done) · the bot editor: Edit Bot's personality, model,
skills, tools and MCP servers, New Bot's Start From lists and the MCP
page's catalog and sign-ins (done) · Assistant speech on the speech server (opens on no
kept answer: the notifier's status answers with the server's key, which is
never kept, and the server's address and steps hang on it; done: a read
that fails keeps the status shown, and the section reopened on the page
opens on the one held in memory) · voice itself (not needed:
AppState's voice check reads Hermes each time, and the pages keep what they
read) · the live voice modes' status lines on Voice settings (Gemini Live,
Qwen Live, Grok Live, GPT-Live; done: each opens on what its last check
said, GPT-Live's per billing, kept as the line it showed, since the check's
answer names its sign-in under `auth`, which the store leaves out. Local
Live's is its fast model, above) · the Pulse screen (not needed: its cards are their own feed; Quiet
for today there keeps the state Pulse answers with, which Settings > Pulse
opens on) · a Pulse notification's Quiet for today (done: it keeps the state
Pulse answers with too) · Watch and CarPlay (not needed: neither shows these
screens) · the notifier (not needed: the pages read the same routes) ·
Settings > Models & providers' Providers section (done: it opens on a kept
summary of which providers are connected, with no key or preview in it) ·
README and docs (not needed: neither describes these pages' loading) · a Bot Chat's Work strip
and panel and a workstream's bar (done: they open on the bot's kept list; see
Bot workstreams)

**Rulings**
- Every screen shows its last saved state at once, and an update never redraws the whole screen (Eric, 2026-10-30, issue #1533).
- An answer is kept per dashboard, profile and route in the saved chats' store, so every wipe of the saved chats takes it, a deleted bot's go with it, and a deleted chat takes its own Artifacts list and its rows from the profile's. An answer about every profile at once (delegation's pause, and Pulse's state and memory, Pulse being one per host) is kept once per dashboard, so each profile's page opens on it. A read is kept only while its dashboard is still the one open and nothing was wiped since it was asked. The open profile's are read ahead with its chats, and the dashboard's own with them; memory holds the answers used last, at most 32 and 8 MB, and an answer over 2 MB isn't kept, on disk or in memory.
- Memory and the kept file leave out credential-shaped keys at any depth (any name ending in key or keys, token or tokens, secret or secrets, cookie or cookies, auth or authorization, one with an `auth` word, and one containing password, passwd, passphrase or credential), a pair's value when its name or key is one of those (`{"name": "Authorization", "value": …}`), and a URL's user and password or a credential-shaped name in its query (`?api_key=…`), since a config can hold a custom endpoint's key. Such a key whose value is true or false stays, being a setting about them (`redact_secrets`); so does a number under a name ending in tokens, or in a pair so named by its `name` or `key` (`max_tokens`, a usage report's token counts), and a `key` beside `is_set`, which names the variable whose presence the row reports. A schema's fields keep their names, which are config paths; what each holds is filtered. A name that only looks like a credential's comes in with Hermes' answer; none of the pages' own fields does. `/api/env` is never kept.
- A page draws its kept answer before its first frame, with its kept schema when it reads one, so no row comes or goes when Hermes answers; with nothing kept it shows its loader as before. A config Conduit saves is what the pages open on next, and a Default model save reads the catalog and the model's info again so their kept copies follow it. Pulse's state is kept from every step that answers with it (a change, a step reading older chats, Quiet for today on the Pulse screen or from a Pulse notification), so Settings > Pulse opens on the last state Pulse gave. A kept Pulse state is only drawn: one with Where you are or Walking past off doesn't stop this iPhone watching shops until Pulse's own answer says so.
- Hermes' answer changes only the fields it changed: a field changed on the page since it asked (a save still in flight included), and the one being typed in, stay as they are. A read that fails keeps what's shown.
- A save that writes several values or a whole list (Save model defaults, Save delegate defaults, Save fallbacks) waits for Hermes' answer, and the kept fallback list can't be edited until then: it may be stale and has no credentials to write back. A single setting saves at once, since its write reads Hermes' config first. On Settings > Pulse, a step that writes back what the page shows besides what was picked (report times, quiet days, the night's start and end, the note, the model, whose refusal puts the shown one back) or acts on it (Set up Pulse, Pin it, reading older chats) waits for Pulse's answer; a setting picked outright saves at once. Forgetting a kept item in What Pulse remembers doesn't wait: it's named by its id, and it leaves the kept list too.
- Voice settings open on Hermes' config and speech toolsets as last read, the config being the one the agent pages keep, and only once both toolsets are kept, so no voice reads not ready for want of one. Which keys are set comes from `/api/env`, which is never kept: a key the kept toolsets don't list as set reads Checking…, with no field, until Hermes answers (after a read that fails it says Hermes didn't say, still with no field), and a read of it that fails keeps which keys the page showed set, from Hermes' last answer held in memory (a key saved since included). Meanwhile the setup steps show the kept settings and the Hermes step says Checking…; if Hermes doesn't answer, it says to connect and the settings stay. With no settings shown it says to connect too; only a Hermes that answers without the voice routes is told to update. Speech to text's speech server opens on the notifier's status as last read, and Local's fast model on the one Assistant speech's status gave, kept without the server's key; Assistant speech's own steps wait for the host, since they hang on that key; reopened on the page, they open on its status read earlier, held in memory with its key (a new key included), while the host is asked again. A read of the speech server, Assistant speech's status or the fast model that fails keeps what's shown, the setup steps included, and says why; their fields wait until the page's next check (Check again included) gets an answer, and Assistant speech's section, showing why its read failed, reads again then too. A new key that fails keeps the one shown. A speech toolset or schema read that fails while the config answers keeps the one shown, so a ready voice doesn't flip to not ready. The provider pickers, Private voice's Use, the provider fields, Show words while you speak, the speech server's address and the fast model's fields, with their Save and Remove key, wait for the answer, as the pickers always waited for a read: a kept value may be stale, and a kept address has no user or password to write back. A choice saves when it's picked, never when Hermes' answer changes it. A voice config save is what the page opens on next. The Voice replies model opens on the slot Hermes gave last, and its pickers wait for Hermes, since a save writes the whole slot; a read that fails keeps it, and the page's next check asks again; a pick written while Hermes is asked stays over that answer; an answer without the slot hides it. The Voice replies, Voice jobs and Settings > Pulse model pickers open on the models of the `model.options` answer Usage keeps, picked from once Hermes answers, and a read that fails keeps the models listed.
- The model sheet and the bot editor's Model page open on the models of that `model.options` answer too; a read that fails leaves them up with "Could not load models." and Try Again under them. Their rows can be picked once Hermes answers, as a list that didn't load is never picked from (see Model lists that fail to load). The sheet's read names its chat's session, and every reader takes only the answer's providers (Usage their quota rows), so one kept answer serves them all; each asks again when it opens (#1567).
- The Bots list opens on the bots and Desktop's groups `profiles.list` gave last time and the hosted rooms `groups.list` gave, with the host's pictures for the rooms up to 1 MB and Desktop's own group pictures up to 1 MB (the rest are left out, so pictures never cost the bots their kept copy), kept once per dashboard as Conduit read them, `profiles.list` listing the whole Hermes. They show until Hermes answers, and a read that fails keeps them up. The kept copy leaves out each bot's ui_meta, which a write sends back whole, so nothing writes a kept bot: Pin, Hide, Edit, Duplicate and Delete wait for Hermes' answer, as do New Bot and New Group Chat, whose picker lists Hermes' bots. A kept bot's row opens its Bot Chat through the lookup, its kept chat counting as the roster's last confirmation, so an empty lookup still makes none. A kept room tapped before Hermes lists the rooms asks for the list first (and whether Hermes hosts rooms, if it hasn't said), then opens as Hermes lists it; one it no longer lists, or on a Hermes that no longer hosts rooms, is no longer available and doesn't open, and a list that fails says to try again. The kept pictures are taken as the first list lands, before the plugin says it keeps pictures too, so only one whose revision moved is fetched again, and a picture set or removed here is kept with the rooms. A bot's face shows from the copy the profile pictures keep on the phone until its fetch lands, and connecting fetches it again. Chats and rooms name teammates from the same bots, and a kept bot's Bot Chat face and color, the @ list, Mention a Bot, the note to the bot and a spoken job's bot names come from them, so nothing changes when Hermes answers (#1568).
- The bot editor opens on what Hermes gave last time for the profile: Edit Bot on the bot's `profiles.describe` (its SOUL, model, skills, tools and MCP servers), New Bot on its Start From profile's lists and the MCP page on Hermes' catalog and its servers' sign-ins, each kept in that profile's answers, as Conduit read them (a server's sign-in as `sign_in`, the servers as a list, since a server's name can look like a credential's), so a deleted bot takes its own. They're read-only until Hermes answers: they may be stale (a change made in Capabilities or on Desktop since), and a save compares with Hermes' answer, never the kept one, so Add, Sign In, the switches, the SOUL and the model wait for it; the description stays the Bots list's until then, as before. A read that fails keeps them shown under its note, the MCP page's with Try Again. A servers list that fails while the catalog answers keeps nothing: the page shows Hermes' catalog with the sign-ins kept last time, where it used to show no sign-ins (from #1588's review). A write Hermes took is what they open on next, even if the read after it fails: a description, SOUL, model or capability section saved, a catalog server added (on, and installed in the catalog) and a sign-in (#1588).
- Capabilities opens each tab on the lists it showed last time on the dashboard and profile: the installed skills and toolsets (shown only once both are kept; an answer listing no toolsets, a Hermes still loading its plugins, isn't kept), the official skills, the year's calls per tool (the usage answer's `tools` alone), the MCP servers and catalog, and the plugins, the plugin catalog being kept once per dashboard, as it's the same for every profile. Each list asks Hermes again when its tab shows; a read that fails keeps it up, and Hermes' answer takes its place, redrawing only the rows that changed. A catalog's read can fail while its list's answers: a kept catalog then stays up and asks again when its tab next shows, as a kept list does. The servers and the catalog are kept as Conduit read them: a server's command arguments, which can hold a key, are left out until Hermes answers, and so are its address's path and query (`/sse/<token>`), its scheme, host and port kept, so a server's page shows its address and command once Hermes answers; how it signs in is kept as `sign_in`, which the filter doesn't take for a credential's name. A catalog entry's command and arguments are kept: they're the catalog's template, the same on every Hermes, and an install's keys go to Hermes, never into them. Kept servers are tested only once Hermes lists them, a change made on the kept list reading them again included, a connector install, an edit or a switch Hermes refused among them; a server switched on or edited is tested once Hermes takes the change, as on a live list, even if the read after it fails, since Hermes taking it says the server is there. A server's page waits for Hermes' list before its own first test too, and says the server is untested if the list's read fails. The plugins are kept as Hermes gave them, the answer the Chat and Memory pages read their choices from, so a plugin's sign-in command, under Hermes' `auth_command`, which the filter drops as it drops every name with an `auth` word, shows once Hermes answers. A switch, install, update, edit or removal Hermes took is kept over any read asked before it, one with nothing kept to change counting all the same, and a list still showing its kept copy then reads it again, since the read on its way no longer commits. It's kept for the dashboard and profile it was made on, a switch to another while it was out included, never for the one switched to: the change is made to the kept copy, not to the rows on screen, and an install or edit, whose row comes with Hermes' answer, counts as a write there; a switch Hermes refused is never kept, and a kept list reads again after one too. A plugin's install, update or removal is kept in the plugin catalog too, and a connector's install or removal in the connector catalog, its entry marked installed or not (a plugin's with no update waiting), so a removal whose read fails offers it again and an install's doesn't; the catalog shown keeps an installed entry until Hermes' answer brings its row. Offline the tabs open on their kept lists too, after a dashboard switch made offline included, and the skill and toolset switches are off until a dashboard connects. Turn All On, Turn All Off and Turn Off Unused wait for Hermes' answer, as they pick from the list shown. The Kanban task composer's skill picker lists the kept skills too (#1569).
- Capabilities' pages open on what they showed last time on the dashboard and profile: a skill's SKILL.md, a catalog skill's preview and a toolset's backends and keys, each one page's of many, kept with the chats' and folders' lists (the 100 read last), and where the terminal runs. A read that fails keeps what's shown. A backend, terminal or key change Hermes took shows on the page at once as Hermes now holds it (the backend chosen, a key set, never the key itself), a page with nothing kept included, and changes the page's kept answer the same way, so the page shows it next time even if the read after it fails; then the page reads again, as before. Offline, a page's backends and keys and a catalog skill's Install, on its row as on its page, are off, as the switches are. A plugins read cut off by leaving the tab is no failure, so the tab asks again when it next shows (#1584).
- The Tasks board opens on what it showed last time on the dashboard: the boards, the board shown and its cards as they show without archived tasks, the profiles, projects and orchestration settings, kept once per dashboard as Hermes gave them, Kanban being shared by every profile; offline too, saying to connect. Nothing on a kept board can be changed until Hermes answers: its cards are read-only, as a board's being switched away from are, and the board still scrolls. A board picked shows its own kept cards while it loads, rather than the last board's. Show archived reads Hermes, as archived tasks aren't kept. Hermes' board answer carries its clock, which nothing shows: it's left out, so a poll that brings back the same board doesn't redraw it. Only an answer Conduit can read is kept: one it can't fails like any read, leaving the last one kept. The board shows once it's pointed at the dashboard open, before the first frame and on a switch before the next, so neither an empty board nor the last dashboard's is drawn first; answers that name the dashboard only later show its kept board until Hermes lists the boards, and answers given again never put kept lists back over Hermes'. The model override (the task composer's and a task's own) opens on the roster the plugin gave last time, kept once per dashboard too (see Model lists that fail to load).
- The Artifacts lists open on what they listed last time: each store's first page of every kind, unsearched, as the list opens, kept for the dashboard and the store's profile as Hermes gave it; a filter, a search and the pages after the first read Hermes, a filter or search showing the last rows dimmed until it answers. The Artifacts page's own stores are kept with each profile's other answers. A chat's own list (a Bot Chat's included) and a folder's listing and recent files are each one of many, so each profile keeps the 100 of them read last, within 16 MB, and never reads them ahead, so they don't take the room the settings pages' answers have. A read that fails keeps the rows shown, and a bot's store that fails shows its kept rows, which don't page on. Kept rows show before the plugin says what it serves, offline too, and the list reads Hermes once it says it serves artifacts; once it says it doesn't, or isn't there, the update notice takes their place, and never before: with nothing kept the list shows its loader until then, or offline, that Conduit isn't connected. Connected with no word from the plugin, the list asks it again as it opens and on a refresh, and with nothing kept says it couldn't reach the dashboard's notifier if it still doesn't answer. A list kept or loaded empty says so at once, through a refresh too. A listed link is kept without a credential-shaped query, as every kept URL is, so offline its kept row opens the address without it until Hermes answers. The Folder tab opens a folder on the listing and Recently Changed the plugin gave last time; a folder opened in the tree, Hermes' own listing (a plugin without the workspace routes), search and a file read Hermes. A kept listing waits for the plugin's word, rather than giving way to Hermes' own listing, which has no sizes or dates: it reads again through the plugin's routes once it says it serves them, or through Hermes' own once it says it doesn't, and the update label waits until then. Only an answer the list or folder can read is kept (#1582).
- Offline, Settings > Usage shows the numbers it kept, the quota with them, under "Connect to Hermes to update these numbers." instead of clearing the page as it did since #813; a refresh that fails says so over them, and a quota that can't be read while connected still goes (Eric's ruling above, #1555). A per-model read that fails is kept as none, so the page opens on the usage route's own rows, as it showed them, never on an older split and its cost beside newer totals.

**Open gaps**
- A page whose answers weren't read ahead (another profile's, the bot editor's included, Usage's, a chat's own Artifacts list and a folder's listing and recent files, which are never read ahead, or one opened before the live list landed), and a save, forget or Capabilities change that lands after a dashboard switch, read their kept files on the main thread: a config or schema is usually tens of kilobytes, as are most chats' Artifacts and folders' listings, and a file can be up to 2 MB. A chat's Artifacts list reads one kept file per store as it opens (with All profiles, its profile's and every bot's), and a folder two (its listing and Recently Changed), so a chat with many bots or a large folder reads the most.

## Composer drafts

Unsent words, files and a quoted reply wait in the composer they were typed
in until they're sent, whichever way the user leaves.

**Siblings:** chat composer (chats, project chats, Bot Chat) · New Chat ·
a saved copy's composer and its waiting message ("Sends when connected") ·
group rooms · the full editor · the notices that say where words went ·
the composer's Sending… while a send checks Hermes

| Leaving by | Chat composer | Group room |
|---|---|---|
| Back, or another chat from the list | text, files and quote kept | text and files kept |
| A room opened over the chat | kept | not applicable |
| Leaving while a send is on its way | back in its draft if it doesn't go | held by the room's pending message |
| Sign-out or another server | dropped | dropped, files deleted |
| The room disbanded or left the list | not applicable | dropped, files deleted |
| An empty chat Hermes lost, replaced by a fresh one | kept, in the fresh chat | not applicable |

**Code**
- The replaced chat's draft: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (lostChatReplacement in composerDraftKeysAreSameChat; see An empty new chat Hermes lost)
- Chat composer: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (loadDraft, saveDraft, handoffComposer, onDisappear, draftKeyToKeep, restoreSubmittedDraftIfNeeded, applyComposerRestoreRequests, sendingNotice, composerInUse), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerUpdates.swift` (isCheckingSend), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerDraftStore.swift` (clearCount)
- A send that didn't go: `Conduit/Services/AppState+PendingSend.swift` (returnFailedComposerSubmission, restoreFailedPendingComposerSend's mayHaveGone), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (composerSubmissionStoppedQuietly, takeComposerSubmissionOfUnknownDelivery); its checks before the message shows: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (checkingBeforeSend, composerSendIsChecking: the stale-idle probe, the transcript freshness read, starting a chat from the empty canvas)
- Waiting message: `Conduit/Services/AppState+PendingSend.swift` (returnPendingComposerSendToDraft, restoreFailedPendingComposerSend, pendingComposerSendNotice), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (conversationIsGone), `Conduit/Models/PendingComposerSend.swift`
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (activeRoomDraft, activeRoomAttachments, pruneRoomStores)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ComposerDraftStoreTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/GroupChatSessionSafetyTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/OfflineChatCacheTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/AppStateChatResumeTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/AppStateForegroundLifecycleTests.swift` (the Sending… line, leaving mid-send)

**Rulings**
- Drafts live in memory per (profile, chat), and a sign-out or server switch clears them on purpose; nothing the composer held before the clear goes back in after it: not when it goes away, hands off to another chat or a room, nor when a send that was on its way fails (2026-10-24, #1185).
- A send's words leave the field when Send is tapped. If it doesn't go, they come back through AppState's restore requests, never through the composer that sent them: leaving the chat mid-send replaces that composer, and words put back into it were lost, so the user had to type them again. The composer on screen puts them in its field when they're its chat's, otherwise in their chat's stored draft. A send that stopped with no error to say so (its chat was left before its message showed) leaves the waiting message's notice: back in the composer, or back in that chat's draft, by name, and only while its dashboard and profile are on screen. One whose reply was lost after its chat was left may have reached Hermes, so its words come back without that notice, a waiting message's included. Sending… keeps the V2 composer open, as other notices do (2026-10-27, #1403, from #1401).
- Until a send's message shows in the transcript, the composer says "Sending…" in the chat it was sent from: on a slow or dropped connection the checks before it (whether Hermes is still busy, whether the transcript is current, starting the chat) can take seconds, and an emptied field with nothing else read as a message that went nowhere (2026-10-27, #1403, from #1401).
- A waiting message is never sent on its own after it's handed back. When Hermes says its chat is gone, its words go into the composer on screen, unsent, with a notice saying so (2026-10-24, #1185).
- A waiting message is words only, so a long paste while its chat is on its way stays in the field as text instead of becoming an attachment, and can wait like typed words. Once the chat is open, a long paste becomes a text attachment, which the draft keeps like any file ("Attaching files", 2026-10-29, #1515).

**Open gaps**
- Drafts don't outlive Conduit being stopped; only a waiting message does (as a file).
- A waiting message left from an earlier run whose chat is gone still goes back into that chat's draft: the gone chats are only known for this run.
- A room's quoted message and its "To" picks aren't kept when the room is left.
- A room that's disbanded while another dashboard is in use keeps its staged files until that dashboard is opened again or the user signs out.

**Checked:** 2026-11-04, #1752 (an empty chat Hermes lost hands its draft and a waiting message to the fresh chat in its place); 2026-10-30, #1527 (a handoff clears the full editor's kept-focus latch, so a send's focus doesn't follow into the next chat); 2026-10-29, #1515 (a long paste stays words while the chat is on its way); 2026-10-27, #1403 (failed sends' words outlast the composer; Sending… before the message shows); 2026-10-24, at #1185; a failed '/command' put back without its suggestion list over it at #1191 (#891 review).

## A new chat that something waits on

Some actions start a chat and then put something in it: a message sent from
the empty canvas, a screenshot, a Hermes call setup prompt. The thing goes
into the chat that action created, never into another one that opened
meanwhile.

**Siblings:** the composer's send from the empty canvas · Ask Hermes About
Screen (the voice sheet's screenshot and a screen question) · Settings' Hermes
test call and watch prompts · a Classic voice conversation's fresh chat ·
New Chat and its focus · a widget's or Shortcut's New Chat · the /new command
· Pulse's Do it on an item from no chat or from a Kanban task's worker
· the fresh chat that stands in for an empty one Hermes lost, which takes
what waited (An empty new chat Hermes lost)

**Code**
- Creating the chat: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (createNewSession and createAndReconcileSession return the chat they opened; startChatForComposerSubmission; startNewChat and focusNewChatComposer; prepareVoiceConversation)
- Screenshots: `Conduit/Services/AppState+ScreenQuestion.swift` (startChatForScreenshot, openScreenQuestion)
- Hermes calls: `Conduit/Services/AppState+HermesCalls.swift` (startHermesCallsChat)
- Widget and Shortcut launches: `Conduit/Services/AppState+WidgetLaunch.swift`
- Pulse's Do it: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (startPulseNewChat), `Conduit/Services/PulseFeed.swift` (actOnPulseCard)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/SessionRenameTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/PulseFeedTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- What waits on a new chat goes in only when the chat createNewSession returned is still the one open. Another chat opened or created meanwhile (a voice action, a screen question, a notification) gets nothing. The message stays in the composer, the screenshot goes back or waits, and the user is told (2026-10-24, #941's review, #1191).
- New Chat focuses the composer only on the chat it made. A Classic voice conversation files and archives only its own new chat under Voice; a fresh one asked for fails when another chat took the screen.
- Pulse's Do it on an item from no chat (and, since #1473, on one from a Kanban task's worker, which Hermes won't reopen as a chat) starts a chat only when New Chat can start one at once, and puts the reminder only in the chat its own create returned, while that one is still open. The Pulse screen stays up until then, so a chat that didn't start leaves it there to say why (2026-10-25, #1240 on the `pulse` branch).

**Open gaps**
- A widget's or Shortcut's New Chat and /new put nothing in the chat, so they only report whether the open chat changed.

**Checked:** 2026-11-04, #1752 (an empty chat Hermes lost hands its screenshot, composer prompt, focus and Classic voice filing to the fresh chat in its place, see An empty new chat Hermes lost); 2026-10-30, #1542 (All history stays after the host's 2000 limit and stops at the oldest reading; the stores needed no change); 2026-10-29, #1517 (the `pulse` branch merged into main: the app paths it lists are on main now; nothing else changed); 2026-10-29, #1479, carrying #1473 from the `pulse` branch (Do it on a card from a Kanban task's worker takes the same new chat); 2026-10-25, #1241 (Pulse's Do it, from #1240 on the `pulse` branch); main's code as at #1191.

## /new in a Bot Chat

`/new` (and `/reset`, `/clear`) starts a new chat, except in a bot's one
chat, which never forks: there it compacts the same chat instead, so the
bot starts from a summary with fresh context and the user stays in Bots.

**Siblings:** the composer's `/new` in chats and project chats (starts a new
chat) · Bot Chat (compacts) · a Bot Chat `/new` with attachments (refused,
the draft kept) · group rooms (no slash commands) · the notice the compaction
shows (says the chat compacts and keeps its memory and skills) · the `/help`
text and the slash suggestions' "Start a new conversation" (the general
command, still right outside Bot Chats) · "A new chat that something waits
on" (a Bot Chat's `/new` opens no chat, so nothing waits on one)

**Code**
- The guard: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (activeChatIsCanonicalBotChat, isCanonicalForeverChatReset, executeSlashCommand's new/reset/clear case, the attachment refusal in performComposerSubmission)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/AppStateSessionCompressTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- A Bot Chat is one continuous conversation: `/new` there compacts it, whatever follows the command, and never opens a chat in Chats. Saved memory and skills stay (upstream Bot Mode's forever chat; 2026-10-26, #1310, issue #1307).
- The chat is a Bot Chat by positive evidence only: one of the chat's own ids is one this process registered when it opened the Bot Chat (a reopened one runs under a fresh runtime id), or the roster's canonical id. Without either, `/new` starts a new chat.
- With attachments, `/new` in a Bot Chat (title or not) is refused and the draft kept: a compaction carries no attachments, and the text is never sent to the bot.
- On the gateway's own listener the compaction is the session authority's fenced `session.mutate` compress, as every compress there is (see Two Hermes servers; 2026-11-02, #1631).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1631 (the compaction on the gateway's listener); 2026-10-26, #1310.

## Bot workstreams

A bot's Bot Chat as its coordinator: it hands work that needs tools to
workstreams, hidden sessions of its own on the bot's profile, follows them by
ref (W1, W2), and hears back when one finishes, fails, waits on the user or
has something ready for them to look at.
It's on for every bot until the user turns it off, in Edit Bot > Work or with
`hermes -p <bot> conduit-push work off`. It was
built on the `bot-workstreams` branches, merged to main on 2026-11-03 (M0, notifier #484; M1
from notifier #490, #491, #493, #495, #497 and #498; M2, the app's Work
panel, from notifier #499 and #1619; M3, Edit Bot > Work, from notifier
#509 and #1649; M4, workstreams that read each other and work in worktrees,
from notifier #510 and #1656; M5a, a voice call's jobs kept in the registry,
from notifier #511, #512 and #1657). It reached both mains on 2026-11-03 (#1701, notifier #519, plugin 0.127.0).

**Siblings:** the Bot Chat (the work tools, offered only there and only
with workstreams on; its policy, strict or lookups, holding its tools and a
fork's; the note on its turns listing open work; the work updates that come
in as hidden turns, which the transcript leaves out as it does every hidden
user turn) · a workstream's session (hidden, titled, on the bot's own
profile, its steps journaled; its own `work_progress` checklist and ready
mark, and its report written for you in its chat; its brief carries the
coordinator's `work_note` notes (labelled as data, never your go-ahead; the
worker doesn't write the bot's memory) and
the message of yours the Bot Chat is answering, quoted as yours (none when a
work update started the turn), with what counts as your go-ahead under the bot's approval mode, and names other running work in the same git repository; it reads the bot's other workstreams with `work_list` and `work_read`, read only, never the asks between bots; with `worktree` it works in a git worktree of its own, Hermes' subagent worktree on a branch of its own, removed on resolve only when it holds nothing and made again when it's sent words; a reply in it sends no push, the Bot Chat's
reply to the update is the one push, and its turns start no Live Activity) · the `conduit://session/` link a work
tool's answer and every work update carry, with the bot's profile (see Links
in messages) · an

Bot mentions and teammate messages (`message_agent` refused in a coordinator

Check first note; Hermes' own crash re-run, `desktop.auto_continue`, retired

voice's interrupts leave it running), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (ToolStep's work cards, runningToolTitle, the brief's card in place of a user bubble, a Bot Chat reply's work links drawn as cards under it by `BotWorkLinks.split`, which reads the notifier's `_link` wording "[Open W3](conduit://session/…)" and leaves out the Desktop reference after it, and the refs it names linked in its words by `BotChatWorkReply` and `BotWorkLinks.linkingNamedRefs`, drawn through `AssistantBubble`'s `shownContent` so Copy keeps the reply's own words), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ConversationScreen.swift`'s `V2ConversationMenu` (Edit Bot in a Bot Chat's ⋯ menu), `AppState.displayedChatTitle` (a workstream's task as its title), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ChatsView.swift` and `AppState.listAllProfilesCatalog` (search and All profiles), `ConduitTests/BotWorkstreamsTests.swift`; `AppState.invalidateBotModeState` (a server change clears the kept work); `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (normalizeMessages, which drops hidden rows from the transcript), `Conduit/Services/ConduitAppLink.swift` and `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (openAppLink, the link's profile); opening a workstream's chat: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (openLinkedSession and notificationOpenNeedsAuthoritativeRead skip the list read for one; `activeProfileSessions` leaves workstreams out, kept by `workstreamsGeneration`; `readUnreadBotsWork` as the roster lands and as the plugin reports workstreams)
- The chat Conduit opens on leaves workstreams out of its newest-chat pick: `Conduit/Services/ChatResumePolicy.swift` (`ChatResumeSessionResolver.target`'s `unlistedSessionIDs`), `Conduit/Services/ChatResumeCoordinator.swift` (`selectTarget`), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (`selectChatResumeTarget` passes the rows `isUnlistedChat` names: workstreams and Pulse's chat), by `BotWorkStore.isWorkstream(_:among:)`, the lists' own rule; `ConduitTests/BotWorkstreamsTests.swift` (`testTheChatConduitResumesIsNeverAnUnlistedWorkstream`)
- A resolved workstream shown in Hermes (Desktop's link): `notifier/work_tool.py` (`_show_in_desktop`, `_show_resolved_once`), and the reads that leave workstreams out by the registry: `notifier/artifacts_index.py` (`workstreams`), `notifier/dashboard/api/workspace.py` (`_workstreams`), `notifier/pulse_hermes.py` (`_workstreams`, `_NOT_WORK`)
- The checklist as its chat's Tasks line: `Conduit/Services/BotWorkstreams.swift` (`checklistPlan`), `Conduit/Services/AppState+ChatCards.swift` (`refreshWorkPlan`), `Conduit/Services/ChatCardsModel.swift` (`applyWorkPlan`, `clearWorkPlan` once the work leaves the list); the Work panel draws it with `PlanItemRow` (`Conduit/Views/Components/ChatCards.swift`)
- Design: designs/bot-mode-coordinator (project files)

**Rulings**
- A workstream's chat the app already knows (its bot's work was read) opens by its id without reading Hermes' list again first, from a link, a card or the Work panel: it's hidden from the list, so the read could never find its row (Eric's build 248 test: every open waited seconds on it; #1706). That holds on both paths: a workstream on the profile in use, and one on another bot's profile, whose open goes the way a notification's does and still switches to that profile. One tapped before its bot's work was read still reads the list once.
- Built on the `bot-workstreams` branches, tested apart from public TestFlight, and merged to main when Eric said so (2026-10-31, notifier #484; merged 2026-11-03, #1701 and notifier #519, Eric).
- Each bot's Bot Chat coordinates its own work; bots ask each other rather than one coordinator for all (2026-10-31, Eric).
- The model names work by ref only: a session id appears only inside the link, and a ref from another bot's registry names nothing (2026-10-31, notifier #484).
- On for every bot until the user turns it off, in Edit Bot > Work or with `work off` (design E, M3; notifier #509). On means lookups by default: the Bot Chat answers what a quick read-only lookup settles and starts workstreams for the rest, since the worst a lookups bot does is start a workstream it didn't need (Eric 2026-11-03, #1703, notifier 0.127.1); strict, "Only Coordinates", stays a choice, and a bot already set to it keeps it. Before that, strict was the default, as M0's comparison picked. Turning work back on in Edit Bot > Work comes back with lookups too. Lookups never write: setting or removing a place rule (a cron job) goes to a workstream, and a stored policy the plugin doesn't know reads as strict (notifier #521's review). A registry that can't be read holds the Bot Chat to strict rather than freeing it (2026-10-31, notifier #484's review). Under either setting the Bot Chat keeps its own memory: `memory` and the profile's memory provider's tools (`memory.provider`: Hindsight's hindsight_retain and hindsight_recall, say; by the tools the provider declares, or its name as their prefix), and its note names them; a workstream keeps the provider's tools as before (Eric 2026-11-04: Furina handed a Hindsight retain to a workstream; notifier #542, #1754).
- Once the bot has a registry (it has had work, or a setting was saved), a chat whose title can't be read is held to the policy for that call, since it might be the coordinator (2026-10-31, notifier #484's review). A bot that's on only by default isn't held on a failed title read: every chat of every bot would be (2026-11-02, notifier #509; the plugin's choice). Where workstreams can't run (a plugin host process, or no session API), the default is off, so a bot never set up keeps its Bot Chat's tools; a policy the user saved stands (2026-11-02, notifier #509's review, #1654).
- Under `plugins.isolation: host` the tools answer with the reason rather than starting anything, since the session API is only in the dashboard's process (2026-10-31, notifier #484).
- "Bot Chat" is the coordinator's title only: work_start refuses it for a workstream, since the title names the session and the policy reads it (2026-10-31, notifier #485).
- A registry that exists but can't be read at a turn's hooks keeps that turn quiet (no push, alert call or Live Activity), since it may be a hidden workstream; the Bot Chat's own turn still pushes when its title can be read (2026-10-31, notifier #485).
- Ideas taken from Claude's project coordinator (design C.11): workers you can talk to in their own chat, states that say who's waiting (ready beside done), a checklist each worker keeps, the coordinator's notes in each brief, and your words quoted as yours (2026-11-01, Eric).
- A workstream's approvals follow the bot's Hermes approval mode (manual, smart, or off/yolo), and Edit Bot can set a separate mode for its workstreams (2026-11-01, Eric). Built in M3 as Same as Chats (the default), Ask Me First (only the user's own words are a go-ahead before a step that can't be undone, with Hermes' approval cards too where the bot's chats have them) and Don't Ask (Hermes' per-session bypass in each workstream's own session, set before each turn the plugin sends, never process-wide, and turned back on only in sessions the plugin turned it off in) (2026-11-02, notifier #509, #1649). Leaving Don't Ask turns approvals back on at once in each of those sessions, reopening one that isn't live, so a turn the user starts there directly asks again; a resolved one is reached only while it's live, reopening ones that aren't stops after 20 seconds, and the ones left (and any Hermes doesn't take) stay marked and are turned back before that workstream's next send, which waits until they are (2026-11-02, notifier #509, #1654).
- Edit Bot > Work reads its settings up to three times, a second and then two apart, and again when the connection comes back, before it says it couldn't; the app's log says why each read failed (Eric 2026-11-03, #1714: "sometimes" it didn't load, as when opened during a reconnect).
- Edit Bot > Work saves each change as it's made, on the plugin, so every device agrees; Edit Bot's Cancel doesn't undo it, and the page takes one change at a time. The plugin keeps one policy, so turning Coordinate Work off and on again comes back with lookups, the default, whatever it was before (2026-11-02, #1649, the app's choice; lookups since Eric 2026-11-03, #1703).
- An update carries a short line of the report and the chat's link; the full report stays in the workstream's chat and in work_read (2026-11-01, notifier #490).
- Asks between bots go coordinator to coordinator, only between the user's bots on one Hermes, and only to a bot whose workstreams are on. What one bot asks or answers reaches the other as data, never as the user's go-ahead, and each bot does the work with its own tools and approvals. An answer goes into the workstream named in `for` (queued, no extra Bot Chat turn; not while it's interrupted, notifier #497), else to the asking Bot Chat; closing an ask unanswered tells the bot that asked (2026-11-01, notifier #493, design C.9).
- After a restart a workstream is continued on its own only when its journal shows nothing that can change things in flight since its turn began (reads are an allow list; a `tool_call` counts by the tools it calls, and a step whose journal entry couldn't be written counts as one that changes things), only once until a turn of it ends, and only with the bot's `--after-restart continue` (the default; `ask` leaves it to the user). A step that can change things and was cut off is never re-run: the Bot Chat asks the user, with a Check first note that changes nothing. Hermes' own crash re-run is retired for workstreams, leaving a live sibling's marker alone (2026-11-01, notifier #495, design C.7). Starts and sends wait for the sweep to settle, and a stop lets a later restart continue the work again (2026-11-01, notifier #495's review).
- A send the restart cut off that Hermes never stored is sent once more only into work recovery continued; into stopped or idle work it would start a turn nobody okayed, so the Bot Chat is told it may not have arrived instead (2026-11-01, notifier #495).
- Only the Bot Chat asks: work_start and work_ask tell the coordinator to ask for a workstream with `for` rather than brief it to ask, and a workstream that tries, with work_ask or Hermes' `message_agent`, is refused and told to name the bot and the need in its report. An answer for an interrupted workstream (a restart or the user stopped its turn) goes to the Bot Chat, not into the workstream (2026-11-01, notifier #497, from the .58 test).
- A clean restart is recovered like a crash: Hermes' own stop of every running turn on its way out isn't taken for the user's, and a step it cut off counts as never finished, so a change it may have made still waits for the user (2026-11-01, notifier #498, from the .58 restart test).
- A workstream doesn't write the bot's memory: what's worth keeping goes in its report, and the coordinator decides what to remember, with `work_note` for what every workstream should know (2026-11-01, Eric, notifier #498).
- The user's own actions from the Work panel go straight to the workstream, never through the Bot Chat's model: a reply is sent as the user's own words, as if typed in its chat; Continue and Check first say the user tapped them. Continue after a restart cut off a step that can change things tells the workstream the step may have run, so it checks before running it again; stopping interrupted work runs nothing (2026-11-01, notifier #499, design C.6 and C.7).
- A start a restart cut off before its brief was sent offers only a reply, which goes in with the brief it never had; one cut off just as Hermes took its brief offers Check first, and Continue says its first steps may have run. A reply can't go in while a start is still under way, so it never lands before the brief; a start that never got a chat is closed by recovery so work_start starts it fresh (2026-11-01, notifier #499 and #501; Eric's rule for recovery, that a step whose effect isn't known is checked, never re-run, design C.7).
- A start still starting two minutes after its chat was made is taken as stuck and offers Stop in the Work panel, and the coordinator's work_send waits until it's running. The two minutes is the plugin's own choice, not a maintainer ruling (2026-11-01, notifier #501's review).
- Work leaves the panel only when it's resolved, by the user (Resolve) or by the coordinator (work_close); nothing resolves itself, however old, and unresolved work stays listed (2026-11-01, Eric: "if it's unfinished maybe people should actually go finish it, or mark it themselves"). The user's pin and reopen win: work_close refuses pinned work, and work the user reopened until it runs again. Resolve is refused while the work is still at it; resolving unpins it. Pins and resolves live in the plugin's registry, so every device agrees (2026-11-01, Eric, notifier #503).
- A workstream's approval can be answered on its "Needs you" card (Approve once, or Deny) and still in its own chat; the coordinator never answers it (2026-11-01, Eric: "it also shouldn't take away the option to do it directly in the session").
- On Hermes Desktop, which doesn't list workstreams (hidden sessions), a workstream opens from its link in the Bot Chat: each work link carries Desktop's own session reference after Conduit's link (`[Open W3](conduit://session/<id>?profile=<p>) @session:<p>/<id>`, the profile left out for the launch one), which Desktop draws as a chip that opens the session by id, joined to it while it runs, its approval card included; the Bot Chat's line for a workstream waiting on the user carries its link and asks the bot to hand it on. Every text that hands the bot a work link (the work update, work_list's description, the waiting-on-you line) tells it to give the link exactly as written, the @session reference included, since a bot that wrote it in its own words left Desktop nothing to open (Eric 2026-11-04, notifier #537, #1735). Workstreams stay out of Desktop's Sessions list while open; unhiding them was the fallback if the chip didn't open a live one (Eric 2026-11-03, notifier #526, #1710). A resolved one is unhidden, by the user or the bot, and work resolved before 0.130.1 once (up to three tries): Desktop opens the chip by its id alone (it drops the profile) and finds a session's backend from its list or its live session, so a finished hidden workstream said "Session owner could not be resolved" (Eric 2026-11-04, notifier #540, #1753). Conduit leaves it out of its own lists by the plugin's list of each bot's workstreams (`workstream_sessions`, resolved ones included): Chats, search and All profiles, and a bot's work is read once as the roster lands for every bot not read yet, so its rows leave the Chats list whether or not its Bot Chat was opened. Like a Bot Chat, a workstream's chat has no row of its own here, open or resolved, so its ⋯ menu has no Rename, Archive or Delete and its Artifacts button is off, as an open one always was, and Conduit never opens on it by itself: Jump to latest activity, and Continue where I left off with nothing saved to continue, pick the newest chat the lists show, as they skip a Bot Chat, while Continue still opens one the user had open (#1755). The plugin's profile-wide Artifacts list and Pulse's reads of the person's chats leave them out by the same registry, with the chats that continue them. In a Bot Chat reply Conduit draws its cards and leaves out the reference right after each work link that names the link's own session; any other reference (another chat's, or one in code) stays as written, a chat link (HermesSessionReference).
- The panel shows the bot's work, not its settings: the policy and its limit belong in Edit Bot (2026-11-01, Eric: "that's a configuration item").
- An opened Work row has its chat's button at the top, above the branch and checklist, so a long checklist doesn't push it out of sight (Eric 2026-11-04, #1742).
- A workstream's chat looks like any other chat: no bar while it runs or waits on you (Eric 2026-11-02: "it's unintuitive"). The composer's Stop stops it through the plugin, its approval card is in the chat, and only a workstream a restart cut off shows Continue and Check first under the title. Back and the edge swipe go to the Bot Chat that started it, not the Bots list (Eric 2026-11-02, #1639). The swipe starts anywhere, not only at the edge, and going between a Bot Chat and its workstream slides like a push and a pop, the workstream in from the trailing edge and the Bot Chat back in from the leading one: both show in one pushed screen, so nothing else animated it (Eric 2026-11-03, #1714). Only that swipe and Back leave a workstream, slow or quick: the system's swipes off the screen (the stack's edge swipe, iOS 26's swipe from anywhere, and the portrait zoom's own edge pan, swipe down and pinch, which ignore a hidden Back) are held off while a workstream shows, found by the names UIKit gives them, since SwiftUI has no switch for the zoom's (Eric 2026-11-06, #1858: a slow held swipe went to Bots Home, a quick one to the Bot Chat).
- The loop guard: an ask never goes to a bot already waiting in its chain (a bot with an open ask from another can't ask that one back until it answers), a chain goes at most two bots deep, and one bot asks another at most 10 times an hour (2026-11-01, notifier #493).

- A workstream reads the bot's other workstreams, never changes them and never sees the asks between bots; a need for another workstream to act goes through its report to the coordinator (design C.10, M4; notifier #510).
- A worktree is made only when the coordinator asks for one (`worktree: true`), on Hermes' local terminal and inside a git repository; where it can't be made, nothing starts, never a start in the shared folder instead. Resolving removes it only when it has no commits and a clean tree; one with work in it stays for the user to merge and Hermes' own worktree sweep archives it later. A workstream sent words after its worktree went gets it back at the same path (2026-11-02, notifier #510; the plugin's choice).
- Other running work in the same repository is flagged to the coordinator and named in the new workstream's brief, never refused (design F.7; notifier #510).
- A call kept with the Bot Chat is a conversation with the coordinator, so its background and quick jobs run on that bot as the coordinator's own workstreams (`started_in_call` in the tool's `work_list`, `call` on the app's row, which the app reads as `BotWorkItem.startedInCall`): counted against the limit, in its note as its own, out of Voice Jobs, and the coordinator's update on each, and its result in the coordinator's note, waits while any call is on in the Bot Chat: until the call is saved with the chat, or ends (`POST /workstreams/call-ended`, sent when the call leaves its chat in any voice mode, Classic included, 15 seconds before release so the call's own saved turns land first), at most two hours. The adopt and the end name the call (the request's `call`, the call's own id; not the app row's `call`, which is "phone" or "watch"), so only that call's own end ends its hold (a save doesn't) and a job kept after its call ended holds nothing (the plugin keeps the last 8 ended calls, so an end that lands before its call's adopt still counts); `work_list` and `work_read` hold the result as the note does. So the call speaks the result first and the coordinator reports it in the Bot Chat after (Eric 2026-11-02, "Bot Chat calls only"; notifier #514, #1657). A workstream the coordinator starts itself during the call (`work_start` from a request the call sent as a Bot Chat turn) reports at once, in a turn of the Bot Chat's own (the plugin's work update); the call says that turn's reply when it's quiet, in Classic and every live mode, as it says a job's result, while a turn someone typed in the Bot Chat stays background and a reply to a voice request no job owns stays a quiet note, as does one while several typed messages wait on replies; who asked for a turn is taken as it starts (the first message no earlier turn took, steers aside, or nobody), so a message typed while a work update runs doesn't pass for its prompt; a report is said as Classic says it in every mode, links as their text (Eric 2026-11-02, his Gridania test: the answer was written but never said; #1667). Calls kept with other chats are as below.
- A call kept with one of the bot's workstreams' chats makes no jobs: its requests go to the workstream (Send, `how` auto), an interrupt while it works (Eric 2026-11-02, #1657). When the app can't tell it's a workstream's chat, because its bot's work hasn't loaded, a request becomes a job rather than being lost (Eric 2026-11-02, decision card, #1657).
- Whether a call's jobs are kept at all is open (see Open gaps). Where one is kept as a call job (a call kept with another chat; a Bot Chat call's are workstreams, above), it never wakes the Bot Chat or counts against its limit, since the call tells the user its result; after a restart it always waits for the user, since nobody would hear a continued turn; a bot whose workstreams are off keeps none; Stop on its Work panel card stops it for the call too (the phone's job is cancelled, never settled as finished when its session goes quiet; a Watch relay job reads the interrupt as cancelled) (2026-11-02, notifier #511, #1657; the plugin's and the app's choices, within design E.6).
- With lookups on, the Bot Chat's note leads with them: a question a quick read-only lookup settles (the weather, news and current facts, past chats, skills, health, location, inbox) is answered in the Bot Chat's own turn, and only the rest that needs tools goes to a workstream; strict's wording stays as it was (Eric's Gridania test 2026-11-03: the weather still went to a workstream; notifier #516).
- Workstreams can run on a model of their own, picked in Edit Bot > Work (Workstream Model); the default is the bot's own, the one its Bot Chat uses. A pick applies to workstreams started after it: running ones keep the model they started on, and a call's jobs keep the voice-job model (Eric 2026-11-03; #1677, notifier #516).
- After starting work the coordinator replies in one short sentence that adds to the Started card (what it'll report, or a question it needs answered), never repeating its title or saying it started it: the card shows the start and its live status, and an empty turn would leave the chat list, the notification and Read Aloud with nothing (Eric 2026-11-03 asked which made more sense and left it to this recommendation; notifier #516).
- A work update or ask that comes in as a hidden turn as Hermes compacts the Bot Chat still reaches the bot's model, rather than ending on Hermes' "Context was compacted" line, and that line never pushes (2026-11-06, #1849, notifier 0.133.4).

**Open gaps**
- A workstream may still call the memory provider's tools, retain included, though it can't call `memory` (its coordinator decides what to remember): a provider's tools don't say which of them write.
- An ask from another bot reaches the Bot Chat as a hidden turn, so the asked bot's transcript shows no "Furina asks" card; the ask is listed in its Work panel instead.
- Chats, search and All profiles leave out only the workstreams of bots whose work the app has read (read once per bot as the roster lands, opened, or kept from last time; one read later leaves the lists already shown at once). Hermes hides an open one; a resolved one is shown there (notifier #540), so one started and resolved since its bot's last read shows in the Chats list until the bot's work is read again (Bots Home, its Bot Chat or its panel), and until then it can be the chat Conduit opens on. A call's chat search leaves known workstreams out too, Hermes' own search included (2026-11-05, #1810).
- The Work panel reads again every 5 seconds while work runs and every 20 otherwise, for as long as a bot's Bot Chat (its title line shown or not, so new work shows), its panel or a workstream's bar is open, once for a bot with workstreams off, and up to four times 3 seconds apart for a bot's chat its list doesn't name; a chat the plugin lists as a workstream but the list doesn't show (a resolved one opened from a card or a link) reads the Resolved list's first page instead, so one resolved longer ago shows no title line. There's no push for a change yet.
- A workstream's approval shows on its "Needs you" card as the plugin reads it from Hermes in the process the workstream runs in (`approval.pending` and `approval.respond` on its live session, by request id), since Hermes answers a session's approvals only for its live session, which the phone can't name; through the chat's card when that chat is open. Only an approval Hermes names by its request shows there; one without (an older Hermes) is answered in its chat, which checks the session's queue first. The card shows the command whole, as written; an empty one or one over 2,000 characters is cut and offered Deny only, and the plugin reads the request again before an approve and refuses it (`deny_only`), as the Watch's approval cards do. The Bot Chat itself never answers it.
- The first session Hermes builds on a secondary profile after the dashboard starts can come up without the work tools; the upstream test takes it with a warm-up session (2026-10-31 canary).
- Ask Me First on a bot whose approvals are off in Hermes is the brief's rule only, with no approval card: Hermes reads `approvals.mode: off` for every session and has no way to ask in one while its config says off (its per-session switch only turns approvals off). Its caption says so. Upstream ask: a per-session approval mode.
- Turning workstreams off leaves running work running, and its Work panel and approvals reachable, as `work off` always has.
- The phone and the Watch still run call jobs on their own engines, not the broker's: Eric skipped M5c (one engine) for now on 2026-11-03 (#1676), since the broker runs only where the bot's work is on and the dashboard hosts its sessions, so the phone's engine would stay as the fallback anyway.
- A coordinator outside the dashboard (a bot on Telegram or another messaging platform) gets "off here" from the work tools, which need the dashboard's session API. Eric parked it (M5d) on 2026-11-03 until people ask: Conduit is already the mobile app most people would use Telegram for (#1676).
- A workstream's call doesn't speak what its requests came to: the workstream's reply shows in its chat and the Work panel, and the call says so rather than following it (it can't follow a workstream's turns, which send the app no events) (#1657). A workstream's call whose bot's work hasn't loaded (its read failed, tried again at most once a minute; a read already under way is waited on for up to five seconds) makes its request a job rather than lose it (Eric 2026-11-02, #1657: a job rather than a lost request, see Rulings). A request while another action on the workstream is on its way is told it's busy, nothing sent (#1657). A Bot Chat call whose Bot Chat isn't open on the phone can't tell a turn typed on another device from the coordinator's report, so it says that too; nor can one tell another hidden turn in the Bot Chat that answers no one on screen (not the plugin's work update) from a report, so that's said too (#1667). Reports waiting to be said keep the newest three (#1667). Classic hears only the chat open on the phone, so a Classic Bot Chat call with another chat open says no reports (#1667). A message sent after a work update is queued but before it starts is taken as the update's prompt, so that report stays quiet and the message's own reply is said (#1667). A call kept with a resolved workstream's chat whose row isn't loaded (past the Resolved list's first page) is told the workstream isn't loaded and to open it from the Work panel, nothing sent: the app knows the chat is a workstream's, so it makes no job (#1657). Until a bot's work has loaded once, a call's request waits for that read (up to its 30 seconds, once a minute while it fails) before its job starts (#1657). A call's chat names a profile only when it's a Bot Chat, or a Watch call's job chat resumed on the phone; the latter's unnamed jobs run on that chat's profile too, as the Watch call's own did (#1657, left open for Eric). A Bot Chat call's held updates go once the call is saved with the chat or ends; only a phone that quit mid-call (its call never ends on the phone) leaves them held for two hours.
- A call's later request that runs as a turn in a chat it already has gets no row of its own: a Watch call's later ordinary requests (`continueJob`) run in the chat its first job made, whose row follows that chat's turns (a turn reopens it), and a request that joins an attached call chat (`joinCallChat`) runs in the user's own chat, which isn't a job's. The registry keeps one row per session, so the Work panel shows the chat's job once, not each request (#1657).
- Whether a call's jobs belong in the Work panel at all, marked as a call's and kept in Voice Jobs too, is Eric's call, asked 2026-11-02 and not yet answered; M5a is built on the recommended yes, with a kept job's chat staying a Voice Jobs chat (its own title, Back and Stop), as every call job's chat is today, not a workstream's (notifier #511, #512, #1657).
- Two journal edges from M0 that recovery leans on (notifier #495's review): a step that starts while a compacted workstream's lineage is still unsettled isn't journaled or noted as missed, and a step's end with an unknown call id closes the oldest open step of that tool by name.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1892 (the workstream's screen also carries NavigationBarKeeper, which shows its bar again after a swipe back let go and leaves a finished pop alone; SystemBackSwipeGate's page lookup and swipe list became statics the keeper shares, the gate unchanged);
