## Bot Screen

A bot's own desktop on its Hermes host (Hermes' Bot Screen: an Xvnc and Xfce
desktop per profile, Linux only, off until started), where the bot clicks and
types with `computer_use`. Conduit shows it live, lets the user take over for
a sign-in or a CAPTCHA and hand back, types on it, starts and stops it, and
installs its packages on the host, so nothing needs a terminal (Eric
2026-11-05).

**Siblings:** the viewer sheet (status, install with its log and the host's
sudo password, the sandbox image switch, Start Screen, the live screen,
Take Over and Hand Back, Hand Back for Them, Stop Screen, the type bar and its
keys) · where it opens: a Bot Chat's and a workstream's ⋯ menu (Bot's
Screen), the Bot Overview's header, a Work panel card's Open Screen (see Bot
workstreams) · the plugin's hold, one of the bot's chats driving the screen
at a time: the Bot Chat, its workstreams and any other chat of the bot (a
delegated child as its parent), refused with who has it; browser tools aren't
held · who drives it now apart from who used it last (`screen` in
`GET /workstreams`, `screen` and `screen_used_at` on each row) · a refused
workstream told when the screen is free · a workstream's ask for the user on
the screen (`work_progress` `screen`), a "Needs you" count and card, the Bot
Chat told in its update and its note · the worker's brief and the tool's
description · the notifier's README and the app's README · Hermes Desktop's
own Bot Screen panel (Hermes', not ours) · the sheet covering its chat, so replies under it keep their notifications (see Notifications) · a takeover handed back when the app goes to the background or the sheet closes, one answered after either handed straight back, and the status read again on return · an install's sudo ask shown again after a reconnect, from the resume's open requests · which hosts can have a screen, read per bot and read again for a new server · the Watch and CarPlay (not
needed: driving a desktop needs a screen to see it on)

**Code**
- App: `Conduit/Services/BotScreen.swift` (`BotScreenStatus`, `BotScreenLease`, `BotScreenUse`, `BotScreenKey`, `BotScreenModel`, which opens the stream itself and relays it to the page, `BotScreenSupport`), `Conduit/Views/BotScreenViews.swift` (`BotScreenSheet`, which counts itself in `botScreenSheetsOpen` while open, from the chat's menu, a Work panel card or Bots Home, `BotScreenWebView`, `BotScreenButton`), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (`display`, `displayStreamRequest`, `respondToDisplaySudo`, the `display.*` events and `display.install.sudo`), `Conduit/Resources/BotScreen/BotScreenViewer.html` (noVNC 1.7.0, MPL-2.0, built by `scripts/bot-screen/build.sh` from `scripts/bot-screen/viewer.js`), `Conduit/Views/BotWorkViews.swift` (`BotWorkRow.screenBox`), `Conduit/Services/BotWorkstreams.swift` (`BotWorkItem.screen`, `screenUsedAt`, `screenAsk`; `BotWorkSnapshot.screen`), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ConversationScreen.swift` (`V2ConversationMenu`, and its screen sheet setting `chatCoveredBySheet`), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2BotsHome.swift` (`BotOverviewSheet`), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (`botScreens`, reset in `invalidateBotModeState`; `chatCoveredBySheet`, `botScreenSheetsOpen`), `ConduitTests/BotWorkstreamsTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/HermesClientTests.swift` (the owed hand back)
- Notifier: `notifier/screen_lock.py` (the hold file, conduit-screen.json in the bot's home), `notifier/work_tool.py` (`screen_block`, `screen_turn_ended`, `_watch_screen`, `SCREEN_BRIEF`, the `screen` ask in `work_progress`, `app_list`'s `screen`), `notifier/__init__.py` (`_pre_tool_call`, `_on_session_end`, `_subagent_start`), `notifier/tests/test_screen_lock.py`

**Rulings**
- One of a bot's chats drives its screen at a time, all of them, not only its workstreams: two on one mouse and keyboard fight, and separate browser tabs don't solve that. Browser automation that needs no shared desktop input stays free (Eric 2026-11-05, notifier #559).
- Who drives the screen now is kept apart from who used it last: a last-used time doesn't say who has it (Eric 2026-11-05, notifier #559, #1832).
- Install from the phone too: a feature with friction doesn't get used. The screen's entries don't show at all on a host that can't have one, such as Windows or macOS (Eric 2026-11-05, #1832).
- A hold lasts until its chat's turn ends, ten idle minutes, or its process going away, so a crash never keeps the screen; a file that can't be read lets the call through, since the hold is coordination, not a fence (notifier #559, the plugin's choice).
- The app opens the stream's socket itself, with the headers every Hermes request carries, and hands the bytes to noVNC in the page, so a Cloudflare Access or authorizer host works as the rest of the app does (#1832, the app's choice).
- Where the host has a real desktop and no Bot Screen (a Linux seat, as on Windows and macOS), the plugin's hold is the host's, shared by every bot, and the app shows no screen there, so a workstream can't ask the user onto it there: Eric's ruling not to show the screen where Hermes has none (Eric 2026-11-05, notifier #559, #1832).
- The type bar sends each character's keysym (Latin-1 as itself, the rest as Unicode keysyms), not keys on a layout, so what's typed is what lands whatever the phone's keyboard, as the type bar's caption says; a hardware keyboard on the screen itself goes through noVNC, as Hermes Desktop's does, so it follows the host's layout (#1832, the app's choice).
- A hand back the app owes is tried again after 1, 3 and 9 seconds, then before the bot's next status read: one the sheet's close, the app going to the background or Hand Back failed to send, or a takeover answered after the sheet closed. One on its way isn't sent twice, a takeover cancels it, and one Hermes refuses isn't owed anymore (from GLM's review of #1832, closed in #1857). A reconnect rebuilds the sheet on the new client without handing back: the user's hold stays theirs under the same viewer id (#1857).
- Each stream's page messages carry its attach's tag, so a stopped stream's late close or failure never ends the one that replaced it (from GLM's review of #1832, closed in #1857).
- In the background no stream opens: a bot's own status change or a read then leaves the stream idle, and coming back watches it again (a sheet a reconnect rebuilds in the background starts away too), so the sheet never sits on a lost stream it never could have kept (2026-11-06, issue 1870, #1872).
- A workstream that compacted mid-turn keeps its screen ask and its "drives the screen" on its card; the waiting list holds up to 20 per bot, one past that isn't promised a message, and a refused free-screen message is tried again after a growing pause (notifier #578).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1872 (no stream opens in the background, issue 1870; Rulings); 2026-11-06, #1857 (with notifier #578: a screen ask and the card's controller across a compaction, the waiting list's per-bot cap and retry pause, a failed hand back sent again, stream messages tagged; no gaps left); 2026-11-05, #1832 (with notifier #559: the screen in the app, one chat driving it at a time, install from the phone)

## Composer Return key

The optional hardware-keyboard shortcut in Settings > Keyboard: with it on,
Return sends the composer message and Shift-Return starts a new line. It
is on by default on a Mac and off on iPhone and iPad; the on-screen keyboard's
Return key always inserts a new line.

**Siblings:** the chat composer's inline field (chats, project chats, Bot
Chat; done) · the full editor, a chat's and a room's (done, #1394) · group
rooms' field (done, #1394) · the Mac, where the iPad app's text system
takes Return before the key presses reach the field (done, #1394: a Return
key command with priority over the text system) · iPad and iPhone with a
hardware keyboard (done, the same command, with the key-press route kept
for keypad Enter) · the Keyboard caption ("When on, Return sends and
Shift-Return starts a new line.", done, #1208) · the toggle's accessibility
hint (not needed, it already says the setting applies to hardware keyboards
only) · the two default footnotes, Mac on and iPhone/iPad off (not needed,
each states the default for its device) · the hardware-keyboards caption
(not needed, shown only off a Mac and already says the on-screen Return key
is unchanged) · a running dictation (done, #1315: Return stops it; the
Keyboard caption is unchanged, as it describes the option)

**Code**
- Policy: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerReturnKey.swift` (ComposerReturnKey)
- Key handling: `Conduit/Views/Components/ReturnKeyTextView.swift` (ReturnKeyTextView: the Return key command and pressesBegan; ReturnKeyTextEditor, the field rooms and the full editor use)
- Chat composer: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerPasteTextView.swift` (ImagePasteTextView), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (submitFromReturnKey, the full editor's)
- Full editor: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerFullEditor.swift`
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift` (field, submitFromReturnKey)
- Settings: `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (ComposerReturnKeySettings)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ComposerReturnKeyTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- On a Mac the composer fields (a chat's, a room's, the full editor) show no inline prediction (autocorrect and spelling stay on; ReturnKeyTextView). macOS draws it in a correction panel with its own nested event loop, and both Mac freezes captured on 2.2.1 (237) ran inside three or four of them, the chat's LazyVStack re-laying out forever (2026-10-28, #1460).
- The caption describes the option, not current behaviour, because the
  option starts off on iPhone and iPad (2026-10-24, #1208, review of #1190).
- While dictating, Return does what the Stop in Send's place does: stops
  the dictation, or calls off one still coming up, and sends nothing. The
  next Return, once the words are in and Send is back, sends (2026-10-26,
  #1315, see Send while dictating).
- Every composer takes the option, the full editor included: Return there
  sends like its Send button, and Shift-Return starts a new line (2026-10-27,
  #1394).

**Open gaps**
- Not yet checked on a Mac or an iPad with a keyboard: the Return key
  command sending, Shift-Return and the IME's Return still reaching the
  text, in chats, rooms and the full editor.

**Checked:** 2026-10-30, #1527 (a Return send keeps the field's focus on a Mac or with a hardware keyboard, see Composer focus after a send; ImagePasteTextView takes focus once in the window); 2026-10-29, #1515 (the same fields take a long paste as an attachment, `onLongTextPaste`; Return unchanged); 2026-10-28, #1460 (inline prediction off on a Mac).

## Composer at rest and expanded

Whether the composer rests as a slim bar (attach, the field, the mic) until
it is used, or stays expanded with its controls row showing: attach, the
model chip, the context ring, agents, the mic and Send.

**Siblings:** the chat composer (chats, project chats, Bot Chat; done, #1512)
· group rooms' composer (done, #1512) · the chat's voice button beside it
(done, #1512: it stays beside a composer that stays expanded, level with its
bottom, and the composer's own voice and mic buttons give way to it, see
Starting a call) · the composer bar the transcript fades under (not needed:
the bar takes the composer's height, see Bars lists scroll under) · the
drawer shell's chat (not needed: its chat composer never rests; its rooms'
composer follows the same rule, #1512) · iPhone, iPad and Mac · text:
docs/VOICE_SETTINGS.md "Dictate into the composer" (done, #1512); no
Settings caption describes it · the placeholder (the chat's: Message,
Interrupt, Steer, Queue, a chat on its way; the room's; the drawer
shell's chat, the same ComposerBar; done, #1541) · accessibility Text
Sizes on a narrow iPhone (both composers, resting and expanded, in both
shells; done, #1541)

**Code**
- Rule: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerLayout.swift` (ComposerLayout.staysExpanded, expandedMinimumWidth, composerStaysExpanded, composerLayoutFromWidth)
- V2: `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ConversationScreen.swift` (chatColumnWidth, composerStaysExpanded, voiceButtonBottomPadding), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (rests, inUseOrHeld, keepsVoiceButtonBeside, showsEmptyDraftSend, controlsRowShowsDictate, composerInUse), `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift` (rests, inUse)
- Drawer shell: `Conduit/Views/RootView.swift` (chatNavigationContent)
- Large Text Sizes: `Conduit/Views/Components/DynamicTypeSupport.swift` (ComposerPlaceholderText, conduitFixedGlyph), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (composerPlaceholder, composerShortPlaceholder), used in `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (composerContent's resting row, composerField) and `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift` (the resting row's attachButton, field)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ChatVoiceButtonTests.swift` (testComposerRestsOnIPhoneAndStaysExpandedOnMacAndWideIPad, testBigButtonSitsLevelWithTheBottomOfAComposerThatStaysExpanded)

**Rulings**
- iPhone: the composer rests and expands while it is used (focus, a draft,
  dictation, a notice, a control's sheet), at any width. iPad: it stays
  expanded when the chat's column has the room (600 pt, Artifacts beside it
  taken off) and rests below that. Mac: it stays expanded at any width, with
  its controls always in reach. There is no setting (Eric, 2026-10-29,
  #1512, issue 1483). A Mac's composer never rests, so a send that keeps
  the field focused changes nothing there. With a hardware keyboard on a
  narrow iPad a send keeps focus too, so a composer that rests stays
  expanded after it until a tap on the transcript (Eric, 2026-10-30, #1527).
  An iPhone never keeps focus after a send, keyboard or not, so its
  composer rests again and the reply has the height (Eric, 2026-10-31,
  #1556, see Composer focus after a send).
- A composer that stays expanded keeps the big voice button beside it, as the
  resting bar does, rather than sliding it aside while typing; the controls
  row then leaves out its own voice button, and its mic when the big button
  dictates. With an empty draft its Send shows dimmed, not the lock a
  composer that can't send (reconnecting, an offline copy, a chat still being made) shows (2026-10-29, #1512).
- Only use opens and closes the composer with its animation; the layout
  rule changing (a chat's first measured width, a window resized) switches
  it at once (2026-10-29, #1512).

- At the accessibility Text Sizes the resting bar's controls (attach, the
  mic, Stop) are capped at xxLarge like the controls row's, and the
  placeholder keeps to one line: the whole hint when it fits, then the
  hint without the agent's name ("Interrupt…"), then that one shrunk to
  fit and cut off. Below them it wraps as before, so the name stays
  (#1476). The same in group rooms (Eric's report, 2026-10-30, #1541).

**Open gaps**
- Not yet seen on a device: an iPad crossing 600 pt as a split or Artifacts
  resizes, and a Mac window at its narrowest. On an iPad the first frame
  of a chat may still show the resting bar before its width is measured.
- Not yet seen on a device: an iPhone at AX3 to AX5 in a running chat and
  in a group room (#1541, checked in code and a unit test only).

**Checked:** 2026-10-31, #1556 (an iPhone rests again after a send, keyboard or not); 2026-10-30, #1541 (the resting bar and its placeholder at accessibility Text Sizes on a narrow iPhone); 2026-10-30, #1527 (a send keeps focus with a hardware keyboard, so the composer stays expanded after it); 2026-10-29, #1512 (new entry, issue 1483).

## Composer focus after a send

Whether the composer's field keeps focus once a message goes, so the next
one can be typed straight away, or gives it up so the keyboard goes down.

**Siblings:** the chat composer (chats, project chats, Bot Chat; done,
#1527) · Send, Return and the long-press choices (Steer, Queue,
Interrupt), and a message that waits for its chat ("Sends when connected";
done, #1527) · Stop in Send's place (done, #1527) · the full editor (done,
#1527: a send from it gives the field focus back as the sheet goes) · group
rooms' composer (done, #1556: it follows the same rule, its full editor included) · a prediction sent from the suggestion row (done, #1527:
the same send, so it keeps whatever focus the field had) · the plan card, which opens whatever the focus on a Mac or with a hardware
keyboard (not needed: its check is for the keyboard, not the focus; its
ruling now says the focus stays, see Plan card) · the resting composer and
the minimised call bar (done, #1527, #1556: with a hardware keyboard on a
narrow iPad the composer stays expanded after a send while the field
keeps focus, until a tap on the transcript, see Composer at rest and
expanded; the call bar, on those and on a Mac, comes back after a send and
hides again only once words are typed) ·
iPhone, iPad and Mac · no Settings caption or doc describes it

**Code**
- Rule: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerLayout.swift` (ComposerLayout.keepsFocusAfterSend)
- Chat composer: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (endInput, dismissComposer, collapseSubmittedDraft, submit, submitFromReturnKey, queueUntilChatIsReady, performComposerAction; handoffComposer, which clears focusesAfterFullEditor; composerInUse and hidesMinimisedCallBar, which follow focus), `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerPasteTextView.swift` (updateUIView and Coordinator.deactivate, which pass the binding's focus to the field), `Conduit/Views/Components/ReturnKeyTextView.swift` (ReturnKeyTextView.setFocusIntent and didMoveToWindow: focus changes after the update that asked, and a field rebuilt with focus takes it once it's in the window; ReturnKeyTextEditor, rooms' field and the full editor, the same), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (composerTyping, read through V2ComposerTypingKey, hides MinimisedLiveVoiceBar)
- Full editor: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerFullEditor.swift`, opened by ComposerBar's expand button (which takes focus from the field) and its sheet
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift` (send; focusesAfterFullEditor, read in the full editor sheet's onDismiss)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ChatVoiceButtonTests.swift` (testComposerKeepsFocusAfterSendOnMacAndOnAnIPadWithAHardwareKeyboard), `ConduitTests/ComposerPasteTextViewTests.swift` (testARebuiltFieldTakesFocusOnlyWhenItWantsItAsItReachesTheWindow, testFocusChangesWaitUntilAfterTheUpdateThatAskedAndTheLastAskWins)

**Rulings**
- On a Mac, or on an iPad with a hardware keyboard, a send or Stop
  leaves the field focused when the user was typing, as a desktop client
  does; a click or tap on the transcript still takes focus away. With only
  the on-screen keyboard it goes down, so the reply has the screen (Eric,
  2026-10-30, #1527). The iPad's check is for a connected keyboard, as the
  plan card's is.
- An iPhone never keeps focus after a send, keyboard or not: a kept
  composer takes height the reply needs (Eric, 2026-10-31, #1556; #1527 had
  kept it with a keyboard).
- Group rooms follow the same rule as chats (2026-10-31, #1556; their
  send had never let go of focus).
- Where the field keeps focus, focus alone doesn't hide the minimised call
  bar: it shows after a send and hides only while words are typed, so a
  kept focus never hides a call (2026-10-30, #1527).
- A send or Stop from the full editor gives the field focus once the sheet
  has gone, not while it is dismissing; if the composer hands off to another
  chat first, that focus doesn't follow it there (2026-10-30, #1527).
- Opening a call from the composer still takes focus away on every device:
  the call has the screen (2026-10-30, #1527).
- Every composer field takes or gives up focus just after the SwiftUI
  update that asked, never inside it, and several asks before then come to
  the last. Resigning inside the update asked the hosting view whether it
  could take focus, which re-entered the view graph: on iOS 27 the whole
  app froze mid-typing until force-quit (2026-11-05, #1785, issue 1781).
  A chat's field, a room's and the full editor share the code
  (ReturnKeyTextView.setFocusIntent), the field being dismantled included.

**Open gaps**
- Not yet seen on a device: a Mac and an iPad with a keyboard sending from
  the field and from the full editor, and which controls besides the
  transcript take focus from the field on a Mac. No test reaches
  `updateUIView` passing the binding's focus to the field (it needs a SwiftUI
  Context), so that link is checked on a device only.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1785 (focus changes after the update that asked, in every composer field, issue 1781); 2026-10-31, #1556 (an iPhone always lets go; rooms follow chats); 2026-10-30, #1527 (new entry).

## A chat's last reply

Reading the newest reply in a chat without opening it, from the open chat's
transcript or else its saved history.

**Siblings:** the Send to Hermes Shortcut ("Wait for Answer") · live voice
calls reading a job's chat · the Watch's answer to a call from Hermes

**Code**
- Reader: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (latestLiveVoiceThreadReply, latestLiveVoiceThreadReplyMessage, latestReplyTurn)
- Shortcut: `Conduit/Intents/SendToHermesIntent.swift` (ShortcutReply.mayBe), `Conduit/Services/AppState+ShortcutSend.swift`
- Live calls: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceBackgroundJobs.swift` (latestThreadReply)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ShortcutSendTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- Only the Shortcut has to tell a new reply from the one before it. Its row ids decide first, then the user's message each reply answers (this run's against another), and the wording last (2026-10-24, #1185).
- Voice calls and the Watch use only the reply's text (2026-10-24, #1185).

**Open gaps**
- The same message sent twice and answered in the same words, read once from saved history and once from the open chat, still can't be told apart.

**Checked:** 2026-11-01, #1631 (an answer to a question this socket never saw passes the call's chat and profile, for the gateway's own listener; see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-24, at #1185; a Shortcut send's failed try counted even when its text repeats the banner at #1191 (#1056 review).

## Following the latest message

Whether a transcript keeps itself at the newest message as replies and
events arrive, or stays where the user scrolled to read, and where a long
reply stops.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats and Bot Chat (one transcript) · group
rooms · a delegate agent's live tail sheet · the jump-to-latest button · how
much history an open transcript keeps · opening a chat with an unread reply ·
Settings > Chat's Long replies switch and captions (shared by Sync across
devices)

**Rulings**
- Only the user's own scroll leaves following, except a long reply's stop below. Being near the bottom (40 pt), the jump button or sending returns to it (TranscriptScroller, for chats and group rooms; group rooms 2026-10-24, #1184, on the transcript's scroller since 2026-10-31, #1590).
- Following keeps the end above the bar under it as the bar grows or shrinks: Predictive's chips, the plan dock or a call's bar coming and going. On iOS 26 only the scroll view's bottom inset changed then, which nothing reported, so the chips covered the reply's actions. The transcript takes the bars' heights, and the keyboard's, as its own insets, so the pass that applies a change pins in it, in the same animation when SwiftUI animates the change; a finger or fling on the chat holds the pin until it lets go, and whether a reader who lets go is near the bottom is measured against the bottom as it was when the finger came down. A reader browsing stays browsing; one a shrinking bar leaves past the new bottom is moved up to it, so no empty space shows (Michel, #1431; accepted by Eric 2026-10-28, #1455; the insets read in the pass that applies them since the transcript rewrite, 2026-10-31, #1577; Eric delegated the chat scroll's design to Claude, 2026-09-28, and approved the transcript rewrite's design, 2026-10-30).
- A reply longer than the screen stops at its start: following never pins past the user's message it answers, and once the reply runs on, the reader is left browsing there. On by default, switchable in Settings > Chat (Eric, 2026-10-25, #1256, notifier issue 365).
- The stop puts the user's message at the top, 37 pt below the viewport's top (where a new chat's first message sits), with the reply under it; a message taller than a third of the screen shows its last third. It was the bottom of the message (#1256), which scrolled the message away a line at a time as the reply reached the bottom, and with little room left kept the chat moving for a whole screen of reply (2026-10-29, issue 1436, #1509; the chat scroll's design is Claude's, 2026-09-28).
- A send, or a turn started on another device, makes room under the message: the transcript's content is at least the stop plus a screen tall, so the message moves to the top in one animated move once that room is laid out (none with Reduce Motion), and the reply streams into the room without moving anything. A short reply ends with empty room under it, as in Claude's and Gemini's apps. The room stays until the hold disarms (the jump button, the title tap, a jump to a question, a session switch, a reader below the reply's start), the reader scrolls away from it until none of it shows, or the next send, which lands in it and keeps it until the new message has a frame; while the content is no taller than the room, following holds the stop even if the room lags a pass behind a keyboard, a bar or a row shrinking. A send goes to the end before its message reaches the scroller, never to the last message's stop, so whichever arrives first the new message lands at the top. Switching Long replies off takes the room away at once. A reader who scrolls away from the room takes it away (nothing on screen moves: the content shrinks only below what they see), so coming back down ends at the reply's last row above the composer, not at the stop over empty room; the hold stays armed, so a reply still streaming is followed and stops at its start once it outgrows the screen. Switching Long replies off and on again afterwards doesn't bring that room back, nor does switching it on after a send made with it off: the reader has left it (2026-10-31, issue 1546, #1595; the chat scroll's design is Claude's). Group rooms, which share the switch, make no room: a room's send still goes to the end, and members' replies arrive whole and land at their top, so the Settings caption names chats for the move to the top. An unread chat opened at its reply makes no room: the reply is already there; it lands with the message at the top when the message is laid out, and with the reply's first row at the top when it isn't (2026-10-29, issue 1436, #1509).
- The stop never moves the offset up: a reader already below the reply's start (back at its end, or a reply that outgrew the screen before its message was laid out) follows on to the end. It holds at the turn's start, not the answer text, because a turn's steps fold and their summaries arrive below that point (2026-10-25, #1256).
- A refresh that brings the same messages from the other source (Hermes' stored rows, or a resume's) keeps the transcript's row ids. A resume row naming its stored row (`row_id`) has that row's id. Rows that still differ (a gateway with no `row_id` numbers resume rows by position) keep the ids the transcript drew them under, except where Hermes' stored ids come in at a turn's end, which win (Eric's ruling 2026-11-02, #1652: accepted rather than building an alias, since Hermes' own gateway sends `row_id` and the alias would touch the delivery checks; see Open gaps), paired by role, text and tool call when each list holds the message once, in order, and their times agree where both say one; a repeated text ("yes", "continue") keeps its own ids, since which copy is which can't be told, and the same text at another time is another message. A live turn's resume rows take the ids of the stored rows read with them the same way, so on such a gateway only the rows Hermes hasn't stored yet are drawn under positional ids (see Open gaps). The scroller takes a latest user message whose id changed, the old one gone and the text the same, for the same message and doesn't arm the stop for it, unless it's a send's own row (`local-`, a retry sending the same words) or its stored row id or time differs (a send's own row taken over by its stored row isn't compared by time: the phone's clock and Hermes' can differ). An optimistic row's id (`local-`) is never carried, and a kept row keeps its stored row id and measured step time. Re-keyed, every row was drawn and measured again from guesses, the reader's place was lost, and the latest user message looked new, arming the stop (2026-11-02, issue 1648, #1652). Compressing a chat (adoptCompressedTranscript) carries no ids: it rewrites the history, so its rows being drawn again is expected.
- What arms it: a send, a new user message from another device, and opening a chat that was unread, which lands at the start of its latest reply once its transcript is in. The jump button, the title tap, a jump to a question and a session switch disarm it (2026-10-25, #1256).
- A chat's row draws in a hosting controller of its own and inherits nothing from the chat: what it reads of the chat's environment reaches it through TranscriptCellEnvironment, and a change reaches the rows drawn in place, their content as it is. A sheet, popover or dialog a row presents stays up when its cell is given to another row: the row's controller waits aside, in the transcript, until it closes. While one is up, every cell given to another row puts its row's controller aside, the presenting row's or not: UIKit's presentedViewController answers for an ancestor's presentation too, so a row can't tell it presented. A key Conduit adds is copied there, or listed in its setInsideRows when the rows set it themselves, where they read it; CI's check-transcript-environment.py fails one that's neither, a listed one nothing in Conduit sets, and one copied or applied from another key's value. The check sees only that something in Conduit sets a listed key, not where, so a key set above the transcript is copied, never listed (2026-10-31, #1577, #1586, under the transcript rewrite's design, which Eric approved 2026-10-30).
- A group room is drawn by the chat's transcript and moved by its scroller, by the same rules. A following room stops at the first new member message's start, 37 pt below the top, where a chat's stop puts the user's message, and the reader is left browsing there once what came runs past the screen; the stop holds through the message measuring taller than its guess, a message arriving while a fling moves the room stops it once the fling rests, as a chat's hold waits for a finger, and a later member message stops at its own start. Anything else new (a caption, a member starting or ending its turn) is followed to the end, what draws nothing new at the end (a turn's heartbeat, the oldest rows trimmed) leaves the stop where it is, and the jump button, a send, Retry and a quoted message's jump end the stop. Switching Long replies off, here or on another device, takes a following room's stop away at once, as it takes a chat's room. A long message opened with Show all keeps the row tapped where it is, as a chat's rows do. Its rows are 18 pt apart with 18 pt margins, as a chat's, where the room's stack had 14 and 16 (2026-10-25, #1256; on the transcript since 2026-10-31, #1590, under the transcript rewrite's design, which Eric approved 2026-10-30).
- An open group room keeps a bounded tail: it opens on the last 200 events, and polling trims back to 200 once it holds 400 (2026-10-24, #1184).
- The delegate tail sheet always follows its end: it is a live log, not a reply to read (2026-10-25, #1256).
- Nothing rebuilds a transcript. Chats and group rooms each rebuilt a following lazy stack that laid out no row on screen (#887, #971, #1367, issue 1358) until the transcript rewrite: their collection view lays out every row crossing the screen, at its measured or estimated height, so the lazy stack's blank screen can't happen there (chats 2026-10-31, #1577; group rooms 2026-10-31, #1590; Eric delegated the chat scroll's design to Claude, 2026-09-28, and approved the transcript rewrite's design, 2026-10-30).
- The jump button, and the "Go to" pill that shares its spot, sit centered over the composer in chats and group rooms, so either thumb reaches them; they show only while the reader browses, so what they cover is about to scroll away (Eric, 2026-11-06, #1860: bottom right suited only a right hand). Both are overlays on the transcript's own area, never on the composer bar: a bar on iOS 26's safeAreaBar takes touches only inside its bounds, so a button drawn above it showed but its taps went to the transcript (group rooms from #1833 until #1915).

**Open gaps**
- Group rooms have no "Load earlier messages", so history above the 200-event tail isn't reachable in the app.
- The Responding row reads the kept tail, so a discussion longer than 200 events (when opened, or after a trim) can lose it while a member still works.
- Trimming a busy room's tail, once per 200 new events, takes away the rows of a reader scrolled up to the oldest ones, who is left on what's at their place then; a reader whose rows stay keeps them where they were.
- On a gateway whose resume rows carry no `row_id` (Hermes' own send it), some rows are still re-keyed: drawn and measured again, a reader anchored on them moved, the stop not armed by it. They are a live turn's rows Hermes hadn't stored when the chat was read (the turn's newest) and any repeated text, re-keyed once when the turn's stored rows arrive, because Hermes' stored ids win there: the delivery checks, the graft of a refreshed page onto older history and the merge of newer stored rows find rows by them. Keeping the drawn ids instead would need those to look rows up through an alias (the row's `rowId`). A `/btw` or slash note shown after such a row is anchored by the row's old id, so it moves to the end of the transcript then too (keepingLocalNotes). And a resume whose positional window moved by a row keeps its new positional ids, which then name other messages than before. Eric chose not to build the alias (2026-11-02, #1652).
- Opening an unread chat lands at the reply after its last user message, so one whose unread rows came without a new user message (a cron or background result after an already read reply) lands at that older reply, not at the newest row; a chat with no user message at all stays at the end.
- A chat restored on launch (Continue where you left off) keeps its saved place, unread or not.
- A group room that opens empty scrolls its first events to the end: that batch is usually the room's history arriving, which should open at its newest row, so only events after a row already seen land at a member message's start.

## A live reply while it can't be seen

A reply or thinking card streaming into the open chat redraws at stream
cadence only while it can be seen: the sessions drawer over the chat, or
Conduit in the background or inactive, pauses the live publishes, and what streamed
shows in one publish when the chat is seen again.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats, Bot Chat and Kanban workers' transcripts
(one ChatView, whose live rows are the only views that observe `liveTurn`) ·
the sessions drawer over the chat · Conduit in the background · Conduit inactive (the app switcher, Control Center; not on a Mac) · not needed:
group rooms (their messages arrive whole, nothing streams), voice modes,
CarPlay and the Watch (they hear the stream through the voice observers,
not the drawn text), the Live Activity (it reads the stream events), the
chat's saved copy and the reply's notification (the settled message)

**Code**
- Pausing and resuming: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (liveRowsHidden, sceneHidesLiveRows, pauseLivePublishes, resumeLivePublishesIfShown; showSidebar's didSet; handleScenePhase's .inactive, .background and .active; scheduleStreamingPublish and scheduleReasoningPublish); the projection, LiveTurnProjection
- The live rows: `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (ChatLiveStreamingRow, ChatLiveThinkingRow)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/AppStateReasoningStreamTests.swift` (testBackgroundHoldsLiveTextUntilActive, testInactiveHoldsLiveTextUntilActiveOffAMac, testBackgroundHoldsLiveReasoningUntilActive, testInactiveHoldsLiveReasoningUntilActiveOffAMac; the drawer's pause flushes the other tests)

**Rulings**
- The pause starts on `.inactive` on an iPhone or iPad (the app switcher, Control Center, a system alert), since a swipe away from the switcher asks Conduit to quit while the reply still redraws (Eric chose it, 2026-11-04, #1744); on an iPad app on a Mac only on `.background`, since it goes inactive whenever another app is in front, where the reply stays in view (#1743).
- In the background a streaming reply kept the main thread redrawing the whole growing reply on each publish, near a full core with tables, so iOS's watchdog killed Conduit going to the background or quitting (0x8BADF00D, 85% of the relay's crash reports; Time Profiler on a phone, 2026-11-04, #1743).
- A turn that completes while hidden still publishes its final text at once (scheduleStreamingCompletion), one publish (#1743).
- A thinking card's first words still mount it while hidden, one publish per card; the words after it wait (#1744, from #1743's review).

**Open gaps**
- If an iPad window that is on screen but not receiving events (Split View or Slide Over beside another app, Stage Manager) reports `.inactive`, its streaming reply waits until the window is touched or focused, then catches up at once; not checked on an iPad (#1744, from the reviews).
- The rest of the chat (the transcript's rows, the composer) still updates in the background on a turn's boundaries: a tool card or a settled message lands as it comes, which is one update each, not stream cadence.

**Checked:** 2026-11-04, #1744 (inactive pauses too, off a Mac); 2026-11-04, #1743 (the background pauses the live publishes as the drawer did).

## Reconnecting to Hermes

How the chat connection comes back after it drops, and when it tries at
once instead of waiting out its backoff.

**Siblings:** a socket that closed (handleDisconnect) · the network path
changing · someone waiting by voice (a call's request, CarPlay back on
screen) · CarPlay, locked, Watch and CallKit calls with the app in the
background · a failed sync's retry · a failed sign-in refresh or ticket's
retry and its banner · coming back to the app (the conversation header's
line and menu dot, the classic layout's status dot) · a message sent while
it reconnects · a tapped Reconnect · a Siri voice launch waiting on the
connection · the backoff
itself · the hidden dashboard page's failed load

**Code**
- Reconnects: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (handleDisconnect, scheduleReconnect, scheduleReconnectAfterFailedSync, reconnectForRetry's failed ticket, quietReconnectAttempts, isRecoveringConnection, networkPathChanged, reconnectNowForWaitingVoice, recoverTransportForCarPlayIfNeeded, handleCarPlaySceneWillEnterForeground, checkQuietTransportOffScreen, clientForVoiceRequest)
- A call's requests: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (voiceBackgroundJobSupervisor's backend), `Conduit/Services/AppState+SpokenApprovals.swift` (respondToApprovalByVoice, respondToClarifyByVoice)
- Network path: `Conduit/Services/PowerPolicy.swift` (pathSatisfied), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (networkPathChanged, the ping of an open socket, checkLiveness)
- Coming back to the app: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (beginQuietReturn, quietReturnWindow, hidesBriefReconnect), `Conduit/Services/AppState+PendingSend.swift` (sendWhenConnected ends the quiet), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ConversationScreen.swift` (V2ConnectionLine, V2ConversationMenu's dot), `Conduit/Views/RootView.swift` (ConnectionStatusIndicator, the classic layout's dot)
- Which renewal failures retry quietly: `Conduit/Voice/DictationClipStore.swift` (DictationUploadRetry.isTransient, shared with dictation uploads)
- A tapped Reconnect and a waiting Siri launch: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (reconnect, surfacesRenewalFailureAtOnce, quietReconnectFailureClass, quietRenewalFailures, the off-screen rule in retryQuietlyAfterFailedRenewal, reauthFailureRetriesQuietly, isHoldingQuietReconnectFailure in showsConnectionRepair, noteQuietRenewalFailure, connect(with:)'s isRenewal for the socket after a silent re-auth; quietReconnectFailure and quietRenewalFailures are cleared by lastConnectionFailure's didSet, so whatever forgets a failure forgets a quiet one), `Conduit/Voice/Wake/PendingVoiceLaunchPolicy.swift` (voiceLaunchConnectionSnapshot)
- Timing in Instruments: `Conduit/Services/ResponsivenessSignposts.swift` ("OAuth refresh" in `Conduit/Services/NativeOAuth.swift`, "Ticket mint" and "WebSocket connect" in AppState)
- The hidden dashboard page: `Conduit/Services/DashboardTicketBridge.swift` (waitUntilReady, mintCookieTicket, requestJSON; reads and the ticket skip it with a session cookie, see A connection's first reads)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ReconnectBackoffTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/CarPlayTransportRecoveryTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/HermesClientTests.swift` (the liveness check), `ConduitTests/DashboardTicketBridgeTests.swift` (testRequestOnAFailedPageReloadsIt, testConcurrentRequestsOnAFailedPageReloadItOnce, testRequestLeavesALoadInFlightAlone), `ConduitTests/AppStateChatResumeTests.swift` (testFailedTicketShowsItsBannerOnlyAfterTheQuietRetries, testQuietTicketFailureShowsWhenTheGatewayStopsAnswering, testTappedReconnectAndSiriSeeAFailedTicketAtOnce, testQuietTicketFailureSurfacesWhenTheLinkKeepsChanging, testAStaleMessageOffersNoRepairDuringTheQuietRetries, testOnlyANetworkCutReauthRetriesQuietly), `ConduitTests/OfflineChatCacheTests.swift` (testAMessageThatWaitsEndsTheQuietReturn), `ConduitTests/AppStateForegroundLifecycleTests.swift` (testLeavingWithAnOpenSocketHoldsItUntilTheAppIsBack), `ConduitTests/ConnectionRepairTests.swift` (testFailedReconnectRetainsTypedFailureUntilRecoverySucceeds: a tapped Reconnect's failure keeps its classification for Repair)

**Rulings**
- A reconnect that skips the backoff needs a usable network path: without one no attempt can work, and the path coming back reconnects at once anyway. A drop mid-reply and someone waiting by voice both check it (#1060; #846 follow-up, #1191).
- The network path changing reconnects at once without reading the path: it runs before the path monitor holds the new one, so a check there would stall recovery for the whole backoff (#1191).
- Someone waiting by voice skips the backoff but keeps its count, so one request after another against a gateway that is down doesn't reset it (#1060).
- The path change's ping of an open socket waits while a large frame (a picture) is still being written: its pings can't be answered in time and would close a working socket. A path that really died fails the write (2026-10-25, #1268).
- A call's request to Hermes made while Conduit is off screen (CarPlay, a locked phone, a Watch call, a call from Hermes; every voice mode, spoken approvals and answers included) first pings a socket that has been quiet 30 s, as the phone coming on screen does: iOS may have held Conduit suspended until the car or the call woke it, and a socket that died then still looks open. Starting, titling and cancelling a call's jobs count, and so does asking whether a chat is busy before its turn. One that doesn't answer in a keepalive ping's 10 s (a relayed path can be slow off screen without being dead) is closed and the request waits for the reconnect, as after any drop. Before, GPT-Live started from CarPlay ran (it starts over HTTP) while every request it handed Hermes waited on the dead socket until it timed out (2026-10-27, #1382, from #1362).
- The hidden dashboard page comes back with the next dashboard request, not only with the next ticket: any request (chat history, status, a ticket) reloads a page whose load failed, and one still loading is waited for, never restarted. A request that stalled across a Wi-Fi change marks the page failed while the socket stays open, and an open socket mints no ticket, so before, every history and status read was refused with "still connecting to your dashboard" until the app quit (2026-10-30, #1526, issue 1412). With a session cookie, reads and the ticket no longer go through the page (see A connection's first reads), so on such a dashboard the page is used only by a write, a ticket refused as signed out (which reloads it and retries) and a read refused as signed out (which waits for it to be ready, reloading only a failed load); a dashboard with no cookie yet goes through it as above (2026-11-02, Eric picked skipping the page after the startup lag audit; #1663).
- Reconnecting stays out of sight while it works: coming back to the app, the header's "Reconnecting…" line waits 10 s (was 3 s, #296) and the menu's dot stays grey, long enough for a sign-in refresh, a ticket and the socket over a slow remote link; a message sent meanwhile ends the wait so its delay is explained, and no network at all says so at once. A failed sign-in refresh or ticket, or a silent re-auth with the saved password that the network cut off, or the socket after a silent re-auth that worked (a sign-in the server refused still asks to sign in), retries quietly like a failed socket and shows "Failed to refresh the dashboard session", and the classified failure that offers Repair, only once three retries have failed, when the status says the dashboard looks down, whether the last one asked for a ticket or found the gateway not answering its readiness probe (Repair never shows while the first attempts are quiet); a refused sign-in still asks to sign in. The count is of renewals failed since the last one worked, so a link that keeps changing (which restarts the backoff) still gets there. Off screen (CarPlay, a call with the app in the background or the phone locked, the Watch) a failed renewal shows at once, as before, since the quiet is for coming back to the app; a failed sync's retry and the hidden page's failed load are unchanged. An older, unrelated message left on screen offers no Repair while a failure is kept quiet. A re-auth the server answered, a 5xx included, asks to sign in as before; only one the network cut off retries quietly. A Reconnect someone or something asked for (anything that calls reconnect: the button, Settings, a gateway restart, a profile switch, a plugin update) still shows its failure at once, and a waiting Siri voice launch still fails at once on a quiet failure, as before. Others feel faster because they reconnect without saying so (Eric 2026-11-01, #1628, issue 1624). Refreshing the OAuth token ahead of time was declined: on becoming active the ticket waits on it anyway, and on suspending, a rotated grant iOS suspends before it's saved signs the user out.

**Open gaps**
- `recoverTransportForCarPlayIfNeeded(immediately:)` still reconnects at once without a path check (CarPlay connecting only).

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1666 (a Repair test still expected a resume's failed ticket to show at once, which #1628 made quiet; it now taps Reconnect, which shows it at once); 2026-11-02, #1663 (the ticket and reads go out without the hidden page when a session cookie is held, so its failed load holds up only writes and a dashboard with no cookie yet; see A connection's first reads); 2026-11-01, #1631 (a call's spoken answers pass their chat and profile, which the gateway's own listener reads an unseen question from; see Two Hermes servers); 2026-11-01, #1628 (reconnecting kept quiet on return, the ticket banner after the quiet retries, signposts); 2026-10-30, #1526 (the hidden page reloads a failed load on any request); 2026-10-28, #1452 (a drop on a socket handed on at a profile switch reaches the client holding it); 2026-10-27, #1382 (a call's request off screen checks a quiet socket first); 2026-10-25, at #1268; 2026-10-24, at #1191.

## Native sign-in browser

The browser a native (PKCE) dashboard sign-in opens in, and the Private
sign-in page switch that makes it start fresh.

**Siblings:** the sign-in screen's Advanced card (Add a dashboard) ·
Repair's Sign In to Reconnect · Settings' Sign In Again · the saved
dashboards screen · the switch's captions in 13 languages · the embedded
browser sign-in (AuthWebView, a different flow) · the bot MCP sign-in
browser (separate)

**Code**
- Browser and setting: `Conduit/Services/NativeOAuth.swift` (NativeOAuthBrowserPreference, NativeOAuthSignInSheet, WebAuthenticationPresenterViewController, NativeOAuthLoginModel.run)
- The switch: `Conduit/Views/Login/LoginScreens.swift` (PrivateSignInPageToggle, advancedFields)
- Error shown when the page fails: `Conduit/Services/ConnectionFailure.swift` (ConnectionFailure.signInPageFailed, ConnectionFailureClassifier.classify), `Conduit/Services/ConnectionSetupFlow.swift` (repairPath: a failed page goes to the staged test)
- Repair and Sign In Again: `Conduit/Views/ConnectionSetupForm.swift` (repairReviewFooter, settingsSignInAgain), `Conduit/Views/ConnectionSetupView.swift` (repairSignInSheet), `Conduit/Services/ConnectionRepair.swift` (ConnectionRepairSignIn.mayOpenNativeSignIn, showsPrivateSignInSwitch)
- Saved dashboards screen: `Conduit/Views/Login/LoginScreens.swift` (LoginDashboardsScreen.mayOpenSignInPage)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ConnectionRepairTests.swift` (testPrivateSignInSwitchShowsOnlyWhereSignInCanBeNative, testRepairRoutingStartsNearTheClassifiedProblem), `ConduitTests/ConnectionFailureTests.swift` (testNativeSignInBrowserFailureClassifiesAsSignInPageFailed, testNativeSignInFailuresNeverClaimBadCredentials)
- Embedded browser sign-in: `Conduit/Views/LoginView.swift` (AuthWebView)
- Bot MCP sign-in, its own browser: `Conduit/Views/BotCapabilitiesView.swift` (BotMcpBrowserView)

**Rulings**
- A native sign-in that opens the sign-in page opens it in an ASWebAuthenticationSession, not ephemeral by default, so the provider's page can remember the account between sign-ins. iOS asks "Conduit wants to use … to sign in" before a non-ephemeral session opens. Hermes accepts only a loopback redirect, so the code still arrives through the loopback listener and Conduit closes the browser itself (2026-10-26, #1329).
- Private sign-in page makes each new browser session ephemeral, so a sign-in that opens the page shows every way the provider offers (a login code as well as a passkey) and can pick another account. It doesn't skip a saved grant: NativeOAuthLoginModel.run signs in with one without opening the page (2026-10-26, #1329).
- The switch, with the caption for its setting inside its label, shows only where a native sign-in can start: the sign-in screen's Advanced card; Repair's Sign In to Reconnect and Settings' Sign In Again when the test's sign-in is native or a choice the capability check may still send to Safari, never when it is the embedded browser, which doesn't read it; and the saved dashboards screen while a row signs in without a saved password, since that row's discovery decides native or embedded browser on the tap (a list of password dashboards never shows it). Each place has its own accessibility identifier (2026-10-27, #1329, Eric).
- A browser that fails or doesn't start reports "The sign-in page couldn’t open" through the sheet's error; only the user closing it is a cancellation, and a closed browser never reopens. Repair's Sign In to Reconnect and Settings' Sign In Again classify it as ConnectionFailure.signInPageFailed and show that message above their sign-in button, not the generic connection failure. Their other native sign-in failures classify too: an HTTP status as at provider discovery (a 401 or 403 is never bad credentials), a malformed answer as an unexpected response (2026-10-27, #1329, #1343).

**Open gaps**
- To switch accounts on a dashboard with a saved grant, sign out first; the switch alone keeps the grant.
- Whether the session shares MobileSafari's own sign-in depends on iOS; in simulator testing with Pocket ID it kept only its own session.

**Checked:** 2026-10-27, at #1343, carrying #1329.

## Native OAuth token transport

The requests a native (PKCE) sign-in's tokens make: the code exchange, the
refresh, and the bearer requests and tickets after it, and what happens to
them when the dashboard's session is torn down.

**Siblings:** the dashboard's request authorizer (DashboardRequestAuthorizer,
the one owner that invalidates it) · not needed: the password sign-in client
(NativeAuthClient invalidates its URLSession only in deinit), HermesClient's
socket (invalidate() drops its session, so nothing reuses it), sign-out and
the certificate check (each invalidates a session of its own, in a defer)

**Code**
- `Conduit/Services/NativeOAuth.swift` (NativeOAuthAPIClient: invalidate, bytes(for:), tokenRequest, requestJSON; NativeOAuthSession: invalidate, refresh, requestJSON)
- Owner: `Conduit/Services/DashboardRequestAuthorizer.swift` (invalidate)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/NativeOAuthTests.swift` (testAClientInvalidatedBeforeARefreshStartsCancelsItWithoutRaising, testInvalidatedSessionCannotTouchReplacementTokens)

**Rulings**
- An invalidated session ends its requests as cancelled, never as a sign-in failure, and never touches the Keychain grant that replaced it.
- The client's URLSession is invalidated only in deinit. invalidate() marks the client invalidated and cancels its tasks, and a request after that fails with URLError(.cancelled) before it reaches the URLSession. A refresh Task that started after its session was invalidated (cancellation is cooperative) used to make a task on the invalidated URLSession, which raises an Objective-C exception: seven aborts in tokenRequest on builds 223 and 244 (2026-11-04, #1737).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-04, #1737 (an invalidated client cancels instead of raising).

## Dashboard sign-in redirects

When an auth proxy in front of the dashboard (an oauth2-proxy-style edge,
a Cloudflare Access gate) sends a dashboard request to sign in instead.

**Siblings:** the hidden dashboard page · requests sent without it
(background requests, file downloads, and on screen the ticket and reads
with a session cookie, see A connection's first reads) · the background session's
redirect rule · the dashboard socket's handshake · the login screen's
signed-in check

**Code**
- The decision: `Conduit/Services/DashboardSignInRedirect.swift` (isSignIn, redirectIsSignIn, isSignInPath)
- Page: `Conduit/Services/DashboardTicketBridge.swift`
- Requests: `Conduit/Services/DashboardBackgroundRequests.swift` (the redirect rule and a returned redirect), `Conduit/Services/DashboardFileDownload.swift`
- Socket: `Conduit/Services/DashboardWebSocketSession.swift` (DashboardSocketHandshakeError.failure)
- Login: `Conduit/Views/LoginView.swift` (isSignedInDashboardPage)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/DashboardProxySignOutTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- One decision for the page, the requests and the socket: any web address on another origin is sign-in, and on the dashboard's own origin only a sign-in page is (#731 follow-up, #1191).
- The dashboard's own host moving from http to https, on https's port or the dashboard's own, counts as its own origin; another port on that host is another origin (#1191).
- A handshake redirect is never followed, so the ticket never goes along.

**Open gaps**
- The background session's redirect rule and the login screen's signed-in check compare origins strictly, without the http to https allowance: such a redirect comes back as the response (and is judged by isSignIn there), and the login screen with a dashboard saved on http behind a TLS edge hasn't been checked.
- The hidden page doesn't follow that upgrade either: its navigation policy cancels an http to https move to an ordinary page as a failed load (no longer as sign-in), so a dashboard behind a TLS-forcing edge must be saved on https. Following it would take the page's landing and script-message checks and the socket off the saved origin, so it was left as is (#1191 review).

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1663 (on screen the ticket and reads with a session cookie go without the page, so the requests' redirect rule decides for them too; the rule itself is unchanged); 2026-10-30, #1526 (any request, not only a ticket, reloads a page whose load failed, so a reload that lands on sign-in now reaches a history or status read as sign-in required, where it got "still connecting" before); 2026-10-26, #1247 (the hidden page's deinit removes its script handler on the main actor); 2026-10-24, at #1191.

## A connection's first reads

What a launch, a return or a profile switch reads from the dashboard
before the chat list and the open chat are current: the ticket for the
socket, the profile list, the chat list's newest page and the display
settings, and which of them wait for what.

**Siblings:** the ticket (a launch, a return, a reconnect, a profile
switch) · the socket's upgrade, which already sent the page's cookies
natively · the profile list · the chat list's newest page · the display
settings (thinking, tool progress, reviews, the time zone) · reads and
writes from every other screen through the same bridge · requests while
the phone app is in the background (CarPlay, a locked phone, the Watch)
· native OAuth sign-ins, which never used the page · the hidden dashboard
page (sign-in landings, its failed load, see Reconnecting to Hermes and
Dashboard sign-in redirects) · the Connection timeline in Diagnostics &
logs (not needed: the steps keep their names, and the ticket and reads now
show shorter)

**Code**
- Reads and the ticket without the page: `Conduit/Services/DashboardTicketBridge.swift` (readsWithoutThePageFirst, mintCookieTicket, sendJSON, writesSent), `Conduit/Services/DashboardBackgroundRequests.swift` (requestJSONWithoutPage, readWithoutPage, cookiesForRequestsWithoutPage)
- Sent as the connection starts: `Conduit/Services/StartupReads.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (sendStartupReads and startupReadFence, called from mintChatResumeTicket and connect; taken in readProfiles, dashboardSessions and loadProfileDisplayPreferences)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/DashboardTicketBridgeTests+Foreground.swift`, `ConduitTests/ProfileDiscoveryTests.swift` (reads landing out of order)

**Rulings**
- With a saved dashboard's session cookie, reads and the ticket go out natively with the page's cookies even while the page can run, as the socket's upgrade already did, so a launch doesn't wait for WebKit and the page's load, and an answer isn't copied through a script on the main actor. With no cookie in any store yet (just after a browser sign-in, before WebKit hands it over), or when a native read or ticket is refused as signed out (a store's cookie may be older than the page's), they go through the page as before: a ticket with its reload and retries, a read once the page is ready, so one native 401 never ends a session. A native ticket that's never answered (a stalled link) goes on to the page's retries too; a read that fails that way is read again once by its step. On screen a request waits at most 0.5 s for WebKit's cookie store when the mirror already holds a cookie (the store answers in milliseconds there); off screen, or with no mirrored cookie, up to 2 s. Writes keep the page while it runs, so a dashboard switch still leaves one waiting for its answer. A bridge built before its dashboard is saved (the login screen) keeps the page, since it shares the default stores (2026-11-02, Eric picked the fixes from the startup lag audit; #1663).
- The profile list, the chat list's newest page and the display settings go out with the ticket instead of each after the step before; on a profile switch they are the new profile's chat list and display settings (a switch doesn't read the profile list). Each step takes the early answer once, only through the same bridge, within 20 s, and only while nothing changed since it was sent: no write through the dashboard started or ended (one still out when the reads went counts), no chat removed from the kept chat list, no display setting saved (a time-zone save is a write, so it voids the early settings read too; one landing while a settings read is out keeps that read's older zone off the screen, and a display save doesn't stop the read setting the zone), and for the chat list no newer listing committed by another load. Writes over the socket (a new bot, say) aren't counted; the window is the connect itself, and the profile list read after a new bot comes after it. A ticket isn't a write: one minted through the page leaves the reads sent with it usable. A new chat shown while its listing is awaited is merged in by the catalog as before. Otherwise, or when the early read failed for any reason (no cookie yet, refused as signed out, a dropped request), the step reads again once its own way. An early read never goes through the page, and a replaced bridge cancels the early reads still out. The early answers are the connection's own steps': once the restore, connect, reconnect or profile switch that sent them ends, whatever is left is dropped, so a pull to refresh or the profile list read after a new bot always reads fresh (#1663). A forced refresh during the connect itself may take the early page, which is seconds old and what the connect's own read would return; accepted rather than threading the flag through.
- Two profile list reads, or two display settings reads, through the same bridge can land out of order (one native, one through the page or read again after a failed native try). An answer whose read was sent before one already taken never commits (a newer read that failed, or a profile list that came back empty, isn't taken, so it leaves the commit to the older one): an older profile list can't bring back a deleted bot, drop one just made, or re-home the profile in use, and an older settings read, answered or failed, can't put back older settings or zone. Order is when each step asked, as for the chat list's read tickets; a read held in its cookie lookup can leave after a later one, a window left open (2026-11-02, from an outside audit Eric asked to validate; #1668).
- No plugin route bundles the first reads: sent together they already cost one round trip, and a route in the plugin would wait for a non-default profile's plugin host to start (2 to 2.6 s on its first request, #1442), so it was left out (2026-11-02, after reading Hermes' plugin hosts; Eric had picked it and was told why in the audit thread; #1663).

**Open gaps**
- The cron runs list, the archived calls and the Bot roster and busy mode (socket calls) still go out when their steps reach them.
- The resume still waits for the chat list, which decides whether the stored chat is still there (#1452's held-back step).

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1668 (an older profile list or display settings read landing after a newer one doesn't commit; the profile list's other readers, a new, copied or deleted bot and a linked chat's profile check, read through the same fence); 2026-11-02, #1665: a time-zone save landing while the settings read is out no longer puts the older zone back, counted apart from display saves so one doesn't cost the other; #1663 (added: reads and the ticket without the page, and the first reads sent with the ticket).

## Conduit tools in Hermes' tool catalog

Hermes defers every plugin tool behind Tool Search. The model sees a catalog
with one line per tool, the first sentence of its description cut at
Hermes' cap (80 characters), and decides from that line whether Conduit can
do what it's asked.

**Siblings:** every tool the notifier registers (toolsets `conduit` and
`conduit_rooms`: calls and call watches, calendar, phone, contacts, health,
location, maps, inbox, notify, present, show, settings, rooms, Linked people
and the Bot workstreams' `work_*` tools) · live calls' host tools, which
read the same descriptions from `/voice-tools` · the skills the descriptions
point to and the notifier README

**Code**
- Descriptions: `notifier/call_tool.py`, `notifier/call_watches.py`, `notifier/phone_tool.py`, `notifier/health_tool.py`, `notifier/location_tool.py` (voice_description too), `notifier/maps_tool.py`, `notifier/inbox_tool.py`, `notifier/notify_tool.py`, `notifier/present_tool.py`, `notifier/show_tool.py`, `notifier/settings_tool.py`, `notifier/room_tool.py`, `notifier/room_asks.py`, `notifier/room_free_busy.py`, `notifier/link_ask_tool.py`, `notifier/work_tool.py`
- Where the call tools' text continues: `notifier/skills/calling-the-user/SKILL.md`, `notifier/README.md` (Calls from Hermes)
- Check: `notifier/upstream/test_tool_catalog.py` (every tool's line, through Hermes' own `_short_desc`, against a real Hermes)

**Rulings**
- Each tool's description opens with one sentence that says what the tool does (its verbs: call, add, set, read) and fits Hermes' cap, so the catalog shows it whole; the details follow. Hermes asks the same of its own tools (2026-11-03, #1709, notifier #525, issue 177).

**Open gaps**
- When the catalog is over Hermes' budget (4,000 tokens, or 5% of a small context) with many MCP tools, Hermes lists names only, or collapses the largest group to a count, so these lines go unseen and the model has to search. Not handled: nothing the plugin can set (#1709).

**Checked:** 2026-11-03, #1709 (seeded: emory's Classic call on issue 177 said it couldn't call; notifier #525).
