install sheet (its Runs line shows arguments the same way) · a connector's
sign-in (the phone's callback, shared with Edit Bot's) and a catalog
connector's key on its page (Edit Bot's MCP keys stay on `mcp.servers.set_api_key`) · Edit Bot's kept MCP page (a sign-in here opens it signed in) · the Capabilities
captions ("Changes apply to new sessions."; the editor's footers) ·
README.md's Capabilities line

**Code**
- Installed lists and switches: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (loadCapabilities, toggleSkill, toggleToolset, keepFlip, showKeptCapabilities, capabilitiesAreKept, canChangeCapabilities, capabilityLoadGeneration, capabilitiesOwner, currentCapabilitiesOwner, capabilitiesAreCurrent, capabilityRowsAreCurrent, retireCapabilitySnapshot, CapabilitySnapshotOwner, CapabilityDetailScope, CapabilityLoadPolicy), `Conduit/Services/CapabilityToggleWrites.swift` (Outcome's taken)
- The rest of the page: `Conduit/Services/CapabilitiesStore.swift` (configure, serves, showsKept, probe, probeServers)
- Views: `Conduit/Views/CapabilitiesView.swift`, `Conduit/Views/Capabilities/CapabilitySkillsTab.swift`, `Conduit/Views/Capabilities/CapabilityToolsTab.swift`, `Conduit/Views/Kanban/KanbanTaskComposerView.swift` (KanbanSkillsPickerSheet)
- Connectors tab: `Conduit/Views/Capabilities/CapabilityConnectorsTab.swift` (CapabilityConnectorsTab's tests, ConnectorDetailPage, its first test waiting for Hermes' list when the kept one shows)
- Editing a connector: `Conduit/Models/CapabilityCatalogModels.swift` (ConnectorServerEdit, ConnectorServer.saved, ConnectorServer.argumentText, used by ConnectorServer.list and ConnectorCatalogEntry.list), `Conduit/Services/CapabilitiesStore.swift` (serverConfig, saveServer), `Conduit/Views/Capabilities/CapabilityConnectorsTab.swift` (ConnectorDetailPage, ConnectorEditSheet)
- Connector sign-in and keys: `Conduit/Services/NativeMCPSignIn.swift` (shared with Edit Bot), `Conduit/Views/Capabilities/CapabilityConnectorsTab.swift` (ConnectorDetailPage.signIn, ConnectorKeysSection), `Conduit/Services/CapabilitiesStore.swift` (setConnectorKeys, testAfterKeySave), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (keepMcpSignedIn)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/KanbanTests+Capabilities.swift`, `ConduitTests/KanbanTests.swift` (CapabilityLoadPolicy), `ConduitTests/AppStateMultiDashboardTests.swift` (testCapabilitiesOpenOnTheSkillsAndToolsetsHermesGaveLastTime), `ConduitTests/NativeMCPSignInTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- A list read that started before a switch was flipped commits nothing, in AppState and in CapabilitiesStore alike (#867; AppState's lists at #1191).
- The lists open on the copy kept on the phone (Screens that open on their last answer). A switch Hermes took is kept in it, over any read asked before it, and one it refused never is, a flip a newer one replaced (which reports no failure) included; one flipped on a kept list, taken or refused, reads the lists again, since the read on its way no longer commits, and the bulk switches wait for Hermes' answer. Offline, where only the kept lists show, the switches and the bulk switches are off until a dashboard connects, since a flip has nowhere to go (#1569).
- Switches reach Hermes one after another in the order flipped, since each rewrites one config.yaml. A failed write puts back what Hermes last confirmed only when no newer flip of that switch is on its way, and a flip a newer one replaced reports no failure (#868 follow-up, #1191).
- The installed lists belong to a dashboard, its bridge and a profile, not a profile name: two dashboards can both have "default". Another dashboard's rows never show, act or seed a picker, a dashboard switch clears them, and Turn All On/Off stops once the list it started from isn't the one showing, and a pushed detail page reads its skill or toolset again once Capabilities points at the new dashboard and profile; a catalog skill's page keeps to the one it was opened for and shows only its name and description after a switch (2026-10-24, #1005, #1219; Eric approved the #1005 fixes).
- Switches, the store's other config-changing writes and the bot editor's writes wait their turn with every other profile config save (Profile config saves), so a settings GET→PUT can't put a flip back (2026-10-24, #1222).
- A connector test runs to its answer once sent, even when the list or page that started it goes away (opening a server from the list cancels the list's tests), and leaving the list starts no more. A test cancelled under it (the dashboard gone) records nothing, so it's tested again rather than shown as "interrupted"; the server page then says it's untested (Eric asked for issue 1570's fix, 2026-10-31, #1574).
- A connector is edited where it lives: the profile's `mcp_servers` in config.yaml, read with `include_defaults=false` so `${NAME}` key references stay references and keys stay in .env. The form changes the name, address, command and arguments and keeps every other key; an argument line left as it was keeps its value, and a whole number typed in place of a number argument stays a number (other text, "007" or "1.10" included, is saved as typed). The JSON is the whole entry. Saving reads the map again and writes it back whole (`PUT /api/mcp/servers`, Desktop's mcp.json save) in one turn of the config queue, so the other servers go back as the host had them a moment before (a Desktop or terminal write landing between those two requests is still overwritten, Profile config saves' open gap); both go to the dashboard and profile the editor opened on, and after a switch nothing is written and the editor says so. A server the host changed while the editor was open is refused rather than overwritten, and a test of the old entry still running is run again on the saved one. When the list can't be read again after a save, the saved server is shown from its entry alone (a key it leaves out is the default), so a renamed page doesn't say it's gone and the re-test follows the saved on/off. The server page, the saved row, the editor and a catalog connector's install sheet show number arguments as written and true/false as words (Eric asked for #1574's review gaps closed, 2026-10-31, #1578). A rename that would take another server's name is refused, an OAuth server's rename says it signs out (Hermes keeps tokens by name), a plugin's server has no Edit, and a Hermes without the route says to update (Eric asked for editing 2026-10-31, #1574, issue 1570).

- A connector signs in the way Edit Bot's MCP servers do: Hermes' `mcp.servers.oauth.*` with the phone's own loopback as `client_redirect_uri`, in Conduit's Safari view, never the dashboard's callback, which providers such as Lovable refuse. The flow keeps the server, profile and Hermes it started on; a switch, leaving the page or Done stops it and cancels Hermes' flow (NolanGarrett's #1634, carried as #1640). A sign-in Hermes took there is kept for Edit Bot's MCP page too, which opens on it signed in (`keepMcpSignedIn`, shared with Edit Bot).
- A catalog connector that signs in with keys (`auth_type: api_key`) sets or replaces them on its page. They go to the profile's `.env` through `/api/env`, only the variables its entry declares, and the config, which already reads them as `${VAR}`, isn't touched; keys are never shown or kept on the phone. A custom server's keys stay in Edit Server's JSON. Edit Bot's MCP add keeps `mcp.servers.set_api_key`: it runs on the gateway, where that RPC is, while this page runs on the dashboard's routes; both end in the same `.env` variable. A switch of dashboard or profile since Save was pressed, or mid-save, stops the keys left; a key Hermes took clears its field, so after a save that failed part way the field still filled is the one not saved; as with Edit Server's save, the list is read again from the host as the save ends and the server is tested only if that read says it's on (a switch turned on another device meanwhile counts; a read that fails or is overtaken tests nothing, and the server shows as untested rather than keeping the old key's result), and a test already running reruns on the saved key, a save that failed part way included (a save that took no key tests nothing). These are Edit Server's rulings, which Eric asked for in #1574 (a server turned off isn't tested; a test of the old entry still running is run again on the saved one); #1640 applied the first to the key save, and #1647 applies both. Eric decided the key save follows them (2026-11-02, recorded in #1655).

**Open gaps**
- Whether a list read can overwrite a flip in the bot editor's lists hasn't been checked.
- The Kanban skill picker says "No skills match." when it withholds another dashboard's skills, the same as a search miss.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1793 (the Skills, Tools and MCP page and Kanban's skills sheet built from Settings' cards, see Sheets in Settings' look); 2026-11-02, #1655 (Eric decided the key save follows Edit Server's test rules); 2026-11-02, #1647 (a key save reads the list again and tests the server only if the host says it's on, and a test running on the old key runs again, as after Edit Server's save; a save that fails part way does both for the keys Hermes took); 2026-11-02, #1640 (connectors sign in through the phone's callback with Edit Bot's flow; a catalog connector's key set from its page); 2026-10-31, #1578 (edited number arguments stay numbers; a renamed server shows after a failed reload); 2026-10-31, #1569 (the lists open on their kept copy and a switch Hermes took is kept in it, never one it refused; offline the switches wait for a dashboard; AppState's list reads are tested through held dashboard requests, its generation guard included, closing a gap; with #1574 merged in, a server's page waits for Hermes' list before its first test and a connector edit counts as a change, see Screens that open on their last answer); 2026-10-31, #1574 (connector tests outlive the page that started them; Edit Server); 2026-10-24, at #1219 and #1222.

## Reply progress signals

Everything that reacts to a turn's output as it arrives: the agent's text,
and its commentary between tool calls (`message.interim`).

**Siblings:** the compaction spinner's release · the Live Activity's writing
state · a call's background jobs (follow-up, status, session) · Local Live's
writing-again · the writing haptic · Classic speech (phone, CarPlay and calls
from Hermes: commentary is said, see Acknowledging work handed to Hermes) ·
saved chat history (the shared message normalizer)

**Code**
- Events: `Conduit/Services/StreamEventParser.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (handleStreamEvent, the compaction release)
- Saved chat history: `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (MessageNormalizer.normalizeMessages: explicit display_reasoning, even empty, wins over raw reasoning; approved display_commentary strings become ordered assistant rows without changing canonical answers or tool IDs). Regression tests: `ConduitTests/MessageNormalizerTests.swift`. Hermes adds these fields to Codex replies' rows (Hermes' history commentary projection, since 0.21, which Desktop also reads); a server without them keeps the raw reasoning. Read last reply and a call's resume history read the same rows, so they see the notes as they would live. This does not replay live events or voice notifications.
- Live Activity: `Conduit/Services/LiveTurnActivities.swift`
- Calls: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceBackgroundJobs.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/LocalLive/LocalLiveTurnRunner.swift`
- Haptics: `Conduit/Services/Haptics.swift` (signal)
- Classic: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceTypes.swift` (VoiceAssistantEvent), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (interim/completion voice notifications), `Conduit/Voice/VoiceConversationController.swift` (speech-segment boundaries)

**Rulings**
- Commentary between tool calls is the agent writing, wherever its text is: it releases a compaction claim, shows as writing and moves a call's job along (#912 follow-up, #1191). Classic says it aloud, as Hermes' acknowledgement; nothing else speaks it (Eric 2026-10-27, #1390).

**Open gaps**
- `Haptics.signal` still plays the writing haptic only for `message.delta`.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1899 (saved history reads Hermes' display_reasoning and display_commentary, so a reopened chat shows progress notes as their own rows like live; carried from #1897); 2026-11-06, #1891 (no Live Activity on a Mac, so no writing state there; see Live Activity for a running turn); 2026-11-01, #1631 (an answer to a question this socket never saw passes the call's chat and profile, for the gateway's own listener; see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-28, #1449 (Local Live's screen shows a reply's attached files, even beside a card); 2026-10-28, #1430 (Local Live's spoken stream passes the action filter; its writing state is unchanged); 2026-10-27, #1390 (Classic speaks commentary, carried from #1384); 2026-10-27, #1374 (the Live Activity's registration only; its writing state is unchanged); 2026-10-24, at #1191.

## Live Activity for a running turn

The Lock Screen and Dynamic Island card for a turn Conduit sent: started when
the prompt is accepted, kept current from the chat's stream while Conduit
runs and by the Conduit plugin through the push relay once it doesn't, and
ended when the turn ends.

**Siblings:** the stream's states (LiveTurnProgress) · the live registry check
when Conduit is back (reconcile) · the card's push token, registered with the
relay · the plugin's reporter (phases, tool categories, context, ends) · the
relay's route, which turns reports into Live Activity pushes · the widget's
Lock Screen and Dynamic Island views · Settings > Notifications > Progress on
the Lock Screen · a tap on the card, which opens the chat · the plugin's
CHANGELOG · Conduit on a Mac, which has none of it

**Code**
- App: `Conduit/Services/LiveTurnActivities.swift` (turnStarted, observe, reconcile, register, registerUnregistered), `Conduit/Services/PushNotificationService.swift` (registerLiveActivity), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (the turnStarted call, liveTurnActivitiesRegistrySnapshot)
- Widget: `Shared/Widgets/HermesTurnActivity.swift`, `ConduitWidgets/HermesTurnLiveActivity.swift`
- Settings: `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (NotificationsSettingsDetail, the Lock Screen section)
- Linking: `project.yml` (ActivityKit weak in Conduit and ConduitWidgets), held by `scripts/check-weak-imports.py` (WEAK_FRAMEWORKS) in the Smoke job
- Notifier: `notifier/live_activity.py` (the reporter, compacted_from), `notifier/__init__.py` (the hooks that feed it), `notifier/relay/src/live-activities.mjs`, `notifier/relay/src/server.mjs`

**Rulings**
- Only a phase, a tool category from a fixed list, a tool count and a context percentage cross the relay; the chat's title stays on the phone (#605, notifier #111).
- A turn's end reaches its card three ways: the stream while Conduit runs, the plugin through the relay, and the live registry once Conduit is back. The relay keeps an end reported before the phone registered the card, and ends a card registered later if it started before that end, never the chat's next turn's (2026-10-27, issue #1361, #1374, notifier #421).
- A turn that a compaction moves to a new session id reports and ends under the id the card was registered with (2026-10-27, #1374, notifier #421).
- A fork of the chat (Predictions' `/predict`, step summaries' /btw, the self-improvement review) never starts, moves or ends its card, even on a Hermes that runs plugin hooks for forks (2026-10-29, #1495 carrying #1489, notifier #464 carrying #462; see Notifications).
- The card's registration runs as a background task, so it finishes when Conduit leaves the screen right after sending, and one that didn't reach the relay is sent again when Conduit is next on screen (2026-10-27, #1374).
- On a Mac there is no card: `LiveTurnActivities.shared` is nil there, so nothing starts, adopts or ends one and Settings shows no Lock Screen section. ActivityKit is weak-linked (in the widget extension too), because macOS 14 has none for iPhone and iPad apps and every build that linked it strongly stopped at launch on Sonoma; nothing may touch it on a Mac (2026-11-06, #1891, issue 1877).

**Open gaps**
- The relay keeps registrations and unwatched ends in memory: a relay restart during a turn leaves its card to Conduit's next time on screen, or to iOS's 8 hours.
- The live registry check reads the profile and dashboard on screen, so a card from another one ends only by push.
- The widget bundle still lists the Live Activity on a Mac: `WidgetBundleBuilder` takes no runtime `if` (#1891's try didn't compile), so whether the launcher widgets load on macOS 14 is untried.
- The registration and its retry go through `URLSession.shared`, so only their decisions (`needsRegistration`, `liveActivityStartedAgo`, `liveActivityRouteExists`) are tested.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1891 (no card on a Mac and ActivityKit weak-linked, issue 1877; the relay, the plugin's reporter and the card's views needed no change); 2026-10-29, #1495, carrying #1489 (a chat's fork never touches the card, notifier #464); 2026-10-27, #1374.

## Model lists that fail to load

What a model picker shows before Hermes's model catalog has rows: still
loading, a fetch that failed, or a gateway that lists no models.

**Siblings:** a provider's page in Models & providers (done: its models can be picked once the catalog answers) · the model sheet · the Model page's Default model, Delegate
model and Fallback models editors · a bot's model picker · the voice job and
voice reply model pickers · the Helper models pages (done: each is the voice
reply section, with its failed row; the list says so with Try Again too) ·
Settings > Pulse's model picker · the Kanban model override's catalog (in the
task composer and on a task's page)

**Code**
- The rule: `Conduit/Views/ModelPickerView.swift` (ModelCatalogState, KeptModelCatalog, and the model sheet's modelSection, searchResultsSection, catalogFailedRow, modelRowsLocked, loadModels), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (modelOptionsAnswer: an answer that isn't one is a failed read)
- Model page: `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (ModelCatalogPlaceholder, ProfileModelSettingsDetail, DelegationModelSettings, FallbackModelsSettings)
- Bots: `Conduit/Views/BotModelPicker.swift` (load, loadFailedRows)
- Helper models: `Conduit/Views/HelperModelViews.swift` (HelperModelsPage's failed row and read, HelperModelsSettingsSection's read and its row hidden on a Hermes without the slots)
- Providers: `Conduit/Views/ProviderSettingsViews.swift` (ProviderDetailPage's modelsSection and catalogFailedRow, ModelPageProviders.reloadCatalog)
- Voice and Pulse: `Conduit/Views/GeminiLiveViews.swift` (the voice job and voice reply model settings: VoiceJobModelSettingsSection.loadProviders and modelsAnswered, VoiceReplyModelSettingsSection.read, tryAgain, reloadProviders and modelsAnswered, VoiceReplyModelPicks.readDidFail), `Conduit/Views/PulseSettingsViews.swift` (Settings > Pulse's model picker, loadModels and modelsAnswered), `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (ModelCatalogPlaceholder's failed row under them), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (loadModelProviders, keptModelProviders)
- Kanban: `Conduit/Views/Kanban/KanbanTaskComposerView.swift` (KanbanModelOverrideSheet's catalogSection, showKept, optionsAnswered and loadOptions), `Conduit/Services/KanbanService.swift` (fetchModelOptions keeps an answer with a model to offer; offerable), `Conduit/Services/KanbanStore.swift` (keptModelOptions), `Conduit/Models/KanbanModels.swift` (KanbanModelOptionsResponse drops a provider row it can't read on its own)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/KanbanTests.swift` (testTheModelOverrideOpensOnTheRosterItListedLastTime), `ConduitTests/KanbanV2Tests.swift` (testModelOptionsDecodeTolerantly)

**Rulings**
- A failed fetch says "Could not load models." with Try Again; "No models are available from this gateway." is only for a catalog that loaded empty; neither shows while loading. A re-load that fails keeps the rows it had (2026-10-24, from #1016's review).
- A list that didn't load is never edited or saved: Save stays off until the catalog is in.
- The Model page's editors open on the catalog kept from Hermes' last answer (see Screens that open on their last answer); a read that fails leaves it up with "Could not load models." and Try Again under it, and Save stays off until Hermes answers (#1552). A Default model save reads the catalog again after, so the provider it marks in use, whose models an inherited delegate shows, follows the save (#1555).
- The model sheet and a bot's model picker open on the models kept from Hermes' last `model.options` answer the same way, with "Could not load models." and Try Again under them (under the sheet's search matches too) after a read that fails, a later one after Hermes answered included (#1816); their kept models wait for Hermes' answer before they can be picked (#1567).
- The voice job, voice reply and Settings > Pulse pickers keep the models they list (kept from Hermes' last answer, or none) when the read fails, and say "Could not load models." with Try Again under the Model menu, which waits for Hermes' answer before a model is picked, as the sheet's rows do. The voice reply section says it when the read of its setting fails too, with a setting kept (with none it stays hidden, as on a Hermes without the slot, until the page's next check asks again), its Try Again asks for both, and a failure older than the answer shown says nothing (#1567). Settings > Pulse's picker lists the models of the profile Pulse runs in, read from the dashboard's route for that profile when it isn't the one open, and drops another profile's list when Pulse's changes (2026-11-03, #1684, issue 1681).
- The Kanban model override, in the task composer and on a task's page, opens on the roster the kanban plugin gave last time, kept once per dashboard, and its models wait for the plugin's answer before one is picked. A read that fails keeps them up with "Could not load models." and Try Again, the free-text entry under them; "No curated model catalog available" and the free-text entry are otherwise only for a roster that loaded empty, and neither shows before the first read answers. A roster with nothing to offer (a plugin whose inventory is down) is shown but never kept over the last one. Try Again over a kept roster shows no loader, as the model sheet's doesn't (#1584). A provider row Conduit can't read drops on its own, so one bad row never empties the roster (#1588, from #1584's review).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1823 (Try Again after a failed Refresh models asks for the live lists again; see Model lists Hermes is still fetching); 2026-11-05, #1816 (the model sheet says a failed read under rows Hermes gave too, as a bot's Model page does, for Refresh models and the read again, see Model lists Hermes is still fetching); 2026-11-03, #1684 (Settings > Pulse's picker lists the models of Pulse's profile); 2026-11-01, #1625 (the Helper models pages reuse the voice reply section and its failed row); 2026-11-01, #1616 (a provider's page in Models & providers picks a default only from a catalog Hermes gave since the page opened, and says a failed read with Try Again; the Model sheet's Add a provider row reads the models again when its sheet closes); 2026-10-31, #1588 (from #1584's review, a provider row the Kanban override can't read drops on its own, never the whole roster); 2026-10-31, #1584 (the Kanban model override opens on its kept roster, picked once the plugin answers, and says a failed read with Try Again, closing its gap; from its review, neither the empty roster's note nor the free-text entry shows before the first read answers, and a roster with nothing to offer isn't kept); 2026-10-31, #1567 (the model sheet and a bot's model picker open on the kept models, picked once Hermes answers, and the bot picker's failed read offers Try Again, closing its gap; the voice and Pulse pickers say a failed read with Try Again, the voice reply section's setting read included, closing theirs, and their Model menus wait for Hermes' answer); 2026-10-31, #1563 (the voice and Pulse pickers' loader, loadModelProviders since #1558, and its gap brought up to date; nothing else changed); 2026-10-31, #1555 (a Default model save reads the catalog again for its kept copy; the Save buttons' rule moved to KeptAnswerGate); 2026-10-31, #1552 (the Model page's editors open on a kept catalog, with Try Again under it when the read fails); 2026-10-27, at #1395 (search matches show only once the catalog is in; loading, failed and empty states unchanged, the Kanban composer's included); at #1334 (the model sheet's loading, failed and empty states unchanged under its new error row); 2026-10-24, at #1190; a reload that lands under unsaved Fallback models edits keeps them at #1191 (#1016 review).

## Model lists Hermes is still fetching

Hermes answers a model picker from its cache of each provider's model list,
and fetches a list that is stale or missing in the background, so a first
read can list only a provider's built-in models and miss the ones only its
live list has (issue 1807: Sonnet and Haiku missing beside Opus).

**Siblings:** the model sheet (iPhone, iPad and Mac) · a bot's Model page ·
the Model page's Default model, Delegate model and Fallback models editors ·
Models & providers' providers and a provider's page there · the voice job and voice reply model pickers
and the Helper models pages (the voice reply section) · Settings > Pulse's
model picker · the Kanban model override (not needed: the kanban plugin's
route waits for the live lists) · Text (not needed: no README, docs or
Settings caption describes the lists)

**Code**
- The read again and Refresh models: `Conduit/Views/ModelPickerView.swift` (ModelCatalogSettle, RefreshModelsButton, the model sheet's loadModels and refreshModelsButton), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (modelOptionsAnswer's refresh), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (loadModelProviders' refresh)
- Bots: `Conduit/Views/BotModelPicker.swift` (load, the toolbar's Refresh models)
- Settings: `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (ProfileModelSettingsDetail, DelegationModelSettings and FallbackModelsSettings' tasks and settleCatalog), `Conduit/Views/ProviderSettingsViews.swift` (ModelPageProviders' task and readAgain, ProviderDetailPage's task), `Conduit/Views/GeminiLiveViews.swift` (VoiceJobModelSettingsSection's loadProviders, VoiceReplyModelSettingsSection's read and reloadProviders), `Conduit/Views/PulseSettingsViews.swift` (the model picker's task and loadModels)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/HermesClientTests.swift` (testRefreshModelsAsksHermesForLiveListsAndAPlainReadDoesNot, testRefreshModelsOnAHermesWithoutTheFlagReadsAgainWithoutIt)

**Rulings**
- Every model picker reads Hermes' models once more four seconds after it opens, while it's still open, so the lists Hermes fetched meanwhile show without a reopen. A read that fails then is like any other (see Model lists that fail to load). The Model page's editors take only the models from it, so a save that lands meanwhile keeps its picks, and one that fails leaves the models they show as they are, without a failure row, as Hermes listed them on this visit (after a first read that failed, they read the whole page again); the voice reply section skips it after a setting read that failed (the page's next check asks again), and Models & providers and a provider's page hold it while a default is being picked, reading once the pick ends (a failed save included). A provider's page opened before the providers list's read again landed (leaving the list cancels it) reads again four seconds after it opens, through the list's read. In every picker only the last read asked lands, so an older read again never undoes a newer Try Again. On the Model page's editors an older whole-page read keeps the models of a newer read again that has landed, and a save Hermes took while a read was asked keeps its picks.
- The model sheet and a bot's Model page have Refresh models in their toolbar: Hermes drops its cached lists and fetches every provider's live list before it answers, which can take a while (a 60 s wait), with a spinner in its place meanwhile. The search, the open provider, the checked row and the model sheet's keyboard highlight (on the same match, wherever it moves) stay, after the read again too; a read that fails keeps the models shown, saying so with Try Again. A Hermes that doesn't know the flag answers from its cache. Only the last read asked lands, and no other read (the read again, Try Again, the read after adding a provider) is asked while a refresh runs; the model sheet and a bot's Model page ask one plain read when the refresh lands if one was skipped, unless the refresh failed (its failure row stays, and its Try Again asks for the live lists again). Hermes Desktop's model menu has the same Refresh Models. A row picked in the sheet that Hermes ran under another id keeps its checkmark through a read while the session still runs it.
- A provider's models are Hermes' rows as given; the same model from two providers is two rows (see Searching for a model).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

`/fast` and `/yolo` · a bot's model picker and the Model page's Default,
Delegate and Fallback model editors (not siblings: they're saved with the bot
or the profile, not live session settings)

- Chip and writes: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift` (the reasoning chip), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (setReasoningEffort, setYoloModeReportingFailure), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (setModel, setSpeed, ModelSwitchOutcome)

**Open gaps**

## Sharing into Conduit

What the share extension takes from another app's Share sheet (text, links,
pictures, videos and files) into a draft, and what it says about anything it
leaves out.

**Siblings:** the share extension · pasting into the composer · dropping on a
chat, a room or the composer field · Ask Hermes About Screen · Files over the
size limit (its own entry) · README.md (the share sheet line)

**Code**
- Reading the share: `Shared/ShareDraft/ShareDraftCollector.swift` (kind, fileType, offersImageObjectOnly, stageFile)
- A picture as an image object, and its PNG: `Shared/ShareDraft/ProviderPicture.swift` (loadImage, pngData), used by the share sheet, paste and drop
- The sheet: `ConduitShareExtension/ShareDraftModel.swift` (collect, ShareDraftProblem.message), `ConduitShareExtension/ShareDraftSheet.swift`
- Paste: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerPasteTextView.swift` (canLoadImageProvider, loadImageObject)
- Drop: `Conduit/Views/Components/AttachmentDrop.swift` (stage, stageImageObject), `Conduit/Views/Components/ReturnKeyTextView.swift` (fieldDrop)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ShareDraftTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- A picture offered only as an image object (the screenshot editor's Share hands over UIKit's own `com.apple.uikit.image`) is attached as a PNG, as a pasted one is. UIKit's archived image type is never read as a picture file; a provider that also offers a picture file is read as that file (2026-11-04, #1750, issue 1747).
- A picture offered only as an image object takes its suggested name without that name's extension: it is always written as PNG (2026-11-04, #1750 review).
- A shared file is read every way its provider offers, in turn: its file, then a picture's bytes (only when they decode as a picture: the header's pixel count first, at most 64 million, then a small thumbnail of the first frame, so a small file claiming a huge picture is never decoded at full size), then the picture as an image object (as PNG; never for a video or document, whose preview would stand in for the file), then the item it hands over under its type and then as its file URL; it is left out only when all of them failed. A provider offering a file URL that doesn't load as a link is read this way too, rather than skipped. Bytes are read only for a picture, so a video or document is never read into the extension's memory whole (2026-11-05, #1821, issue 1747 on build 251).
- An unreadable item's Left out line adds the system's reason under it, and each failed step is logged (category ShareDraft, the reason kept private), so one try on a device shows which step failed (2026-11-05, #1821).
- A picture with no bitmap of its own (`pngData()` nil) is drawn once and that is written, in the share sheet, paste and drop alike; a dropped picture whose file can't be read is taken as its image object too (2026-11-05, #1821).
- When nothing could be added, the sheet shows the Left out list a draft has, each thing with why (too large, unreadable), scrolling however many there are; the general "nothing here" line is only for a share that offered nothing Conduit reads (2026-11-04, #1750, issue 1747).

**Open gaps**
- A drop decides from the dragged item's listed types alone, so a drag that offers only UIKit's image object isn't taken by a chat, a room or the composer field (no source is known to send one; pasting one works).
- Something the share offered under a type Conduit doesn't read at all is skipped without a line, alongside things that were added.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1821 (issue 1747 on build 251: the picture was still left out as unreadable; every read is now tried in turn, with the reason shown and logged).

## Files over the size limit

What Conduit says when a file is too large to attach, and which limit it
names.

**Siblings:** the chat composer (picker, drop, camera) · pasting into the
composer · the share extension · Ask Hermes About Screen · a recorded voice
message · the group room composer · the Settings caption for the limit

**Code**
- The limit and its message: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerAttachments.swift` (AttachmentSizeLimit, tooLargeMessage)
- Chat composer: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerBar.swift`
- Paste: `Conduit/Views/Components/ComposerPasteTextView.swift`
- Dropped files: `Conduit/Views/Components/AttachmentDrop.swift` (through AttachmentStaging.stageCopy, the Document picker's path; a picture whose file fails, through stageImageObject, which holds its PNG to the limit before writing it, #1821)
- Share extension: `Conduit/Services/AppState+ShareDraft.swift`; `Shared/ShareDraft/ShareDraftCollector.swift` (stageFile: a file's size before and after its copy, a picture's bytes before they are decoded or written, #1821)
- Ask Hermes About Screen: `Conduit/Intents/AskHermesAboutScreenIntent.swift`
- Voice message: `Conduit/Services/AppState+VoiceMessage.swift`
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Services/GroupRoomFiles.swift` (stagingLimit, tooLargeMessage), `Conduit/Views/Components/GroupRoomComposer.swift`
- Settings: `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (the attachment size limit setting)

**Rulings**
- The message names the limit that refused the file. When that is the user's Settings limit it says where to raise it; when it is a route's own cap at or below the Settings limit (a group room takes 50 MB), it names that cap and offers no setting (2026-10-24, from #935's review, #1190).

**Open gaps**
- The voice message says "larger than your attachment size limit" without the size or where to change it.
- A pasted picture link whose header claims more pixels than a reply's picture may have is refused as "The image provider returned invalid image data.", not as too large.
- The Settings caption doesn't say that a group room takes at most 50 MB whatever the limit.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1821 (a picture whose file fails is held to the same limit when it is taken as its bytes or its image object, on the share sheet and a drop); 2026-10-29, #1515 (a long paste over the limit isn't attached: it goes into the field, as pastes did before); 2026-10-28, #1411 (dropped files refused with the same limit and message as picked ones); 2026-10-24, at #1190; the paste's pixel bound at #1191 (#892 review).

## Sending files in a chat

How a message's pictures and files go up to Hermes before the prompt, and
how long a large one may take on a slow link.

**Siblings:** the chat composer (picker, drop, camera, paste, a long paste as a text file) · the share
extension · Ask Hermes About Screen · a recorded voice message · Bot Chat and
project chats (the same send) · the group room composer (its own upload) ·
the socket's keepalive, the network path change's probe and the foreground
connection check · Settings captions, briefings, the notifier's tool text and
README (none describes upload size or timing) · the notifier (the upload is
Hermes' own RPC)

**Code**
- The send: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (sendMessage: image.attach_bytes, file.attach when Hermes refuses the image, file.attach for every other file; a long paste's `title_preview`, `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` sendPrompt, from `Conduit/Views/Components/PastedTextAttachment.swift` titlePreview)
- Resizing a picture: `Conduit/Services/PictureUpload.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (AttachmentHelper.pictureForHermes)
- Budgets and the socket: `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (uploadTimeout, attachImage, attachFile, requestsBeingWritten, keepaliveQuietTimeLeft, probe, healthCheck; canHandOffSocket, which keeps a profile switch from handing on a socket mid-write, #1452)
- Group rooms: `Conduit/Services/GroupRoomFiles.swift` (timeoutMilliseconds)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/HermesClientTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/ComposerAttachmentPolicyTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- A picture sent as an image whose long edge is over 2048 px goes as a 2048 px JPEG (quality 0.85), upright, with a .jpg name, or a 2048 px PNG when some of its pixels are see-through (an alpha channel alone still goes as a JPEG); one that size or smaller, an animated one, or one the JPEG wouldn't make smaller goes as it is. The chat shows the picture as picked. Files sent as files are never changed (Eric, 2026-10-25, #1268, for #1265: a full-size photo on a slow link outlasted Hermes' own socket ping and dropped the connection).
- An upload's budget is two minutes, or about 1 s for every 64 KB it carries (about 0.5 Mbit/s) if that is longer, for a picture and a file alike; a group room's upload allows the same rate, with its own three-minute floor (2026-10-25, #1265 report: 3 to 4 MB photos failed now and then under the 30 s every request had).
- While a frame of 256 KB or more is still being written (a cancelled request's too), the keepalive, the network path change's probe and the foreground check don't ping: a ping queued behind it can't be answered in time and would drop a working socket. The request's own budget answers for the socket, and once it ends the pings come back; a cancelled request's frame counts until the socket finishes or fails the write, two minutes at most (2026-10-25, #1265 report).

**Open gaps**
- Files go up one after another as base64 over the chat socket; nothing shows how far an upload has got.
- The foreground check skipped behind an upload counts as passed, so a chat resumed then finds a dead socket only when that upload's budget ends or its write fails.
- An upload whose budget ends while its frame is still going out stops counting as written then, not when the socket finishes the write: the keepalive pings again, and a profile switch can hand the socket on behind it (#1452).

**Checked:** 2026-11-01, #1631 (on the gateway's own listener this speaks the session authority's shapes, see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-29, #1515 (a long paste goes as a text file with Desktop's title preview); 2026-10-28, #1452 (a profile switch's socket hand-off waits out a large write too); 2026-10-25, at #1268.

## Phone change errors

What Hermes and the user are told when a calendar, reminder or alarm change
can't be made on the phone.

**Siblings:** a change from a voice call (PhoneVoiceTools) · a change queued
by Hermes through the notifier (its result note) · the phone sync status line
· alarms and timers · the wording the notifier's tools give models · Pulse
(the `pulse_turn` refusal, and a suggestion's Add or Undo the phone store
refuses)

**Code**
- Calendar and reminder errors: `Conduit/Phone/EventKitPhoneSource.swift` (PhoneCalendarSourceError, apply, moveDestination)
- Alarm errors: `Conduit/Phone/PhoneAlarmSource.swift` (PhoneAlarmError)
- Voice tools: `Conduit/Phone/PhoneVoiceTools.swift` (the add, change, delete and alarm tools' catches)
- Queued changes and status: `Conduit/Phone/PhoneSyncEngine.swift` (record, lastError, describe)
- Notifier: `notifier/phone_tool.py` (the wording models read, `pulse_turn` among it), `notifier/pulse_proposals.py` (a suggestion's refusals)
- Pulse: `Conduit/Services/PulseSettings.swift` (PulseRefusal: what a suggestion's refusals say)

**Rulings**
- An error names what is missing: the item ("That item isn't on this iPhone any more."), or the calendar or list it was to move to, which leaves the item in place (2026-10-24, from #876's review, #1190).
- Voice tools turn only a missing item on a change or delete into "read the calendar again for its id"; every other error reaches the model as "It couldn't be changed: <reason>" (or added, deleted, set, cancelled) with the error's own text (2026-10-24, #1190).
- While a Pulse turn is in flight in Pulse's chat, `conduit_calendar` and `conduit_phone` refuse a change asked for from that chat, or from a call Hermes names no chat for, with `pulse_turn`: Pulse is taking a turn there and nothing in it can change the phone, so ask again once its message is in. A suggestion's Add or Undo that the phone store refuses shows the store's own note on the Pulse screen and leaves the suggestion to tap again; Undo before the phone has sent what it added says to try again in a moment (2026-10-27, notifier #417, #1356).

**Open gaps**
- Adding an event or reminder when the phone has no default calendar or list (and the one named is gone) says "That item isn't on this iPhone any more."

**Checked:** 2026-10-30, #1542 (All history stays after the host's 2000 limit and stops at the oldest reading; the stores needed no change); 2026-10-29, #1517 (the `pulse` branch merged into main: the app paths it lists are on main now; nothing else changed); 2026-10-27, at #1375, carrying #1356 from the `pulse` branch (Pulse's `pulse_turn` refusal and a suggestion's refusals, with notifier #417); 2026-10-24, at #1190.

## Live-call sends on a slow connection

How a live call's microphone audio, and the text turns and tool answers
sent beside it, go out when the connection stops taking them: in order,
with a bounded backlog, so a stalled socket doesn't pile up audio the model
can't use or hold text without end.

**Siblings:** Gemini Live · Qwen Live (its socket goes through the same writer) · Grok Live · Local Live · GPT-Live (WebRTC) ·
Classic's transcription streams · Watch calls (Gemini, Qwen, Grok, Local Live; GPT-Live over the host's audio bridge)

**Code**
- The writer: `Shared/GeminiLive/LiveVoiceSocketWriter.swift` (maxQueuedAudio, maxQueuedOther, Backlogged); what counts as audio: `Shared/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveProtocol.swift` (LiveVoiceClientMessage.isAudio)
- Sessions: `Shared/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveSession.swift`, `Shared/GrokLive/GrokLiveSession.swift`, `Shared/LocalLive/LocalLiveSession.swift`
- Watch: `ConduitWatch/WatchDirectCallModel.swift` (maxSendsInFlight, flushUplink; the same Gemini, Grok and Local Live sessions), `ConduitWatch/WatchBridgeCallModel.swift` (sendsInFlightLimit, eventsInFlightLimit, GPT-Live's bridge socket)
- Classic: `Conduit/Voice/SpeechServerTranscription.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/HermesLiveTranscription.swift` (sendChain)

**Rulings**
- Each connection's frames go out one at a time, in order. Up to 96 capture chunks of audio may be outstanding, the one on the socket included: for Gemini about two seconds of the tap's 1,024-frame buffers at 48 kHz (longer on a route that captures at a lower rate), and the same count of Grok's and Local Live's own chunks; audio past that is dropped as it arrives. Frames for a socket the session replaced fail instead of going out, and dropped audio is logged (2026-10-24, #1223).
- Text turns, context notes and tool answers are never dropped on their own. Up to 32 may be outstanding, the one on the socket included; one more means the socket stopped taking frames, so everything it holds fails and the session reconnects, each frame's failure handler handing its result back as for any failed send (2026-10-25, #1231).
- GPT-Live's audio on the phone is WebRTC's to pace; on the Watch it goes over the host's audio bridge, already capped at 20 sends in flight. The bridge's text events (Hermes' replies) are capped too: before each reply goes out, 32 events outstanding on the connection means the socket stopped taking them, so the Watch rejoins and the replies not yet sent stay pending for the new connection. A reply's chunks go out together, so one reply can take the count past 32. The check guards growth: a stalled socket with nothing more to send holds what it has, and the bridge's ping watchdog ends it (2026-10-25, #1231). Classic's transcription streams keep a whole utterance, since dropping audio there loses words (2026-10-24, #1223).

**Open gaps**
- On the Watch's GPT-Live bridge, a reply already handed to a socket that then drops is lost with it, on any dropped connection and not only a backlogged one: the bridge sends without asking for a confirmation, where the phone's writer hands a failed frame's result back.

**Checked:** 2026-10-28, #1424 (only audio the writer took counts toward the call trace's levels); 2026-10-25, Qwen in the siblings, at #1182, carried in #1235; #1231, for the text cap; 2026-10-24, #1223.

## Live call trace

The steps of the last Grok Live, Qwen Live, Local Live or GPT-Live call that
Diagnostics & logs (Last connection) shows and copies, so a user can paste them
into an issue: setup, the microphone, the server's turn detection and the
user's turns, and each tool call; for GPT-Live, its startup.

**Siblings:** Grok Live (phone, CarPlay, calls from Hermes) · Local Live ·
Qwen Live (turn steps and the controller's tool steps) · GPT-Live on the iPhone,
CarPlay and calls from Hermes (startup steps, #1611) · Gemini Live (no trace) ·
Watch calls (no trace here; the Watch's own call log, Voice settings > Apple
Watch, already keeps a GPT-Live call's `briefingApplied` and `greetingApplied`
in `bridgeStarted`) · docs/VOICE_SETTINGS.md

**Code**
- The trace and its report: `Conduit/Voice/LiveCallTrace.swift`, `Conduit/Views/ChatSupportSheets.swift` (lastConnectionReport)
- Steps: `Shared/GrokLive/GrokLiveSession.swift`, `Shared/LocalLive/LocalLiveSession.swift`, `Shared/GeminiLive/QwenLiveSocket.swift`, `Shared/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveSession.swift` (onTrace), `Shared/GrokLive/LiveTurnTrace.swift`, `Shared/GrokLive/GrokLiveProtocol.swift` (turnDetectionSummary), `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveConversationController.swift` (traceName, traceInputRoute)
- GPT-Live's steps: `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveSession.swift` (onTrace, requestStep, answerStep), `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveConversationController.swift` (traceName), `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveClient.swift` (the answer's `source`)
- Wiring: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (traceName, session.onTrace)

**Rulings**
- A long call keeps its first 20 steps (the setup) and its newest ones, up to 200, so a late turn that never ends is kept (2026-10-28, #1424).
- Event kinds, function names, routes and levels only: never what the user or the model said, a call's arguments or a tool's answer (2026-10-28, #1424, from #1418).
- The user's turns show when the server heard speech start and end, with the microphone's loudest and quietest 100 ms between them, and say once when 15 s of audio pass with no start or no end, so a turn the server never ends can be told apart from audio that never arrived (2026-10-28, #1424, from #1418).
- Qwen Live's trace has the turn steps, dropped microphone audio and the controller's tool steps; Grok's own session steps (setup, functions taken) have no Qwen counterpart (2026-10-28, #1424).
- A tool step is noted only while its call is still the current one, so a lookup that returns after hang-up stays out of the next call's trace (2026-10-28, #1424).
- GPT-Live's trace is its startup (#1611): the request's briefing length and whether it carried a persona and memory (by their blocks), whether it was a call from Hermes, a greeting or waits for the user, and how many history items; what the host answered (built by Hermes or the plugin, the billing path, `briefing_applied`, `greeting_applied`, the voice); session.started or its timeout; a briefing or opening Conduit sent after the start, or asked for again; which side spoke first; connection drops and the provider's error code, never its message. "Applied" means the text was in the instructions the host sent, not that OpenAI took it or the model followed it (2026-11-01, #1611).

**Open gaps**
- Gemini Live sends no turn detection events and GPT-Live's turns run over WebRTC, so neither has turn steps; Gemini Live has no trace; the Watch has no trace to show.
- Every trace keeps only the last call, in memory until the app restarts (its steps also go to the system log, which keeps them longer), and nothing joins a call from Hermes, its saved call and the host's session request (#1611 asked for an alias).

**Checked:** 2026-11-01, #1612 (GPT-Live's startup steps, from issue 1611); 2026-10-28, #1424.

## Narrated actions left out of speech

What a spoken reply leaves out that the chat keeps: a persona's narrated
actions in single asterisks or underscores, and emoji. Hermes' file tags
have their own entry, Files Hermes attaches, in what voices say.

**Siblings:** Classic voice (phone, CarPlay; streamed) · Read Aloud and its
Now Playing title · live read-back of a reply ("read me the last reply", in
Gemini, Qwen, Grok and GPT-Live) and the result a Hermes call reads out ·
Local Live (Hermes' words, streamed) · Gemini Live, Qwen Live, Grok Live and
GPT-Live, and Local Live's agent mode, with the Hermes personality (told not to say actions) · the chat
transcript (never filtered)

**Code**
- The filter: `Conduit/Voice/SpokenTextFilter.swift` (firstActionMarker, closingMarker, speakable)
- Classic voice: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceConversationController.swift` (spokenTextFilter)
- Read Aloud: `Conduit/Voice/MessageReadAloudController.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/ReadAloudNowPlaying.swift` (title)
- Read-back: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceReadBack.swift` (plainSpeech, line by line), read by `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveToolBridge.swift` (read_last_reply), `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveDelegationBridge.swift` (lastReplyText) and `Conduit/Voice/HermesCalls.swift` (a call's result)
- Local Live: `Conduit/Voice/LocalLive/LocalLiveTurnRunner.swift` (actions, after SpokenVisualSplitter)
- Persona instructions: `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveConversationController.swift`, `Conduit/Voice/GPTLive/GPTLiveConversationController.swift`
- Tests: `ConduitTests/GeminiLiveVoiceTests.swift` (testSpokenTextFilter…), `ConduitTests/VoiceBackgroundJobTests.swift` (plainSpeech), `ConduitTests/HermesVoiceGatewayTimeoutTests+LocalLive.swift` (testLocalLiveTurnLeavesNarratedActionsOutOfSpeech)

**Rulings**
- An action is three or more words between a single `*` or `_` pair on one line; emphasis ("*really*"), bold and snake_case are spoken (2026-09-28, 223fca85).
- As in Markdown, a marker followed by a space opens nothing and one after a space closes nothing, so "price * units sold * 12" is spoken; one after a space with a word right after it opens again (2026-10-28, #1429). A marker inside a word ("2*3", "4*5", snake_case) neither opens nor closes one (#1430). The Now Playing title strips emphasis, list and quote markers but keeps a spaced `*` within the line's words.
- Every path that speaks Hermes' own words drops actions, so a reply sounds the same in Classic voice, Read Aloud, a live read-back and Local Live; the live models that speak for themselves are told not to say them (2026-10-28, #1430).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1896 (Local Live's agent mode can take the persona too, told the same); 2026-11-01, #1631 (an answer to a question this socket never saw passes the call's chat and profile, for the gateway's own listener; see Two Hermes servers); 2026-10-30, #1524 (Hermes Desktop's directives are read alongside, with their own entry, Cards made for Hermes Desktop); 2026-10-28, #1449 (Hermes' file tags are left out too, with their own entry, Files Hermes attaches); #1429, carried in #1430.

## Speech stream failures

What a spoken reply says when its speech stream fails partway: Classic voice
and Read Aloud speak through Hermes's speech stream or the user's speech
server.

**Siblings:** the Hermes speech stream · the speech-server speech stream ·
the one-shot fallback a Hermes stream falls back to before any audio, and
this iPhone's voice it falls back to (see iPhone voice) · the speech-server
transcription stream (listening, not speaking)

**Code**
- Hermes speech: `Conduit/Voice/HermesVoiceGateway.swift` (HermesSpeechStream: pathLostError, armFinishIdleTimeout, socketWentSilent, the fallback)
- Speech server: `Conduit/Voice/SpeechServerSpeech.swift` (SpeechServerSpeechStream)
- Listening: `Conduit/Voice/SpeechServerTranscription.swift`
- Keepalive: `Conduit/Voice/VoiceSocketKeepalive.swift`
- The iPhone fallback: `Conduit/Voice/OnDeviceSpeech.swift` (FallbackSpeechStream)

**Rulings**
- A dead Hermes speech stream is reported as a lost connection, not a timeout: "Lost the connection to Hermes speech." "Timed out" is only for a live stream that went quiet after some audio (2026-10-24, from #980's review, #1190). The speech-server speech stream can't tell yet (Open gaps); listening on a speech server says "Lost the connection to your speech server." when a send fails or the server closes early.
- Before any audio, a Hermes stream that drops or goes quiet tries the one-shot fallback instead of failing.

**Open gaps**
- The speech-server speech stream has no keepalive, so a dead path there shows as "Your speech server stopped speaking." after its idle timeout.

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1664 (the iPhone fallback's voice is the iPhone voice entry's); 2026-10-24, at #1208, carried in #1229.

## iPhone voice

Which of iOS's own voices speaks a reply when Settings > Voice > Assistant
speech is On this iPhone: Classic voice, Read Aloud, and a Hermes voice that
fails before any audio, all through one on-device speech stream.

**Siblings:** Classic voice on the phone and in CarPlay (the car plays the
phone's audio) · Read Aloud, in chats and group rooms · the Hermes speech
fallback (see Speech stream failures) · Settings' speaking test · Assistant
speech's captions · docs/VOICE_SETTINGS.md. Not the Apple Watch: it has no
Classic voice, and its calls speak with their live voices.

**Code**
- Picking the voice: `Conduit/Voice/IPhoneVoices.swift` (best, pick, installed, the pick per language)
- Speaking: `Conduit/Voice/OnDeviceSpeech.swift` (SystemSpeechSynthesizer.voice(for:), OnDeviceSpeechStream's reply language)
- Settings: `Conduit/Views/IPhoneVoiceSettingsView.swift`, in `Conduit/Views/VoiceSettingsView.swift` (iPhoneVoiceDetail)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/OnDeviceSpeechTests.swift`

**Rulings**
- Siri's own voices aren't offered: iOS never lists them to apps (WWDC20 session 10022), and private ones would fail App Review. Settings says so and points to Premium voices, the closest there is (2026-11-02, from a tester's report of a robotic voice).
- Automatic picks, for the reply's language: any voice but iOS 17's screen-reader voices (Eloquence: Eddy, Flo…), then Mandarin over Cantonese for Traditional Chinese (a reply recognized as Cantonese the other way round), then Premium, then Enhanced, then iOS's default for the language, the exact language, the iPhone's region, and the name, so the pick never follows iOS's list order. Screen-reader voices are used, and listed in Settings, only when a language has nothing else or the user picked one, which stays until they change it; novelty voices and Personal Voice never.
- A pick in Settings is per language (all its regions; Chinese by script, as replies are told apart: Simplified, and Traditional with Cantonese voices, so a Hong Kong pick speaks Traditional replies) and per device, not per profile: voices are installed per device. A picked voice that's deleted goes back to automatic.
- The reply's language comes from its first sentence long enough to tell; until then ("OK.") it's the app's.
- A voice downloaded or deleted while Conduit runs is used from the next sentence (iOS's voices-changed notice), and Settings reads the list again when it opens or Conduit comes back from iPhone Settings.
- With no Enhanced or Premium voice for a language, Settings says replies use a basic one and where to download one; when only screen-reader voices are installed, it says that instead, since that's why they sound robotic. A pick in the app's language plays the speaking test.

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1664 (new entry: a reply recognized as Cantonese, or a Cantonese system language, speaks with a Cantonese voice, and a Chinese script named outright wins over the region; automatic skips screen-reader voices, a pick per language, newly downloaded voices used at once; review: Automatic clears a deleted pick, screen-reader voices listed only when alone, Chinese kept apart by script, screen-reader voices below any other, an app in Traditional Chinese falls back to Traditional, Mandarin over Cantonese unpicked, a short opening sentence no longer fixes the reply's language).

## Providers and keys

Connecting the model providers a profile's models come from: an account
Hermes signs in to, an API key, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
Settings > Models & providers' Providers section, the Add a provider sheet
and a provider's page.

**Siblings:** the Model page's Default model and Fallback models (read the
catalog again after a change; done) · Memory & delegation's Delegate model
(not needed: it reads Hermes' catalog as its page opens; Remove names it
when the delegate runs on the provider) · the Model sheet's Add a provider row
(done) · the bot editor's Model page and the Voice replies, Voice jobs,
Pulse and Kanban model pickers (not needed: each reads Hermes' catalog as it
opens) · the voice key rows and toolset key fields (not needed: speech and
toolset credentials, kept apart) · Usage's provider quotas (not needed: they
read the same accounts) · Profile config saves (a custom endpoint) ·
Screens that open on their last answer · Profile names (done: the Add a
provider sheet names the profile by its Conduit name) · Watch, CarPlay and
the notifier (not needed: none shows provider settings) · README's
Notifications and control list and the Settings captions (done) · Helper
models (their own entry; their pickers read Hermes' catalog as they open) ·
Profile config saves (the key order, a profile setting)

**Code**
- Service: `Conduit/Services/ProviderSettings.swift` (ProviderEntry and its KeyAccess states, its Settings, keysInUse and signInsInUse, ProviderCatalog.entries, credentialCounts and summary, ProviderSettingsService: share, unshare, override, useShared, removeRows, removeCopies, sign-ins and endpoints)
- Views: `Conduit/Views/ProviderSettingsViews.swift` (ModelPageProviders, ProvidersSettingsSection, AddProviderSheet and AddProviderSheetHost, ProviderDetailPage, ProviderKeyEditor, ProviderSettingsRows, KeyOrder, KeyOrderPicks and KeyOrderSection, ProviderSignInView, CustomEndpointForm)
- Model page: `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (SettingsView's `.model` page and providerChanges, ProfileModelSettingsDetail's and FallbackModelsSettings' refresh)
- Model sheet: `Conduit/Views/ModelPickerView.swift` (addProviderRow)
- Helper models for Remove: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (loadHelperModels, keptHelperModels)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/ProviderSettingsTests.swift` (testTheKeysAProfileTakesTurnsOver, testTheKeyOrderKeepsAPickOverAnOlderAnswer)

**Rulings**
- Providers live on the Model page, renamed Models & providers; no new Settings row (Eric, 2026-11-01, #1616).
- Keys only go up: Conduit never calls `/api/env/reveal`, never shows Hermes' masked preview and keeps no key on the phone (Eric, 2026-11-01, #1616). The kept summary names the providers, the variables a key goes under, the pool rows (id, place, label, source), accounts' sign-in commands and links, and endpoints' names, models and address without its path, which can carry a token; an endpoint is edited only once Hermes has given its full address.
- A read of the pools, accounts or endpoints that fails fails the reload, which keeps what's shown; only a route an older Hermes lacks (404, 405, 410) is read as nothing there. A reload that started before a later one is dropped. A write that changed the host reads the page again even when its cleanup failed.
- Model defaults stay per profile; a key is set once for every profile, with an override per profile when needed, done from Conduit with no upstream change and no copying of keys between profiles (Eric, 2026-11-01, #1616). A shared key is a row in the main (`default`) profile's credential pool, which a profile with no rows of its own for the provider falls back to. An override is a row in that profile's pool, with Hermes' copies of the shared rows removed, since Hermes copies them into a profile's pool and the copy comes first (tested on 0.22.2). Replacing or removing a shared key removes its copies in every profile Conduit lists.
- A key in the main profile's `.env` reaches no other profile; it shows as "Saved for the main profile only" with a note to paste it again to share it. Pasting it there shares it and takes the `.env` variable out, since Hermes would read it into the pool ahead of the shared row. A key shared from another profile also clears the rows ahead of it there (its own key, an old copy), so that profile uses it too. A variable another provider owns (a non-primary `provider_profiles` entry) is never counted as this provider's key or removed for it. A key editor writes only once Hermes has answered, and a save whose cleanup failed anywhere, another profile's copy included, says the key is saved and that a profile still on the old one shows it as an old copy; the Add sheet stays open on that note. A provider's model list is picked from only once Hermes has given the catalog since the page opened. An endpoint matches its catalog row by its config key, never its display name.
- Hermes tries a key before it's saved; only a check that reached the provider and was refused stops the save. A provider that reads only another provider's variable isn't checked (Hermes would try the key on that provider). A variable two providers read as their own key is never removed for either, nor the pool row read from it (by Remove key, Use the shared key, a key of its own or sharing).
- A provider's page shows "Could not load models." with Try Again when Hermes' catalog read fails, as the Model lists ruling asks.
- Sign-ins live on the main profile, which Hermes already shares; custom endpoints are per profile, in its config, saved in the config write queue with `api_key` left out when nothing was typed (an empty one clears the saved key).
- A provider that runs the default model can't be removed, nor its key (Remove shared key, Remove key, Remove this profile's key; going back to the shared key is fine), and the page says so; each key removal asks first and names the delegate and fallback models on the provider; Remove waits for Hermes' catalog (not the kept one) to tell; it names the delegate and fallback models on it, and the helper models pinned to it, Pulse's included (#1632), which the page reads from Hermes apart from its catalog, Remove waiting for that read too, the kept ones only if it fails (#1636; a name only, it changes nothing).
- A key another provider also reads stays in the profile's settings, where Hermes still uses it first, and the key section says so, as does a save behind it; Use the shared key is offered only when the row the profile uses first is one Conduit may remove.
- A new endpoint's config key is made from its name (`lab-vllm`, then `lab-vllm-2`), clear of the profile's endpoints and of every slug, display name and alias in Hermes' model catalog, so it never takes a built-in's catalog row; Custom endpoint waits for that catalog, and says so with Try Again when it isn't in.
- A provider's settings that aren't keys (each non-password `provider` variable it owns in `/api/env`: a base URL override, Bedrock's AWS region and profile, Vertex's credentials file) are rows in a Settings section of its page and its Add page, set or cleared in the profile's `.env`, their values never shown. A provider with only such settings gets a card, and one with a setting saved and no key or sign-in reads "Settings saved" ("Settings saved, no key yet" when it takes a key); one that signs in isn't set up by a setting alone (#1625).
- Key order (Hermes' `credential_pool_strategies.<provider>`, per profile: first key until it runs out, take turns, random, least used first) shows on a provider's page once the pool the profile uses holds two or more keys: the main profile's whole pool, `.env` rows included, or another profile's own rows, else the shared ones it falls back to. It's a profile setting, saved in the config write queue once Hermes has answered (a read that fails leaves the picker waiting, with Try Again, never Hermes' default shown as its answer), and offered only for an id a dotted config key can name (#1625). Sign-ins in the pool (OAuth) count with the keys, as Hermes takes turns over them too, and a profile whose own pool holds only a sign-in uses its own pool, its card saying Signed in (still listed as connected) and its API key section not showing the shared key as in use; a key saved in that profile's `.env` reads as its own, removed with Remove this profile's key (the sign-in stays), never Use the shared key, and a key pasted there defaults to Only this profile, since a shared one wouldn't reach it; a profile-only replace also takes the old key out of the profile's `.env`, which Hermes would read back ahead of it (#1636); an answer to a read asked before a save ended is dropped (#1632). With a sign-in among them the page says "keys and sign-ins", and a kept config without the setting shows no order until Hermes answers (#1636). A summary kept by a build before the sign-in counts reads as unknown: the API key section and key order wait for Hermes, and a profile with no key rows of its own shows Connected (#1638).

**Open gaps**
- A profile Conduit doesn't list, or one that can't be read when a shared key is replaced, keeps its copy of the old key until its page's "Use the shared key".
- A custom endpoint's saved key can be replaced but not removed from Conduit.
- Conduit adds one key per provider and scope, so a second key for the key order comes from Hermes (`hermes auth add`) or the `.env`.
- Key order isn't offered for a provider whose id has a dot (`custom:together.ai`): the profile setting's dotted key would split it.
- Removing the shared key or signing out on the main profile checks only the main profile's default, delegate, fallback and helper models, not other profiles' that run on it.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1823 (#1816 checked here: Models & providers and a provider's page read the models again after opening, see Model lists Hermes is still fetching); 2026-11-01, #1638 (a summary kept by an older build, without sign-in counts, waits for Hermes: key section on the provider page and the Add sheet's connect page and key order wait, a failed read says so, the card says Connected); 2026-11-01, #1636 (key order says keys and sign-ins, waits for Hermes over a kept config without the setting; Remove reads the helper models from Hermes); 2026-11-01, #1632 (key order counts sign-ins, a profile's own sign-in among its own rows, its picks in a tested type; a removal names the helper models pinned to the provider); 2026-11-01, #1625 (stage 2: key order, providers with only settings; two gaps closed, two opened); 2026-11-01, #1620 (from #1616's last reviews: a removal tries every variable, a save behind a held key says so, a given-up sign-in is cancelled on Hermes, a model pick's spinner stays until its own catalog read lands; base-URL-only providers noted as a gap); 2026-11-01, #1616 (entry added: Providers section, Add a provider, shared keys with overrides and cleanup; host-tested on Hermes 0.22.2: an override wins after its copies go, across restarts, and replacing and going back to the shared key work)
