the same Markdown, a bot's `MEDIA:` pictures read from its own profile; the
user's attached files show as names, never as pictures) ·
HTML previews (a page shown in place, not a picture, so two in a row stay
two pages, their fallback pictures included) · iPhone, iPad and Mac (the same views; a grid takes
as many tiles to a row as the width gives) · Apple Watch and CarPlay (they
show no message pictures) · the cards drawn in web pages, which share the
memo and the transcript's rule for rows growing above the reader (see Cards
drawn in web pages) · text that describes it (none today: no Settings
caption, briefing or doc says how pictures load)

**Code**
- Attachments: `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (UserImageAttachmentPreview and its isTile; UserMessageContent.attachmentViews, which grids two or more)
- Two or more pictures as a grid: `Conduit/Views/Components/PictureGrid.swift` (PictureGrid.plan, shownCount, moreCount; PictureGridLayout; the tiles and the "+N" badge), `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownProseRun.swift` (pictureRanges, isGridPicture, Piece.isPictures, pictureSlot), `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (MarkdownPictureGrid, RemoteMarkdownImage.tileContent), and in the bounded views `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownRichContent.swift` (RichBudgetedMarkdownBody.slotView) and `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownLargeDocumentView.swift` (LargeMarkdownExpandedView's pictureRanges and pictureBlock)
- Reply pictures (`MEDIA:` and web): `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (RemoteMarkdownImage, WebFallbackImage), `Conduit/Views/Components/BoundedRemoteImage.swift`, `Conduit/Views/Components/GatewayMediaDataURLResolver.swift` (imageCacheKey, imageCacheKey(forMediaPath:)), set for job sheets in `Conduit/Views/LiveVoiceCallJobs.swift` and for a group room's bot messages in `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (mediaResolver(for:), GroupMemberBubble.mediaResolver, GroupRoomImageGallery), from `Conduit/Services/GroupChatModels.swift` (GroupRoomTurns.localProfile, speaker)
- Kept and remembered: `Conduit/Services/TranscriptImageCache.swift` (files on the phone), `Conduit/Services/TranscriptPictureMemory.swift` (decoded reply pictures, attachment previews, every picture's size and the card heights, loaded as the app opens from `Conduit/ConduitApp.swift` and again asked for by ChatView), both forgotten in `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (wipeOfflineChatCache, deleteSavedChats)
- A picture's arrival, or its failure: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (placeGatewayImage, placeRemoteImage, placeGatewayFailure, placeRemoteFailure), the row's new height reaching `Conduit/Views/TranscriptLayout.swift` (rowResized) from `Conduit/Views/TranscriptView.swift` (TranscriptCellRoot, and TranscriptViewController's rowResized, which asks at once for the pass that lands it), and `Conduit/Services/TranscriptScroller.swift` (keepAnchor) keeping the reader's row, see Cards drawn in web pages
- Tests: `ConduitTests/TranscriptInlineImageTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/TranscriptScrollerTests.swift` (Rows changing height), `ConduitTests/TranscriptLayoutTests.swift` (testARowChangingHeightMovesTheRowsUnderItInTheSamePass), `ConduitTests/ChatTypographyTests+PictureGrid.swift`

**Rulings**
- Two or more pictures in one message (a sent message's attachments, or pictures one after another in a reply, `MEDIA:` or web) show as square tiles side by side, cropped to the square, never stretched: as many to a row as the message's width takes at 104 pt or more, at least two, the rows evened out (six in a 640 pt column are two rows of three, not five and one; a chat column wider than about 650 pt puts six in one row; a grid asked for its ideal size wants a row of every tile at 180 pt, so a group room bubble, which hugs its ideal width, still gives it the room's width), each tile at most 180 pt. Six tiles show at most; the sixth says "+N" for itself and the rest, and VoiceOver hears how many more. A tap on any tile opens the picture viewer there, which pages through all of them. One picture alone keeps its own shape, and a video, sound or document Hermes sent keeps its card and splits the pictures around it. A sent message's files follow its pictures. A large or heavily structured reply, which mounts its blocks a few at a time, grids the pictures of a run it has mounted, so one cut by Continue reading shows its rest as a grid of its own once mounted. Every tile takes its square while it loads or when it won't, so a grid never changes height as its pictures arrive; a web picture that won't load here opens its address on a tap (Eric asked for it on every platform, 2026-11-05, issue 1801).
- A row never changes height when its picture arrives, if the picture has loaded on this phone before: its size is remembered (kept next to the pictures, read once off the main thread) and its placeholder takes it (2026-10-25, #1239, #1238).
- Reading, decoding and keeping a picture, and its size, stay off the main thread: a body looks pictures and sizes up in memory only (a local photo's existence is still checked there: a stat, never a picture read). A picture kept on the phone is never fetched again (2026-10-25, #1239).
- A picture with no remembered size takes its height as it arrives, as a card does. In a chat the reader's row (the first starting on screen) stays put in the same layout pass, scrolling or not, a finger keeping its drag and a fling its momentum (TranscriptScroller.keepAnchor): a row above it grows up out of view, one on screen grows down. Its size is remembered as it shows. A picture still loading when its row's cell goes to another row is dropped, and shows from memory or loads again when the row is back; one whose row has moved on to another picture never shows there. In a chat a web picture lands without its fade, since the move needs the growth in one pass (2026-10-25, #1270, #1238; taken at once, scrolling or not, since the transcript rewrite gave every row a frame of its own, 2026-10-31, #1577: the wait for the reader's scrolling to rest, and the rules it needed, went with ChatScrollEngine; Eric delegated the chat scroll's design to Claude, 2026-09-28, and approved the transcript rewrite's design, 2026-10-30).
- A picture that won't load (unavailable, too large, or a web picture its page can't show either) gives its place to its label or fallback the same way, at once, the reader's row kept by what the label's layout took. The web fallback's page measuring the picture goes the same way, and a row loading again a picture that failed keeps its label meanwhile (2026-10-26, #1270; at once since 2026-10-31, #1577, under the transcript rewrite's design, which Eric approved 2026-10-30).
- What memory already holds for a row (its picture, decoded, or the picture's size) shows as the row draws, on its first frame or a later one (another row of the same picture showed it since, a cold launch's kept sizes loaded): a row that resizes on its own keeps the reader's row like any growth, so nothing waits for an arrival. A web picture already decoded shows on the first frame too, its size remembered or not (2026-10-26, #1270; on a later frame too since 2026-10-31, #1577, under the transcript rewrite's design, which Eric approved 2026-10-30).
- A bot's `MEDIA:` pictures and files in a group room show as in its Bot Chat, read from the bot's own profile on the connected Hermes, where Hermes saved them, and page in the room's picture viewer. Another gateway's bot (a peer member) and a member the room no longer lists keep their tags as text, since their paths name files on another host; so does Hermes Desktop's read-only group sheet, and the user's own room messages, as in a chat (Eric's report, 2026-11-07, #1914: a room reply showed "MEDIA: /root/.hermes/cache/images/….png" as links).
- Outside a transcript (job sheets, whose web pictures load through the same view) a picture, or the label of one that won't load, takes its height as soon as it arrives too, but nothing there keeps the reader's row: a row above them grows down into what they read (2026-10-26, #1270). The saved copy's rows are the chat's own, drawn by its transcript, so their pictures arrive as a chat's do (2026-10-30, #1550), and so are a group room's, whose web pictures land without their fade as a chat's do (2026-10-31, #1590).

**Open gaps**
- A picture never loaded on this phone, or kept by a build before #1239 and not shown since, or whose row was laid out before a cold launch's kept sizes loaded, still grows its row once as it arrives: above the reader the offset moves with it, on screen it grows below what they look at, unanimated. Its height follows the row's width, so the memo can't reserve it before it loads, and only a read on the main thread before the first frame, which the ruling above keeps off it, would have the kept sizes in time.
- Job sheets have no transcript: a web picture never loaded on this phone grows its row where it is, and above a reader scrolled back it moves what they read, as chats did before #1270.
- Past 4,000 remembered sizes the memo starts again (no LRU), so pictures grow once more until each loads again.
- Not checked on a device yet: the grid's width as a Mac window is resized, and the "+N" tile under VoiceOver.

**Checked:** 2026-11-07, #1914 (a group room's bot messages load their `MEDIA:` pictures and files from the bot's own profile, closing the gap #1524 left; Siblings, Code, Rulings, gaps); 2026-11-05, #1803 (two or more pictures in a message show as a grid of tiles, issue 1801; Code, Rulings, Tests, gaps); 2026-11-02, #1643 (a row growing in a reply moves the cells under it in that pass, not only the layout's frames: the context names every row under it); 2026-11-01, #1622 (the pass that lands a row's new height is asked for at once, so a picture or its label arriving in an idle chat or room lands with the reader's row kept without waiting for the next thing to wake the app, as "at once" says; Code); 2026-10-31, #1590 (group rooms draw on the transcript: a picture, or its label, takes its height as it arrives with the reader's row kept, and a web picture lands without its fade, the room's rows reading a ChatRowDisclosure as a chat's do; Rulings, gaps); 2026-10-31, #1577 (chats draw on the transcript's collection view: a picture, or its label, takes its height as it arrives, scrolling or not, and TranscriptScroller keeps the reader's row; ChatRowArrival and the engine's wait for a rest are gone; the rulings #1566 departed from rewritten, and its Open gaps line gone; Code, Rulings, Tests, gaps); 2026-10-31, #1566 (TranscriptScroller's rule for rows growing above the reader, not called yet; pictures arrive as before; Code, and the rulings it departs from in Open gaps); 2026-10-30, #1550 (the saved copy is drawn by the chat's engine, so its pictures arrive as a chat's); 2026-10-30, #1524 (group rooms get the connected Hermes' resolver for Desktop cards only, their `MEDIA:` pictures still don't load; the resolver gains connectedDashboardBridge); 2026-10-29, #1491 (a tapped picture opens in the picture viewer among the chat's pictures); 2026-10-26, #1281 (wipeOfflineChatCache also forgets Predictive's state); at #1270.

## The picture viewer

A picture tapped full screen: swiped left and right through the pictures
around it, closed with a swipe down, zoomed with a pinch or a double tap, and
shared or saved from its Share button.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats and Bot Chat (attachments, reply pictures,
tool pictures) · the saved-chat copy · call job result sheets and the cards a
voice model shows · group rooms · the Artifacts page, a chat's Artifacts sheet
and the panel beside the chat · the Markdown reader (a Markdown artifact or file card) · the Folder tab · iPhone, iPad and Mac (the
same viewer; keys and a trackpad on an iPad or Mac) · Quick Look, which still
opens videos, audio and documents · README.md · text that describes it (the
pictures' VoiceOver hint "Opens full screen with save and share")

**Code**
- Viewer and presenting it: `Conduit/Views/Components/ImageGalleryViewer.swift` (ImageGalleryViewController, ImageGalleryPageController, ImageGalleryDecoder, ImageGalleryItem, ImageGallery, ImageGallerySource, the `imageGallery` environment value), `Conduit/Views/Components/MediaPreviewPresenter.swift` (presentGallery)
- What a chat lists: `Conduit/Views/Components/ImageGalleryItems.swift` (ChatImageGallery, the item makers), set in `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (chatImageGallery, from chatRowsOnScreen: the saved copy's pictures while it stands in) and `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift`
- Taps: `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (UserImageAttachmentPreview, whole or as a tile), `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (RemoteMarkdownImage.openImage, whole or as a tile of MarkdownPictureGrid)
- Other lists: `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (GroupRoomImageGallery), `Conduit/Views/LiveVoiceCallJobs.swift` (both sheets), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ArtifactsViews.swift` (openImage), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2WorkspaceViews.swift` (openImage), `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownDocumentSheet.swift` (the reader's own source)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/MarkdownLargeDocumentTests+ImageGallery.swift`

**Rulings**
- Pictures page in Conduit's own viewer, not Quick Look: Quick Look shows one file and has no swipe down. Videos, audio and documents still open in Quick Look; a picture never pages to one (2026-10-29, #1491, Eric asked for both gestures).
- A picture pages through the pictures of what it was tapped in, in the order they show: a chat's (each message's pictures in its text, then the ones it attaches, then a tool's), the saved copy's, a room's, a job result's or card's, the Artifacts list's as filtered, or the Folder's (the search's names, else the file's folder, else Recently Changed); one in a Markdown file the Folder previews, or the Markdown reader shows (from Artifacts or a file card), pages through that file's pictures. Each picture is listed once, where it first shows. One its list doesn't have (a reply still streaming) opens alone (2026-10-29, #1491).
- The list is read when a picture is tapped, never while scrolling: each screen holds one source, so no row redraws for it. Each picture fetches its original only as its page comes near (its own, then its neighbours once it is in, so a tap never starts three large downloads at once), the way its row opened it alone: the photo on this device, the copy kept on the phone, then Hermes; a picture in a list fetches as Artifacts and the Folder open a file. The row's own copy shows until the original is in, and stays if the original can't be had (2026-10-29, #1491).
- A swipe down (or up) of a picture that isn't zoomed in drags it, fading the backdrop; past a fifth of the screen or flung it closes, short of that it springs back. A zoomed picture pans instead, and its edge hands a sideways swipe on to the next. One finger only: two are a pinch. A trackpad's two-finger swipe does the same; on a keyboard the arrows page and Escape closes; VoiceOver pages with a three-finger swipe and closes with the escape gesture (2026-10-29, #1491).
- A single tap shows or hides the bar (Done, the name, "3 / 12", Share); Share opens once the picture's original is in. The Folder's Share or Save opens a picture in the viewer too, since its Share saves and copies (2026-10-29, #1491).
- A picture whose original can't be had keeps the row's copy, or says "Image unavailable" ("Too large to open on this phone" for one over the download limit), and one that failed otherwise (a dropped connection) is fetched again each time it is paged to; one too large isn't, since it would be again (2026-10-29, #1491).
- Copies fetched for the viewer are removed once it is two pages past them, and the rest when it closes, so a long list of large photos doesn't fill the phone (see Files prepared for preview and Save to Files).

**Open gaps**
- A room's list keys a bot's `MEDIA:` picture by its path alone, as a chat's does, so two bots on Docker or SSH profiles citing one container path in one room page as one picture, fetched through the first one's profile (the tapped picture itself shows its own file). Members of a room are profiles on one host, where one path is one file in every other case (2026-11-07, #1914).
- Not checked on a device yet: the swipe down beside the pager's own pan, the zoomed edge handing on to the next page, and the trackpad swipe on a Mac.
- A reply still streaming isn't listed: its pictures open alone until it settles.
- An animated GIF plays at up to 120 frames, drawn small enough that its frames stay within 32 MB (the pager holds three pages); Quick Look played every frame at full size.
- The Folder pages through its listed files only: a folder not opened in the tree isn't listed.

**Checked:** 2026-11-07, #1914 (a group room's list holds a bot's `MEDIA:` pictures too, each fetched through its own profile, see Pictures in messages); 2026-11-06, #1884 (the Markdown reader's pictures page through the file's own, not the chat's it opened over); 2026-11-05, #1803 (a tile of a message's picture grid opens the viewer as its picture did, the "+N" tile on its own picture, the rest paged to; Code); 2026-10-30, #1550 (a saved copy's pictures page through the chat's own list, from the rows drawn); 2026-10-29, #1491.

## Cards Hermes shows

Boards: one `conduit_show` call shows up to 12 native cards in the chat
(maps and places, stats, charts, weather, comparisons, steps, media, people,
status, and since plugin 0.128 tables to sort, day-by-day timelines,
checklists, lists, progress and callouts, and since plugin 0.133 diffs),
stacked or as tabs, with up to four follow-ups under it. Live models put the
same cards on the call screen with show_on_screen.

A diff card (issue 1818) shows changes Hermes presents: a review, a commit, a
config, two versions of a text. Hermes gives a unified patch, the path of a
patch file on the host, or a before and after; the plugin reads it into
files, hunks and lines. The chat shows the files and totals; a tap opens a
sheet with every file, line numbers, colored lines and the changed words.
Presenting only: no Git operations.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats and Bot Chat (the tool row) · the saved-chat
copy · the call screen (Gemini, Grok, Qwen and Local Live show_on_screen;
Classic and GPT-Live through Hermes) · saved call transcripts · group rooms ·
Hermes Desktop (the plugin's Desktop half draws the board) and messaging apps
(the Markdown) · the Watch and CarPlay ·
Predictions' reply chips (the follow-ups are the same chip) · what models read:
conduit_show's description and answers, the drawing rule, the
`conduit_push:drawing-boards` skill (its Showing changes recipe), show_on_screen's description · the
notifier README and CHANGELOG · for diffs, the full-diff sheet and the kept
diffs route (`/boards/diffs`)

**Code**
- Schema, shared byte for byte: `notifier/cards/card-schema.json`, `notifier/cards/card-vectors.json`, copied to `Conduit/Cards/card-schema.json` and `ConduitTests/Fixtures/card-vectors.json` (`scripts/check-card-schema.py`); normalized the same way in `notifier/card_schema.py` (normalize_cards with notes, normalize_next, normalize_layout, the Markdown) and `Conduit/Cards/RichCardSchema.swift` (prepared, cell, followUps)
- The tool: `notifier/show_tool.py` (problems, markdown, the old-Conduit cap, BOARD_RULE, the typed chat's TYPED_CHAT_NOTE), how the turn's message was entered in `notifier/turn_surface.py` (turn_entry), the rule and the checklist note in `notifier/__init__.py`, recipes in `notifier/skills/drawing-boards/SKILL.md`; the phone's features in `Conduit/Services/PresentedScreens.swift` ("board-cards") and `notifier/present_store.py`
- Checklist ticks on the host: `notifier/checklist_store.py`, `notifier/dashboard/api/boards.py` (`/boards/checklists`, capability "board-checklists"); in Conduit `Conduit/Cards/RichChecklistMemory.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState+Boards.swift`
- Cards and views: `Conduit/Cards/RichCard.swift`, `Conduit/Cards/RichBoardCard.swift` (RichBoard, RichTable…; FinishedToolMemo keeps each finished row's board and live names, so a row drawn again isn't read again), `Conduit/Cards/RichBoardCardViews.swift` (RichBoardLayout, RichBoardFollowUps, RichBoardMarkdown), `Conduit/Cards/RichCardViews.swift`; the chat row in `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift`, its follow-ups in `Conduit/Views/ChatRowState.swift` (followUpBoardRowID) and `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (requestBoardFollowUp)
- Diff cards: reading a patch in `notifier/card_schema.py` (read_diff, parse_patch, read_patch_file, answer_diff, `_diff_markdown`, DIFF_FEATURE), the answer in `notifier/show_tool.py` (`_diffs_answered`, keep_diff), kept on the host by `KeptDiffs` in `notifier/room_boards.py` (`_keep_diff` in `notifier/__init__.py`), read from `notifier/dashboard/api/boards.py` (`/boards/diffs`, capability "diff-cards"); the Desktop half's Diff in `notifier/desktop/plugin.js`; in Conduit `Conduit/Cards/RichDiffCard.swift` (RichDiff, RichDiffLine.numbered and changedParts, RichDiffLoader), `Conduit/Cards/RichDiffCardViews.swift` (RichDiffCard, RichDiffSheet), normalizeDiff and the "line" format in `Conduit/Cards/RichCardSchema.swift`, installRichDiffReader in `Conduit/Services/AppState+Boards.swift`, the "diff-cards" feature in `Conduit/Services/PresentedScreens.swift`
- Live models: `Conduit/Voice/GeminiLive/GeminiLiveToolBridge.swift` (showOnScreenDeclaration, invalidCardsNote; RichCardSchema.liveToolParameter leaves diffs out)
- Group rooms: `notifier/room_boards.py`, `_save_room_board` in `notifier/__init__.py`, `notifier/dashboard/api/boards.py` (`/boards/rooms`, capability "room-boards"); in Conduit `Conduit/Cards/RoomBoards.swift` (RoomBoard.placed, RoomBoardsView), `Conduit/Services/AppState+RoomBoards.swift`, the row in `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift` (GroupMemberBubble) and `Conduit/Views/TranscriptModel.swift` (GroupRoomRow.event)
- Hermes Desktop: the half `notifier/desktop/plugin.js` (the `::conduit-board{id="cb-…"}` directive, its cards, the "seen" handshake), `DesktopBoards` in `notifier/room_boards.py`, `_save_desktop_board` and `_desktop_half_live` in `notifier/__init__.py`, the Desktop branch and DESKTOP_BOARD_RULE in `notifier/show_tool.py`, `notifier/dashboard/api/boards.py` (`/boards/desktop`, `/boards/desktop/seen`, capability "desktop-boards"); Conduit hides the line in `Conduit/Views/Components/TranscriptDirectives.swift` (conduitBoardName, removingBoards), and `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` keeps it hidden (directiveSegments, and parseDocument's empty-blocks fallback, so a reply that is only the line stays empty), as does a pin's excerpt in `Conduit/Models/PinnedReplies.swift`
- Tests: `ConduitTests/RichCardTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/RichCardTests+Boards.swift`, `ConduitTests/RichCardTests+Diff.swift`, `notifier/tests/test_diff_cards.py`, `ConduitTests/MarkdownLargeDocumentTests+DesktopCard.swift` (testConduitBoard_…), `notifier/tests/test_cards.py`, `notifier/tests/test_show.py`, `notifier/tests/test_checklists.py`, `notifier/tests/test_room_boards.py`, `notifier/tests/test_desktop_boards.py`, `notifier/upstream/test_desktop_half.py` (Hermes' own Desktop lint over the half)

**Rulings**
- One tool: conduit_show grows; there is no second board tool (Eric, 2026-11-03, #1713 with notifier #528).
- Never blank: every answer carries the cards' Markdown. Conduit shows it in the board's place when it can't draw every card, never part of a board, and a model outside Conduit gets it for its reply (Eric, 2026-11-03, #1713 with notifier #528).
- Exact errors: what normalization leaves out goes back to the model as `problems`, by path, so it can fix the board and show it again (Eric, 2026-11-03, notifier #528).
- Conduit lays the board out: Hermes picks only stack or tabs; small cards pair up on a wide window (2026-11-03, #1713).
- Follow-ups are plain messages the user would send, at most four, offered only under the last turn's board while Hermes is free and connected and the composer is empty: tap sends, long-press edits, and taps in their first 0.4 s are ignored, as Predictions' chips (Eric, 2026-11-03, #1713).
- Checklist ticks in a chat are kept on the host for every device, and Hermes hears what changed once, at the chat's next turn; on the call screen they stay on the phone (Eric, 2026-11-03, #1713 with notifier #528), kept by the list's name as a chat's are, so a list of that name on another call's screen shows the same ticks (#1713).
- A tick goes to the host on its own, in the order made, and the host applies it to the newest ticks any device saved, so a tick from another device is never undone (2026-11-03, #1713 with notifier #528).
- A chat's ticks are read and saved only through its own dashboard: after a switch to another Hermes they stay unsent on the phone, in order, and go when the chat is drawn on its own dashboard again, since the other Hermes would take the chat's ids and answer as saved (2026-11-04, #1748, issue 1745).
- A chat's ticks belong to the chat, not to the ids it's known by: when its ids grow while it's open (the durable id confirmed, an alias from the catalog, a Bot Chat's roster ids), the phone's copy moves to the new ids, and a tick not yet sent still goes to the host and stays shown (2026-11-04, #1748, issue 1746).
- In a group room this host runs, the board is kept on the host and drawn under the agent's next message there (within 15 minutes), for every Conduit saying "room-boards"; the room's other agents read only the message, and are told so. A room run elsewhere, or an older Conduit, gets it in the agent's reply as Markdown (`group_room`) (Eric, 2026-11-03: text first, cards in a follow-up PR; 2026-11-04, notifier 0.129). Other people's agents may read a room, so contact cards (a person's numbers, a text drafted for the user) stay out of it, with a problems line, whatever the turn's surface. A room's board has no follow-ups (a tap would speak for the user to the whole room) and its checklists keep no ticks.
- In Hermes Desktop the plugin's Desktop half ("Conduit boards", off until the user turns it on in Desktop) draws the board: conduit_show keeps it on the host (root home, the newest 500, a month) and asks the agent for `::conduit-board{id="cb-…"}` on a line of its own, only while the half has said it's loaded in the last two hours; otherwise Desktop gets the Markdown as before. The half draws the native kinds (stats, charts, comparisons, steps, status, tables, timelines, checklists with the chat's ticks, lists, progress, callouts) and each other card's own Markdown, with tabs and follow-ups. Conduit draws the same board from the tool row, so it hides the line on every surface (Eric, 2026-11-04, chose to build the half after the probe, notifier #539 with #1751).
- A Conduit without "board-cards" gets at most four cards, no layout and no follow-ups (2026-11-03, notifier #528). Only the Conduits used in the last three days count, for board-cards, room-boards and the other card features, and the drawing rule names the weather and how to reach conduit_show behind Tool Search: on .52 four installs last used days before kept the rule off and trimmed the phone's boards (Eric, 2026-11-04, notifier #539).
- Real data only: models are told to fill tables, stats and charts from tools, sites or the user's files, with their source (2026-11-03, notifier #528).
- A turn whose message Conduit reported as typed keeps nothing for a call's screen: its chat is open, not a call. Its cards are drawn in the chat from the answer, and Markdown alone is refused (`typed_chat`) so Hermes writes it in its reply, never saying it's on a screen. A message typed during a call goes the same way: the user is typing in the chat, so that's where it shows. Spoken and unreported turns (calls, a call's jobs) reach the call screen as before. A group room has no call screen either, so Markdown alone there is refused too (`group_room`) (2026-11-05, issue 1808, notifier #556 with #1815).
- Diffs: Hermes hands over a patch it already has (`patch`), a patch file's path on the host for anything past a few dozen lines (`patch_file`, so a long review costs a path, not the diff in output tokens), or `before` and `after`; the plugin never runs Git, and nothing is GitHub-specific (the PR or commit link is the card's `source`) (Eric, 2026-11-05, issue 1818, notifier #566).
- A `patch_file` that isn't a unified diff is refused with none of its content in the answer, so the tool can't put an arbitrary host file on screen; up to 2 MB, 300 files and 20,000 lines, tabs as four spaces, a line past 1,000 characters cut (notifier #566).
- A diff of up to 150 lines over up to 20 files travels whole in the answer (drawn offline, in the saved copy and by Desktop); a longer one keeps only its file list and totals in the answer, and the whole diff on the host (root home, its conduit-diffs folder, the newest 200, a month) under a `cd-` id read from `/boards/diffs` when the user opens it, so a big diff never reaches the chat's history or the model's context (notifier #566).
- The chat's card draws only from what the answer carries (bounded height, stable from the first frame): totals, a five-block bar, up to six file rows or a single file's first 20 lines. The sheet folds deleted, binary and files past 400 lines; lines wrap or scroll (remembered); a file's patch and a line can be copied.
- Card text is untrusted host text: control characters become spaces, and the invisible characters that can make text read differently from what it holds (bidi embeddings, overrides and isolates U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069, ZWSP, word joiner, BOM) are dropped from text and shown as U+FFFD in a line (a diff's or code's), so the review and Copy Changes show one was there; a board's Markdown fallback shows them as U+FFFD too, keeping its lines and tabs, in what it draws and copies (2026-11-06, issue 1867, #1872). ZWJ, ZWNJ, LRM, RLM and ALM stay (emoji and scripts need them). The plugin and Conduit clean it the same way, with a shared vector (2026-11-06, issue 1852, #1854 with notifier #576).
- A Conduit without "diff-cards" gets no diff card and Hermes is told to give what it held in its reply, a group room's board too when its Conduits draw rooms' boards but not diffs; the Markdown fallback is the file list then the first 40 lines in a ```diff block. Live models aren't offered diffs; a diff Hermes shows during a call still reaches the call screen.

**Open gaps**
- Diffs: no side-by-side view, and the unchanged lines between hunks can't be expanded (only the patch is known); a kept diff can't be opened offline, nor once the host has pruned it.
- A room's checklists can't be ticked, and a board in a room another host runs (Linked Rooms) goes as text.
- Desktop's half draws maps, places, weather, media and contacts as their Markdown, not natively.
- The call screen draws a board stacked, with no tabs and no follow-ups (the user speaks the next question).
- The Watch and CarPlay show no cards.
- Checklist ticks on the call screen don't reach the chat or Hermes.
- A checklist in the saved copy, a chat on its way or a saved call's transcript can't be ticked and shows no ticks (a chat's are on the host; a call's stay with its live screen).
- A checklist that stays on screen reads other devices' ticks only when it's drawn again or ticked here.
- A typed message on a Hermes where Conduit's report doesn't reach the turn (plugin isolation, a compute host) is unknown, so Markdown alone there still waits for a call screen that may not be open.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1872 (a board's Markdown fallback cleaned, issue 1867; Rulings); 2026-11-06, #1854 with notifier #576 (hidden bidi and zero-width characters cleaned from card text, issue 1852; Rulings); 2026-11-06, #1853 (a finished row's board read once, issue 1851; Code, gaps); 2026-11-05, #1833 with notifier #566 (diff cards, issue 1818; intro, Siblings, Code, Rulings, gaps); 2026-11-05, #1815 with notifier #556 (a typed chat's conduit_show keeps nothing for a call screen, issue 1808; Code, Rulings, gaps); 2026-11-04, #1751 with notifier #539 (boards drawn in Hermes Desktop by the plugin's Desktop half; Conduit hides its line; Siblings, Code, Rulings, gaps); 2026-11-04, #1748 (ticks fenced to their own dashboard; unsent ticks follow the chat's ids); 2026-11-04, #1736 with notifier #536 (boards drawn in group rooms); 2026-11-03, #1713 with notifier #528.

## Cards drawn in web pages

How an HTML preview (`::preview{file=…}`), a Mermaid diagram or a LaTeX
formula draws in a message, and the room its row takes before its page
reports its height.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats and Bot Chat (the transcript's rows) · the
saved-chat copy · call job result sheets · group rooms · the full-screen
sheets (the same page, interactive) · pictures in messages (the same memo
and the same rule, see Pictures in messages) · the same page opened from
Artifacts and the Folder · text that describes it (README.md's Chat list: the
900-point cap and its fade, and `window.hermes.send` answering `undelivered`,
since Conduit sends no prompt from a page; the stand-in `window.hermes` only
keeps a Desktop widget's buttons from throwing)

**Code**
- HTML previews: `Conduit/Views/Components/HTMLPreviewBlock.swift` (HTMLPreviewBlock, heightKey, sheetPage, HTMLPreviewPage.placeholderHeight, SheetPage, clampedInlineHeight, maximumInlineHeight: the 900 pt a preview draws to in a message, full screen showing the rest, since previews shipped; isCutInline, CutFootFade, bridgeScript); full screen from Artifacts and the Folder: `Conduit/Views/V2/V2ArtifactsViews.swift`, `Conduit/Views/V2/V2WorkspaceViews.swift` (OpenPage); the `::preview` grammar, shared with Desktop cards: `Conduit/Views/Components/TranscriptDirectives.swift` (segments, isHTML)
- Diagrams and formulas: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkupBlock.swift` (MarkupBlock, heightKey(for:), placeholderHeight(for:))
- The room a card holds, and its height taken: `Conduit/Views/Components/ChatCardHeight.swift` (frameHeight, pageMeasured, pageReplaced), the row's new height reaching `Conduit/Views/TranscriptLayout.swift` (rowResized) from `Conduit/Views/TranscriptView.swift` (TranscriptCellRoot, and TranscriptViewController's rowResized, which asks at once for the pass that lands it)
- The reader's row kept: `Conduit/Services/TranscriptScroller.swift` (keepAnchor: a row growing above a browsing reader moves the offset by as much in the pass that lays it out, under a finger and through a fling too; see Following the latest message)
- Heights kept across launches: `Conduit/Services/TranscriptPictureMemory.swift` (height, rememberHeight, with the picture sizes), forgotten in `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (wipeOfflineChatCache, deleteSavedChats)
- Built from Markdown: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (htmlPreview, math and mermaid blocks)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/TranscriptScrollerTests.swift` (Rows changing height), `ConduitTests/TranscriptLayoutTests.swift` (testARowChangingHeightMovesTheRowsUnderItInTheSamePass), `ConduitTests/TranscriptInlineImageTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/MarkupBlockTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/MarkdownLargeDocumentTests+HTMLPreview.swift`

**Rulings**
- A card holds one height from its first frame until its page has measured itself: the height it measured on this phone before (kept with the picture sizes; a preview by its file on the connected Hermes, a diagram or formula by kind, text size and source), else a placeholder (280 pt for a preview, 180 for a diagram, 56 for a formula). Loading the file, the page drawing and a redraw (theme, text size, Try again) all happen inside that room (2026-10-25, #1270, #1238).
- A card takes the height its page measured as soon as it reports, scrolling or not. In a chat the reader's row (the first starting on screen) stays put in the layout pass that lands it, a finger keeping its drag and a fling its momentum: a card above it grows up out of view, one on screen grows down. In the background, where the scroller leaves the offset alone, what grows meanwhile moves under the reader, and their row is put back where it was when the app is back (2026-10-25, #1270, #1238, under which a card waited for the reader's scrolling to rest; taken at once since the transcript rewrite gave every row a frame of its own, 2026-10-31, #1577; Eric delegated the chat scroll's design to Claude, 2026-09-28, and approved the transcript rewrite's design, 2026-10-30).
- Outside a transcript (job sheets) a card takes its height as soon as its page reports too, and so does a picture (see Pictures in messages), but nothing there keeps the reader's row. The saved copy's rows are the chat's own, drawn by its transcript, so their cards take their heights as a chat's do (2026-10-30, #1550), and so are a group room's (2026-10-31, #1590).
- A row's height is its own cell's measurement, so a growth is the row's own change: a reply streaming in below the reader never passes for a card above them. The rows above the reader's row that change height in a pass move the offset by exactly their change, in that pass. When rows below the reader shrink or go so far that the end is above where their row would put them, they're back at the latest message, following it, since nothing under them is left to stay on (a bar shrinking under them leaves them browsing at the new end instead; see Following the latest message). No growth waits, so a drag or a jump has none to drop (2026-10-31, #1577, replacing #1270's owed shifts, which the stack's separate content-size and frame reports needed; Eric delegated the chat scroll's design to Claude, 2026-09-28, and approved the transcript rewrite's design, 2026-10-30).
- A full-screen sheet whose page is held in an optional (one set by the tap) is presented by that page (`.sheet(item:)`), never by a flag beside it: the flag let the sheet build before it saw the page and open blank, as What's New did (#1227). A message's preview, Artifacts and the Folder present `HTMLPreviewSheet` so; a diagram's sheet takes its own document, never optional, so its flag can't race (a fix bringing the preview in line with #1227, 2026-11-01, #1610, from a user's report).
- A page taller than a message draws (`maximumInlineHeight`) fades at its foot, so a widget with its result at the bottom reads as continuing rather than cut off (Eric chose the fade, 2026-11-01, #1610, from a user's report).
- A page that fails gives its place the same way, at once: the file card (a preview whose file can't be read or drawn) or "Couldn't draw" (a diagram or formula), the reader's row kept by what its layout took. A preview showing its file card keeps it while the file is read again, and the card comes back the same way once it reads; a surface with no way to read the file shows the file card from the first frame (2026-10-26, #1270; at once since 2026-10-31, #1577, under the transcript rewrite's design, which Eric approved 2026-10-30).

**Open gaps**
- A card never measured on this phone still grows once, as its page reports; the first scroll up through a chat from another device grows its cards one by one as they draw, the reader's row kept.
- On a cold launch, a card laid out before the kept heights have loaded (read off the main thread as the app opens) holds its placeholder and grows once, like one never measured. Taking the kept height later would still be a growth, so only a read on the main thread before the first frame would save it.
- A kept height is for the width and text size it was measured at: an iPad whose chat column changed width, or a formula after a text size change, takes the kept height and then its new one, like any growth.
- Past 2,000 remembered heights the memo starts again (no LRU), so cards grow once more until each is measured again; the picture sizes have the same limit at 4,000 (see Pictures in messages).
- Job sheets aren't on a transcript, so their cards grow where they are, and above a reader scrolled back move what they read.
- The page a tap opens is tested (`SheetPage`), but not the sheet presenting it, nor the fade: there is no hosted tap test for the block yet.

**Checked:** 2026-11-07, #1914 (a group room's bot messages draw their `::preview` pages, read from the bot's own profile, closing the gap #1524 left; another gateway's bot, Desktop's read-only groups and the user's own room messages keep the directive as text, see Pictures in messages); 2026-11-02, #1643 (a row growing in a reply moves the cells under it in that pass, not only the layout's frames: the context names every row under it); 2026-11-01, #1622 (the pass that lands a row's new height is asked for at once, so a card or its fallback taking its height in an idle chat or room lands without waiting for the next thing to wake the app, as "at once" says; Code); 2026-11-01, #1610 (a message's preview opens full screen by its page, not a flag, so it no longer opens blank; the sheet hangs on the block so a fallback leaves it open; a page cut at 900 pt fades at its foot, Eric's choice; the cap and `window.hermes.send` in README.md; Siblings, Code, Rulings, gaps); 2026-10-31, #1590 (group rooms draw on the transcript, so their diagrams and formulas take their heights with the reader's row kept; Rulings, gaps); 2026-10-31, #1577 (chats draw on the transcript's collection view: a card or picture takes its height at once, scrolling or not, and TranscriptScroller keeps the reader's row; the wait for a rest, the owed shifts and the closing chat's waiting cards give way to that one rule, under the chat scroll's design being Claude's; the rulings #1566 departed from rewritten, and its Open gaps line gone; Code, Rulings, Tests, gaps); 2026-10-31, #1566 (TranscriptScroller's one rule for rows growing above the reader, not called yet; cards take their heights as before; Code, and the rulings it departs from in Open gaps); 2026-10-30, #1550 (the saved copy is drawn by the chat's engine, so its cards take their heights as a chat's); 2026-10-30, #1524 (the `::preview` grammar moved to TranscriptDirectives.swift, shared with Desktop cards; group rooms still show no previews); 2026-10-26, #1281 (wipeOfflineChatCache also forgets Predictive's state); at #1270.

## Cards made for Hermes Desktop

A Hermes Desktop plugin with a client half has the agent write a directive
only Desktop draws, such as hermes-rich-ui's `::richui{id="…"}` from its
`rich_present` tool. Conduit doesn't rebuild those renderers: it shows a card
in the directive's place that says what was there and where it opens, and
nothing that reads a reply says the directive out.

**Siblings:** chats, project chats, Bot Chat, group rooms, the saved-chat
copy and call job sheets (every Markdown surface, with or without the
connected Hermes) · Read Aloud, Classic voice's spoken reply and Local Live's
split · live read-backs and a Hermes call's result · what live models are
handed, on the phone and the Watch · chat list and bot list previews and
quote chips · the
notifier's push text and the README line that describes it · `::preview`
(the same grammar, see Cards drawn in web pages) · the plugin's own
`::conduit-board` (see Cards Hermes shows)

**Code**
- The grammar: `Conduit/Views/Components/TranscriptDirectives.swift` (segments, rewriting, naming, DesktopCardDirective; also built into the Watch app, `project.yml`)
- The card, its details sheet and the read of hermes-rich-ui's card: `Conduit/Views/Components/DesktopCardBlock.swift` (DesktopCardBlock, DesktopCardSheet, DesktopCardContents, DesktopCardContent, PluginRead, TranscriptDirectives.readable), through `Conduit/Views/Components/GatewayMediaDataURLResolver.swift` (connectedDashboardBridge, pluginRead)
- Built from Markdown: `Conduit/Views/Components/MarkdownText.swift` (desktopCard block, directiveSegments, holdsDirective), in group rooms with the connected Hermes' resolver, `Conduit/Views/GroupChatView.swift`
- Spoken: `Conduit/Voice/MessageReadAloudController.swift` (toggle), `Conduit/Voice/VoiceReadBack.swift` (plainSpeech), `Conduit/Voice/SpokenMediaTagFilter.swift` (Classic, Read Aloud's Now Playing, Local Live)
- Live models: `Conduit/Views/Components/GatewayMediaTags.swift` (namingFiles)
- Previews and quote chips: `Conduit/Services/PreviewText.swift` (strip), `Conduit/Views/Components/ChatQuote.swift` (excerpt)
- Push text: `notifier/events.py` (media_free, _desktop_free), described in `notifier/README.md` (what notifications show)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/MarkdownLargeDocumentTests+DesktopCard.swift` (the grammar, the read cache with its clock and fetch passed in), `ConduitTests/GeminiLiveVoiceTests.swift` (testSpokenMediaTagFilterGivesTheSameSpeechHoweverTheReplyIsSplit), `notifier/tests/test_events.py` (test_no_push_shows_a_desktop_directive)

**Rulings**
- A card's line, and a preview's where previews draw, leaves a list (the list carries on after it), and a list or heading marker before it on its line goes with the directive; a directive in a table cell is table text, as a preview's is. A directive still being written while the reply streams shows as text until its closing brace, as a preview does.
- Never hidden without a trace: every directive Conduit can't draw becomes a visible card naming its plugin, and a tap shows the directive as written. Maintainer's ruling (2026-10-30, #1522). The one exception is the plugin's own `::conduit-board{…}`: Conduit already draws that board from conduit_show's tool row, so the line is hidden everywhere (no card, nothing said, previewed or handed to live models), the text around it kept; like a card's, it holds only attributes, so `::conduit-board{}` or CSS stays text; one in a code span, fence, quote or table cell stays as written, and is read as written (a table's rows are table text, as its header is); a pinned reply that is only the line keeps it as the pin's excerpt, which is how the pin finds its reply again; and a push reads "🗂 Board" (Eric, 2026-11-04, building the Desktop half, #1751 with notifier #539).
- Conduit doesn't draw a plugin's components (Table, Chart, Metric…) as its own cards: that would be the plugin's Desktop half rebuilt, kept in step with a plugin we don't control. Agents that want cards in both apps use `conduit_show` (2026-10-30, issue #1522).
- hermes-rich-ui's card shows its own plain-text fallback, `meta.title` and `meta.summary`, from `GET /api/plugins/hermes-rich-ui/cards/<id>` on the connected Hermes, only for a well-formed id (`ru-` and 12 hex). Without it (plugin not installed, card gone, no network, no connected Hermes as in the saved copy) the card says "Card for Hermes Desktop" and to open the chat there. A read is kept for the launch; a failed one is tried again after five minutes, by a card on screen too, waiting only for what's left of them, and one shown before Hermes connected or while its page loads asks again within seconds (nothing is kept for it).
- The card holds one title line and two summary lines from its first frame, so it never changes height as its text arrives; the whole summary is in the details sheet. VoiceOver hears that a tap shows the full summary and the line Hermes wrote.
- A directive is one at a word's start, `::name{…}` holding only `key="value"` attributes, at least one: prose, code spans and CSS (`::selection{color:red}`) stay text. A quoted directive is an example and a table cell (header or row) is table text, read as written as it's drawn, as for previews (#1751). Desktop cards show on every Markdown surface; previews still need the connected Hermes.
- Read Aloud and voices say "(There's a card here for Hermes Desktop.)" and leave a preview out, as Read Aloud already did; live models are told "(a card in the chat made for Hermes Desktop, from <plugin>)" and a preview as its file; previews and quote chips read "Card for Hermes Desktop" and a preview as its file; a push reads "🗂 <plugin> card" and a preview as its file, named as a MEDIA tag's (notifier 0.120.4). Lines in a fenced code block and directives in a code span stay as written everywhere.

**Open gaps**
- The on-screen retry loop has no unit test: it lives in the view's task (the read cache and the wait it sleeps for are tested).
- Two rows showing the same card while it is first read each ask for it.

**Checked:** 2026-11-07, #1914 (a group room's bot message supplies its own profile's file reader, falling back to the room's; the Desktop card's read is unchanged); 2026-11-04, #1751 with notifier #539 (the plugin's `::conduit-board` line is hidden, not a card; Siblings, Rulings); 2026-10-30, #1524.

## Self-improvement updates

The "💾 Self-improvement review" rows Hermes adds to a chat after it saves a
memory or a skill, and the Chat setting that shows or hides them
(`display.memory_notifications`: Use Hermes default, Always show, Never show).

**Siblings:** the Chat settings row and its caption · the review row in the
chat, live and in the offline copy · chats, project chats, Bot Chat and group
rooms (all the dashboard's chats) · Hermes' messaging platforms · the
notifier's live read of the setting for chats already open

**Code**
- Setting: `Conduit/Views/AuxiliaryViews.swift` (ChatSettingsDetail fields, `display.memory_notifications`), `Conduit/Models/Models.swift` (ProfileDisplayPreferences.showReviews), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (loadProfileDisplayPreferences, setProfileSetting)
- Row: `Conduit/Services/StreamEventParser.swift` (`review.summary`), `Conduit/Services/HermesClient.swift` (reviewActivity), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (the review cache, mergeCachedReviews, placingReviews, replacingSavedReviews after Load earlier), `Conduit/Views/ChatView.swift` (SELF-IMPROVEMENT REVIEW, ReviewSummaryCard, ReviewRunCard, and ModelChangeSummaryCard and CardHeaderCaption, which share its layout), `Conduit/Views/TranscriptModel.swift` (rows, which leaves out a review that draws nothing), `Conduit/Views/ChatActivityRows.swift` (ChatMessageScrollTarget.drawsRow, drawsReviewCard, ChatReviewRun, ChatReviewPlacement), `Conduit/Services/ChatScrollState.swift` (placeReviews, restorationAnchorID), `Conduit/Services/TranscriptScroller.swift` (a saved place on a folded review restores to its run, through restorationAnchorID), `Conduit/Views/ChatRowDisclosure.swift` (a run's open choice); the offline copy's reviews are the chat's own rows while they stand in
- Tests: `ConduitTests/AppStateChatResumeTests.swift` (testReviewRowsFollowTheSelfImprovementSetting, testConsecutiveReviewsFoldIntoOneRun, testSavedReviewsGoAmongHermesRowsByTime)
- Notifier: `notifier/review_notices.py`, `notifier/tests/test_review_notices.py`

**Rulings**
- A changed setting reaches chats already open at their next review, with no restart: the dashboard reads it only when it builds a chat's agent, so the plugin reads it again from the chat's profile before each review. Hermes' messaging platforms need nothing, its gateway reads it every turn (2026-10-25, notifier #373, #1260).
- Never show hides the rows a chat already has too, live and in the offline copy (from the setting last read for that profile, kept on the phone, until the dashboard answers; Settings then reads Never show), without deleting them: they come back when the setting does. Anything but "off" (or a YAML false) shows them, as Hermes reads it (2026-10-25, #1260; Eric's rule to close gaps in the same change).
- On the review row, as on the Model updated card beside it, the card's caption and its time share the top row, the time on the right on one line (a long caption wraps beside it), and the summary runs the card's full width below, never in a column beside the time; at the accessibility text sizes the time goes under the caption (2026-10-29, #1507, issue #1440).
- A review the phone saved goes back among Hermes' rows by its time when the chat loads, before the first row timed after it, and never moves Hermes' own rows; a row with no time doesn't decide its place. Load earlier places them again among the older rows it adds (2026-10-30, #1551, issue #1549).
- Two or more reviews in a row fold into one line, "N self-improvement reviews" with the last one's time, closed every time the chat opens; a tap opens it to every card as before, and the choice lasts while the chat stays open, like a run of steps. Any other row ends the run, so an approval, a question or an error is never folded into it; a lone review keeps its own card. Live and in the offline copy, every chat kind. No setting of its own: Never show still hides them all (2026-10-30, #1519, issue #1518).

**Open gaps**
- A saved review's place uses the phone's clock and Hermes' rows the host's (Hermes' review event carries no time), so a host clock that is off by more than the time between a review and the next row puts the review on the wrong side of that row when the chat reloads. Reviews are stamped to the millisecond, so a row from the same second doesn't (#1551).
- An open run of reviews keeps its choice by its first review, so loading older history that holds reviews right above it closes it again; runs of steps do the same.

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1663 (the display settings' first read goes out with the ticket; a setting saved since voids it, see A connection's first reads); 2026-10-31, #1577 (a saved place on a folded review restores through TranscriptScroller; Code); 2026-10-31, #1565 (which reviews draw is decided in TranscriptModel; Code); 2026-10-31, #1552 (its settings open on their kept answer; what they save is unchanged); 2026-10-30, #1551 (saved reviews placed by time, not after the newest message, #1549); 2026-10-30, #1550 (the offline copy's reviews are drawn and folded by the chat's own rows); 2026-10-30, #1519 (runs of reviews fold into one line, #1518); 2026-10-29, #1507 (caption and time on the row's top line, summary full width below, #1440); 2026-10-26, #1282 (display settings kept on the phone, so the offline copy follows Never show from launch); 2026-10-25, #1260.

## Profile glow color

the Profiles sheet, else the main color of its photo, else its bot's color in
Hermes, else the gold accent.

**Siblings:** the tab roots and the iPad chat placeholder (the profile in
use) · the open chat (chats, project chats, Bot Chat: the chat's own agent)
and its working line · sheets over the open chat (Model, Context) · group
rooms (the profile in use; each member's name and bubble in its bot's glow
color, see Bot messages in group rooms) · Settings and its pages · the Profiles and All
profiles sheets · the Live Activity's color · Settings captions and
model-facing text (none describe the glow)

**Code**
- Colors: `Conduit/Services/ProfileGlowColors.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState+V2Shell.swift` (profileGlowTint), `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (profileGlowColors, setProfileGlowColor, conversationIdentityProfile), `Conduit/Services/ProfileAppearanceStore.swift` (picks)
- Backdrop: `Conduit/Theme.swift` (ConduitBackdrop), `Conduit/Views/V2/V2TopBar.swift` (V2Backdrop, glowProfile)

- Tests: `ConduitTests/ProfileGlowColorTests.swift`, `ConduitTests/BotModeTests.swift` (conversationIdentityProfile, the bot's glow)

**Rulings**
- A Bot Chat glows in its bot's color: its backdrop, the Model and Context sheets over it, its working line and its Live Activity; the Bots list and every other root keep the profile in use (2026-10-25, Eric's report, #1263).
- Sheets reached from Settings or a page take the glow as an environment value (`settingsGlowTint`), not from AppState, so a sheet built on them needs nothing injected (#638).

**Open gaps**
- The drawer shell (Appearance, V2 off) draws every chat on the gold backdrop, a Bot Chat included, though the Model and Context sheets over it take the chat's glow.
- The chat's other sheets (gateway diagnostics, workspace browser, delegate agents, pinned replies) never took a profile glow and stay gold.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1874 (group room names and bubbles take the glow).
