A deliberate repeat of the same words inside those five minutes after a lost reply is taken as the lost one (the authority answers the first admission's receipt): Conduit's lost-reply check already restores the words only when Hermes didn't take them, so this covers that check being wrong (2026-11-02, #1631). Its receipt's `queued` is its place in line: the authority has no busy policy and runs a send into a running turn as the next turn, so a send (Queue or not) while this socket saw a turn running in that chat (from `message.start` to `message.complete`, which ends every authority turn, a failed one included: it carries the error card and the authority sends no turn-ending `error` event (Hermes run_turn_runner, 2026-11-02, #1631); the snapshots' `running`, a control told no turn runs, and an interrupt Hermes took, at its reply: the interrupted turn still ends with its `message.complete` right after, and a send then starts as soon as it does, so reading it as a turn of its own is right within moments, though the authority's receipt says queued, and never leaves it waiting on an end this socket may not see), reads as held; any other reads as a new turn, a Queue send into a chat this socket saw idle included, since the authority starts it at once (2026-11-02, #1631). A receipt's `execution_generation` names a turn only once it runs (`started`, or a steer handed to the running turn): a queued one has none until its turn claims it, so folding it into the fences never moves them past the running turn (Hermes session_authority._receipt and hermes_state_runtime's claim, 2026-11-02, #1631). Predictions' hidden turn (`display_kind: hidden`) is taken as it is (2026-11-01, #1631, probed on the canary).
- `prompt.btw`, `prompt.background`, `subagent.steer`, `subagent.interrupt`, `session.context_breakdown` and `process.stop` take the dashboard's shape on the authority too, and so do `subagent.list`, `subagent.tail`, `command.dispatch` (a skill or plugin slash command) the Model sheet's `model.options` (`explicit_only` and the chat's `session_id`) and the automatic title's `llm.oneshot` (`session_id`, `task`, `instructions`, `input`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`; the authority lends it the chat's model as the dashboard does): their params are within the authority's fields and their answers carry the keys Conduit reads (`subagents`; `available` and `text`; the same model payload, built by the same inventory code; `text`), checked against the canary's session_ancillary, session_commands, session_config and session_llm_oneshot (2026-11-02, #1631); the title read is `session.info`, whose answer names the stored `title` (`profile` dropped for the chat's own profile, 2026-11-02, #1631), and side agents' `btw.complete` and `background.complete` come back (2026-11-01, #1631, probed on the canary). Steer, redirect and interrupt name the running turn's `execution_generation`; a stale one reads the session again, takes its generation as Hermes gives it (even a lower one; other snapshots and events only raise it, and a stale refusal corrects one that is too high), and goes once more only if a turn still runs (2026-11-01, #1618). An interrupt reports the turn it stopped (the generation its request named, the retry's included, or none when nothing ran), and a turn that started while it was in flight still reads as running (2026-11-03, #1696); a session that says a turn runs but names no generation leaves the refusal standing and the chat reading as running (2026-11-02, #1631).
- Rename, branch, compress, a model pick and Move to project are `session.mutate` on the authority, fenced by the session's revision, and by the turn's generation for all but rename; a `revision_conflict` or `stale_generation` that carries the current fences goes again once with them. A branch keeps rows through the reply's own row id (2026-11-01, #1618).
- An approval or clarify answer whose turn ended (`stale_generation`), or whose chat no longer lists it, reads as no longer active, and one another surface answered first (`already_resolved`) as answered elsewhere ("This approval was answered elsewhere."), never as a refusal or a timeout. The authority names every approval it asks, and AppState matches an id-less card to its waiting request by command before answering (legacyApprovalTarget), so a card still without an id sends nothing there and reads as no longer active, never answering an approval it doesn't show. A clarify answer names the chat's profile, as an approval answer does. The authority asks one question per `clarify.request` for a client like Conduit (Hermes' clarify_batch_turn), so its `resolved` settles that card; an answer with neither a cached prompt nor a chat to read it from sends nothing and reads as no longer active (a voice answer always has its reply's chat, which asked), and one whose chat Hermes no longer has (session not found) expires the card as no longer active, as an approval does, and a voice job's question the same way (answerJobQuestion). An approval or clarify card names its prompt and the turn that asked from the socket's event; one this socket never saw asked (shown before a reconnect or relaunch, a voice job's or Local Live reply's included, which pass their chat) reads both from the chat's resume, which lists the prompts Hermes still waits on, and one it no longer lists reads as answered or ended; a resume also drops the cached prompts it no longer lists, so their answers aren't sent. When that read fails for any other reason (a timeout, a dropped socket), nothing was sent: the card stays answerable and says why Hermes couldn't be reached, never "did not accept". A snapshot older than a turn this socket already saw start says nothing about whether that turn runs, so a send during it still reads as held. A guarded model pick answers `confirmation_required` with a token and its `target_model`; the confirmed pick sends that token back (2026-11-01, #1618, both tried on the canary and in the notifier's upstream leg).
- A redirect on the authority answers `redirected`, `queued` or `rejected` (with `delivered: false` when no agent could take it, the contract's "queue it as the next prompt"), the words SessionRedirectOutcome already reads (probed, notifier #504's listener leg) (2026-11-01, #1631).
- On the authority a chat's runtime id and stored key are the same (`local-…`, the create's `session_id` and `stored_session_id`), so Move to project and the other mutations that name a chat by its stored key find the fences its events and snapshots keyed (2026-11-01, #1631).
- A card's id is the payload's `prompt_id` when it has one, before `request_id`: the authority's answers and the cached prompt name `prompt_id`, and the dashboard's payloads carry only `request_id` (2026-11-02, #1631).
- Predictions on the listener answer only while the gateway holds the chat's agent (up to its cache's hour after the last reply); a chat opened after a gateway restart, or idle past that hour, answers 404 with its own reason ("That chat's agent isn't loaded on the host"), and a failed lookup 502. Kept as the limit: building the fork from the authority's stored history would mean a full agent start per chip ask (Eric, 2026-11-02, #1631, notifier #504).
- An approval or clarify answer sent in the dashboard's shape before the ready was read, and refused once the socket proved to be the authority's, goes again in the authority's shape, as other early requests do (an approval card still without an id sends nothing there, as above: AppState matches an id-less card to its request by command first); only a shape refusal (`invalid_params`, an unknown verb) sends a request again, and a model `config.set` the authority refuses by name (`use_session_mutation_model`) goes as its model mutation; any other refusal stands (2026-11-02, #1631).
- An answer to a prompt the authority asked goes to `clarify.respond` even if a resume also listed its id among `open_requests` (2026-11-02, #1631).
- A question another surface answered first reads "This question was answered elsewhere." (or the batch form), as an approval does (2026-11-01, #1631).
- An approval or clarify answer that went out and got no word back (a dropped socket, a timeout, a cancel; not one refused as not connected or one the socket refused to send, which were never written) may have been taken, or settled by a timeout (an approval that timed out is denied and the turn goes on), so a retry that hears `already_resolved` reads as no longer active, neither accepted nor answered elsewhere; if the chat's resume no longer lists the prompt, the retry reads as no longer active whether or not its turn still runs, since nothing says whose answer settled it (an approval that timed out is denied and the turn goes on). A refusal or a status clears the record, which keeps the newest 256 and drops the oldest first, and every client shares it, since a reconnect builds a new client and a drop is the usual reason to retry (2026-11-02, #1631).
- Verbs that aren't a chat's reach Hermes' own handlers on the listener too: the authority answers its own and hands the rest to the dashboard's handlers when the socket holds the full interactive grant, as Conduit's does. Projects (`projects.tree`, `projects.project_sessions`, `projects.create`, `projects.update`, `projects.delete`), the Bot profiles card (`profiles.*`), its MCP editing (`mcp.catalog`, `mcp.servers.list`, `mcp.servers.add`, `mcp.servers.set_api_key`, `mcp.servers.test`), the agents' pause state and its toggle (`delegation.status`, `delegation.pause`) and `client.capabilities` answer in Conduit's shapes (checked on a real listener, notifier upstream test_conduits_host_verbs_answer_on_the_listener). `cron.list` doesn't, and isn't needed: scheduled jobs read REST first. `image.detach` isn't needed: nothing on the listener holds a staged picture (2026-11-02, #1631).
- Reactions (`message.react`), slash commands (`slash.exec`, `commands.catalog`), staging a file or picture and the list verbs keep the dashboard's shapes on the authority, which takes them unchanged (probed on the 2026-11-01 canary); a staged picture rides in its message's `attachments`, since the authority holds none for the next message (Attaching files, 2026-11-02, #1631). The authority's resume names waiting prompts under `prompts`, never `open_requests`, so an answer to one always takes the authority's `approval.respond` or `clarify.respond` (2026-11-01, #1631).
- A folder chat's create sends `cwd` on both servers: the authority's create takes it (`CREATE_FIELDS` in Hermes' gateway/session_policy.py, listed by `runtime.describe`) (2026-11-01, #1631).
- `approval.respond` and `clarify.respond` answer only `resolved` or `already_resolved` on the authority (their result contract is closed to those two), so any other answer can only come from a Hermes that broke it and reads as no longer active (2026-11-01, #1631).
- A branch on the authority names its reply by Hermes' row id; a reply whose id never arrived (its completion missed in the background) asks the user to open the chat again, which reads the ids, rather than branching by copied text as the dashboard does (2026-11-01, #1631).
- A branch on the authority takes no folder: Hermes' branch copies the parent's saved policy, its working folder included, so it opens where the parent works; the dashboard's `cwd` is the same folder, read from the parent (2026-11-01, #1631).
- The authority answers its refusals with code 4001 and a `data.reason`; only `not_found` (or no reason, the dashboard's "session not found") reads as a gone session, so an `invalid_params` or `permission_denied` on an answer or a resume shows as the refusal it is; an `invalid_params` naming an optional prompt key in `data.fields` takes the same drop-and-resend fallback as the dashboard's 4000 (2026-11-01, #1631).
- Rewind already speaks `session.mutate` with the resume's fences on both servers; its result's fences are kept for the next request. A conflict on it is shown, not resent with the new fences: it is the user's edit of a chat that moved meanwhile, and they choose again. The session's reasoning, Fast and YOLO switches stay `config.set` with the session id, which the authority takes (scope `session`); only `model` moved to a mutation (2026-11-01, #1618, probed on the canary).
- The listener serves its own profile's chats; another profile's (a Bot Chat's) answers `profile_mismatch` unless the gateway serves several profiles (`multiplex_profiles`). That is Hermes' setup, not Conduit's: Conduit names the chat's profile wherever it reads a chat again (a stale steer, redirect or interrupt, an unseen approval or question), as on the dashboard (2026-11-01, #1631, probed on the canary; multiplexed profiles not tried).
- Busy mode stays on the phone on the authority, which has no profile-wide busy setting: Conduit already sends steer, interrupt or Queue itself (2026-11-01, #1618).
- A bare refusal token from Hermes ("invalid_params") is shown with the request and the keys Hermes named; Hermes' own sentences are shown as they are (2026-11-01, #1618).
- Setup docs keep recommending `hermes dashboard`; the Webapp's address is mentioned as also working (2026-11-01, #1618).
- The plugin's chat features run on the listener too (Eric, 2026-11-01: port them now, merged together). A process whose gateway API is up (`gateway.run_api._ACTIVE_RUNNER`) reads chats from its session authority and never from the TUI gateway, which a gateway process may load but whose chats no client sees. The plugin's own chats (Watch jobs, a Watch call's Local Live chat, Pulse's turns) keep their code: `gateway_chats.session_api()` takes the TUI gateway's requests and answers in its shapes, on a connection of their own that acts for the host's owner as Conduit's Webapp sign-in does, so the phone opens those chats. It adds a `submission_id` per call, names the turn's generation, answers an approval by its prompt id (a requestless one is the oldest waiting, as the TUI gateway takes it), reads `approval.settled` as `approval.cancelled`, and a stale control as nothing running; closing a chat detaches its view (2026-11-01, #1631, notifier #504, checked on the canary).
- Turn surface on the listener: there is no Hermes record to keep Conduit's report on, and a turn runs from its admitted message, not on the socket that sent it, so it can't tell Conduit's turn from another client's. The report is kept by session id instead, and the turn whose session and text match it takes it: only Conduit reports, for the exact text it is about to send in that chat. The plugin's Watch transports report their own turns the same way (2026-11-01, #1631, notifier #504). A send that failed (refused, or never sent) has Conduit drop its report on either server (`POST /turn-surface/discard`, capability `turn-surface-discard`), so the same words sent from another client in that chat don't take its line; a send whose reply was only lost keeps it, since its turn may have started (2026-11-02, #1631, notifier #504). The discard isn't ordered after a report still on its way: a report slower than the send's short wait is cancelled, and one that lands after its send failed lapses with the listener's 15 minutes. Accepted as the window, since holding the discard for an upload Conduit already gave up on would hold nothing back reliably either (2026-11-02, #1631).
- Predictions on the listener fork the chat's agent from the gateway's cache (running or idle since its last turn), under the authority's profile (2026-11-01, #1631, notifier #504).
- Pulse on the listener sends its hidden turn to the authority, which queues it behind a running turn (no busy refusal, no takeover), and puts the chat on Pulse's model with a fenced `session.mutate`, confirming a guarded switch with its token (the user picked the model in Settings > Pulse) (2026-11-01, #1631, notifier #504).
- Desktop views say not observing on the listener (reason `gateway-authority`): the authority knows which clients view a chat but not which one Desktop has selected, so Conduit keeps its own read tracking and a reply-ready push still goes (2026-11-01, #1631, notifier #504).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-03, #1696 (an interrupt names the turn it stopped, for Voice's cancelled-turn note; a turn that starts during it keeps running); 2026-11-02, #1631 with notifier #504 (pictures ride in the message's attachments; host verbs checked on a real listener; Predictions' limit ruled); 2026-11-01, #1631 with notifier #504 (the plugin's chat features ported to the authority: turn surface, Predictions, Watch jobs, a Watch call's Local Live chat, Pulse's turns; Desktop views ruled; each checked on the canary); 2026-11-01, #1631 (seeded; issue #1618; probed against the 2026-11-01 canary; unseen prompts and the model confirm closed; the other socket verbs, the hidden turn, sends into a running turn and other profiles probed).

## Where a message was sent (turn surface)

Just before a send, Conduit tells the notifier plugin where in Conduit the
message came from (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Vision Pro, CarPlay, a Shortcut) and
whether it was typed or spoken, with the hash of the exact text; that turn
gets one line of context saying so (#888). A send that failed drops its
report.

**Siblings:** the composer's sends (typed, dictated, a caller's surface such
as a live call's request) · a live voice call's turn into the open chat ·
a call's request into an existing chat · a Shortcut's send · the plugin's
own Watch jobs and call chats (they name the Watch themselves) · the line
and its hints the model reads (`notifier/turn_surface.py`: FORM_HINT,
SPOKEN_HINT) · the gateway's own listener (Two Hermes servers) · conduit_show,
which keeps no call-screen card for a typed turn (Cards Hermes shows) · the
notifier README's "Where in Conduit a message was sent"

**Code**
- The report and discard: `Conduit/Services/TurnSurface.swift`, `Conduit/Services/AppState+TurnSurface.swift` (reportTurnSurface, discardTurnSurface)
- Send sites: `Conduit/Services/AppState.swift` (performComposerSubmission's report and its catch, the live call's chat turn, the call request into an existing chat), `Conduit/Services/AppState+ShortcutSend.swift` (the Shortcut's send)
- Plugin: `notifier/turn_surface.py` (record, take, discard, record_for_authority, discard_digest_for_authority, note, start_turn, turn_entry), `notifier/dashboard/api/chats.py` (record_turn_surface, discard_turn_surface)
- Tests: `ConduitTests/AppStateTurnSurfaceTests.swift`, `notifier/tests/test_turn_surface.py`

**Rulings**
- A send waits for the report at most `TurnSurface.wait`, then goes anyway; a report that misses its send is cancelled, so it can't label the next turn (#888).
- Every send site that reports drops its report when the send fails (refused, or never sent: a busy chat, a failed read), so the same words sent from another client in that chat don't take its line; a send whose reply was only lost keeps it, since its turn may have started. A plugin without `turn-surface-discard` keeps the report until it goes stale (2026-11-02, #1631, notifier #504).

**Open gaps**
- None known.

**Checked:** 2026-11-05, #1815 with notifier #556 (the turn's tools read how its message was entered, turn_entry; Siblings, Code); 2026-11-02, #1631 (entry seeded with the discard; notifier #504).

## Back-deployed Foundation API in shipped targets

A comparison of two Dates calls the target's own `<=` and `>=`, never
Foundation's: the 27.2 SDKs back-deploy those two, and Foundation in early
iOS 27.2 betas lacks them, so a build that imported them crashed at launch
there (TestFlight 251, "Error" and "Keeps crashing", 2026-11-05).

**Siblings:** every shipped target compiles `Shared/DateOrder/DateOrder.swift`: the app, the
notification service and location push extensions (through `Shared`), the
widgets, the share extension, the Apple Watch app and its widgets (the folder
itself) · CI's two checks (project.yml's targets on Linux, the smoke build's
binaries on macOS) · not needed: the test bundles and UI test runners (they
don't ship; `@testable import Conduit` resolves to Foundation's)

**Code**
- `Shared/DateOrder/DateOrder.swift` (Date's `<=` and `>=`, internal and `@_disfavoredOverload`)
- `project.yml` (each shipped target's sources)
- `scripts/check-weak-imports.py` (targets: every application and app extension reaches DateOrder.swift, its excludes honored; binaries: no shipped Mach-O weak-imports a BANNED symbol or strongly loads a WEAK_FRAMEWORKS framework, ActivityKit and ImagePlayground, see Live Activity for a running turn), `scripts/tests/test_check_weak_imports.py`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the self-test job's "Every shipped target keeps Date's comparisons", the smoke job's "No back-deployed Date comparisons or strong framework loads in the build"), held by `scripts/tests/test_ci_workflow_contract.py`; `docs/RELEASE_WORKFLOW.md` (the archive's check before upload)

**Rulings**
- A Foundation API the SDK back-deploys to a version whose betas are in testers' hands is declared in each target instead, or not used; a newly back-deployed symbol Conduit calls goes in both DateOrder (or a file beside it) and BANNED. The shadow stays `@_disfavoredOverload`: an internal, `@_spi` or `@usableFromInline` copy is visible to `@testable import Conduit` and makes ConduitTests' comparisons ambiguous (checked with Xcode 27B52, 2026-11-06; Claude's pick after the TestFlight 251 crash Eric asked to be fixed, #1848).

**Open gaps**
- The binaries check's Date half passes without testing anything while the hosted runner's Xcode predates the 27.2 SDK (its framework half, #1891, runs on any Xcode); the targets check holds until then, and each TestFlight archive is checked on the Mac (`conduit-save-dsyms`, docs/RELEASE_WORKFLOW.md, the "Archive and upload" step of section 3). A failed check there renames the archive to `*.xcarchive.blocked-weak-imports`, so the upload step can't find it whatever the per-build scripts do with the exit code.
- The smoke build has no Watch app, so only the targets check covers the Watch's binaries.

**Checked:** 2026-11-06, #1891 (the binaries check also fails a strong load of ActivityKit or ImagePlayground, issue 1877; DateOrder and BANNED unchanged); 2026-11-06, #1856 (a failed archive check blocks the upload; Open gaps); 2026-11-06, #1848.

## Feature map rules

How a change brings its connected features along, and how this map stays
current with nobody tending it.

**Siblings:** CONTRIBUTING.md (the full rules) · this map's intro · the PR
template · the reviewer prompt · the notifier's CONTRIBUTING.md, PR template
and reviewer prompt · the map check in CI · README.md and docs/CI.md, which
point at the map and its check

**Code**
- Rules: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/FEATURE_MAP.md` (the intro and the sibling sets), `.github/pull_request_template.md` (Siblings)
- Reviewers: `.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml` (the Connected features focus area)
- Notifier: `notifier/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `notifier/.github/pull_request_template.md`, `notifier/.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml`
- Map check: `scripts/check-feature-map.py` (paths, entry shape, and on a PR the Checked line of each entry it edits; on a PR into `pulse` or `linked-rooms` that merges main, main's maps where the PR and its base meet main tell which entries came from main), `scripts/tests/test_check_feature_map.py`, run by `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Feature map paths exist; a PR into `pulse` or `linked-rooms` runs that branch's copy, whose trigger lists it), its PR number, base map and main's maps pinned by `scripts/tests/test_ci_workflow_contract.py`
- Pointers: `README.md` (Architecture), `docs/CI.md` (the self-test job under Jobs)

**Rulings**
- A checked-in map, a Siblings section in every PR, and rulings in each entry; a sibling left out without a reason is a major review finding (2026-10-23, #1167, Eric).
- Nobody tends the map separately: the PR that changes a feature updates its entry, adds one for a connected feature that has none, adds a sibling an earlier change missed, and records the maintainer's rulings with the date and the PR (2026-10-24, #1178, Eric).
- CONTRIBUTING.md holds the full rules. The intro, the PR templates and the reviewer prompts each carry the part their reader needs, so a rule change starts in CONTRIBUTING.md and then reaches each copy (2026-10-24, #1178).
- The notifier's reviewers can't read this map, so a notifier PR names its entry, or the hermes-conduit PR that adds or updates it (2026-10-24, #1178).
- An entry a PR adds or edits names that PR on its Checked line, and CI fails one that doesn't; a commit is only for an entry seeded from main. A carry PR names both, like "#1188, carried in #1200". The PR template asks for a Siblings line for every sibling the entry lists, Settings and model-facing text included (2026-10-24, #1209, Eric).
- On a PR into `pulse` or `linked-rooms` that merges main, an entry main changed between where that branch last met main and where the PR meets it, and that matches main's copy there, came in with main and keeps main's Checked line, so bringing main into the branch doesn't name the merge on every entry main changed. A PR into either that doesn't merge main gets no such pass, and neither does an entry main didn't change (2026-10-25, #1248; the first such merge after #1209 failed the check on 48 entries). `linked-rooms` gets the pass as `pulse` does, since Eric asked for the Linked Rooms app side on a branch like `pulse` (2026-10-26, #1287).
- A refactor that changes no behavior and no user-facing or model-facing text (moving code, or changing how state is stored or observed) has no siblings: its PR says "No mapped feature" and adds no new entry, and reviewers don't ask for one. If it moves code an entry's Code lists, it updates those paths and the Checked line (2026-10-25, #1271, Eric; reviewer prompts and notifier copies in #1273 and notifier #377).

**Open gaps**
- A connection nobody has noticed yet isn't caught by any check; it goes in the first time a fix turns it up.
- A notifier PR that moves a file listed here fails the next hermes-conduit PR's map check, not its own.
- A PR that changes a mapped feature's behavior without touching its entry isn't caught by CI; a reviewer flags it (minor). A refactor that changes no behavior is exempt unless it moves a listed path.
- On a merge of main into `pulse` or `linked-rooms`, an entry both sides changed that the merge settles on main's copy keeps main's Checked line, so CI doesn't flag dropping the branch's edit; a reviewer checks that choice. CI only sees content, and that copy is main's word for word.
- If GitHub can't say whether a PR into `pulse` or `linked-rooms` merges main, or can't give main's maps, the step warns and checks without them, so a merge of main fails on the entries it brings in until a re-run.

**Checked:** 2026-11-02, #1642 (docs/CI.md names the self-test job for the map check); #1314.
